In a moment she felt pleasure; in a moment she become excited; in a moment she became conscious and in a moment her mind was filled dejection. In a moment she got up from her bed and roamed about here and there and in a moment she came back to the bed.

## \|\| 16.6-7 \|\|

*bhramantī kṣaṇamudvegādvivasantī kṣaṇaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇameva samudvegādasvāpsītpunareva sā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*puṣpacandanatalpaṃ ca tadbabhūvātikaṇṭakam \|*  
*viṣamāhārakaṃ svādu divyarūpaṃ phalaṃ jalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. In a moment she got up in disgust and walked around and in a moment she removed her clothes and the next moment she came back to the bed. The bed of roses troubled her like a bed of thorns, the divine tasteful water looked to her like poison.

## \|\| 16.8 \|\|

*nilayaśca nirākāraḥ sūkṣmavastraṃ hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*sindūrapatrakaṃ caiva vraṇatulyaṃ ca duḥkhadam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The house looked completely lonely to her. The fine clothes worn by her looked like fire to her, vermilion spot appeared like a boil on her.

## \|\| 16.9-11 \|\|

*kṣaṇaṃ dadarśa tandrāyāṃ suveṣaṃ puruṣaṃ satī \|*  
*sundaraṃ ca yuvānaṃ ca sasmitaṃ rasikeśvaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

*candanokṣitasarvāṃgaṃ ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*āgacchantaṃ mālyavantaṃ paśyantaṃ tanmukhāmbujam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kathayantaṃ ratikathāṃ cumbantamadharaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*śayānaṃ puṣpatalpe ca samāśliṣyantamaṅgakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. In a moment she felt drowsy. In the meantime she caught sight of a beautiful person. He happened to be a beautiful young man who wore a smile on his face and all his limbs were plastered with sandal-paste. He was adorned with ornaments studded with gems. A beautiful necklace adorned his neck. He was looking at Tulasi constantly. Reclining over the flower bed, she listened to the passionate story and was mentally attracted towards Tulasi embracing her.

## \|\| 16.12 \|\|

*punareva tu gacchantamāgacchantaṃ vasantakam \|*  
*kānta kva yāsi prāṇeśa tiṣṭhetyevamuvāca sā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Tulasi looked at him again as if the spring had arrived. In the meantime she while asleep, uttered, “O lord, О master of my life, where are you going? You slay here for some more time.” Then she got up.

## \|\| 16.13 \|\|

*punaḥ svacetanāṃ prāpya vilalāpa punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tapovane sā ca tasthau tatraiva nārada \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О Ncrada, on regaining consciousness she started lamenting again and again. Thus the lady was spending her time in the Tapovana.

## \|\| 16.14 \|\|

*śaṅkhacūḍo mahāyogī jaigīṣavyānmanoramam \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya mantraṃ samprāpya prāpya siddhiṃ tu puṣkare \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. At that point of time Samkhacfida received the pleasant mantra of lord Krishna from a sage named Jaiglsavya Rsi and recited it in the Puskara region. He ultimately met with success.

## \|\| 16.15 \|\|

*paṭhansadā tu kavacaṃ sarvamaṅgalamaṅgalam \|*  
*brahmeśācca varaṃ prāpya yattanmanasi vāñchitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He had recited the name of Krishna who bestows welfare on all and had also received the desired boon from Brahma.

## \|\| 16.16-20 \|\|

*ājñayā brahmaṇaḥ so'pi badarīṃ vai samāyayau \|*  
*āgacchantaṃ śaṅkhacūḍamapaśyattulasī mune \|\| 16 \|\|*

*navayauvanasampannaṃ kāmadevasamaprabham \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śvetacampakavarṇābhaṃ ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*śaratpārvaṇacandrāsyaṃ śaratpaṅkajalocanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mahāratnagaṇāklṛptavimānasthaṃ manoharam \|*  
*ratnakuṇḍalayugmāḍhyagaṇḍasthalavirājitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pārijātaprasūnāḍhyamālyavantaṃ ca susmitam \|*  
*kastūrīkuṅkumayutaṃ sugandhitilakojjvalam \|\| 20 \|\|*

16-20. О sage, at the command of Brahma he went to BadrikasTama and Tulasi found him coming to her. He was quite youthful and as beautiful as the god of love; he had the glory of white campa flowers and was adorned with all the ornaments. The lustre of his face resembled the rays of the full moon during the winter season. His eyes resembled the lotus flower of the winter season, he was mounted on a beautiful plane studded with best of gems. The beautiful young man stood there. Two gems studded Kundalas were decorating his ears and he had a long garland of Parijata flowers around his neck; he wore a smile on his face. His body was plastered with the paste of sandal-wood, saffron and kastiirl.

## \|\| 16.21 \|\|

*sā dṛṣṭvā sannidhāne taṃ mukhamācchādya vāsasā \|*  
*sasmitā taṃ nirīkṣantī sakaṭākṣaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Finding such a youth before her, she covered her face with a piece of cloth and he started looking at her with side glances again and again. She cast her head down with shyness due to her first meeting with him.

## \|\| 16.22-30 \|\|

*babhūva sā namramukhī navasaṅgamalajjitā \|*  
*kāmukī kāmabāṇena pīḍitā pulakānvitā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pibantī tanmukhāmbhojaṃ locanābhyāṃ ca santatam \|*  
*dadarśa śaṅkhacūḍaśca kanyāmekāṃ tapovane \|\| 23 \|\|*

*puṣpacandanatalpasthāṃ vasantīṃ vāsasā vṛtām \|*  
*paśyantīṃ tanmukhaṃ śaśvatsasmitāṃ sumanoharām \|\| 24 \|\|*

*supīnakaṭhinaśroṇīṃ pīnonnatapayodharām \|*  
*muktāpaṃktiprabhājuṣṭadantapaṃktiṃ subibhratīm \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pakvabimbādharoṣṭhīṃ ca sunāsāṃ sundarīṃ varām \|*  
*taptakāñcanavarṇābhāṃ śaraccandrasamaprabhām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*svatejasā parivṛtāṃ sukhadṛśyāṃ manoramām \|*  
*kastūrībindubhiḥ sārddhamadhaścandanabindunā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sindūrabindunā śaśvatsīmantādhaḥsthalojjvalām \|*  
*nimnanābhigabhīrāṃ ca tadadhastrivalīyutām \|\| 28 \|\|*

*karapadmatalāraktāṃ nakhacandrairvibhūṣitām \|*  
*sthalapadmaprabhājuṣṭaṃ pādapadmaṃ ca bibhratīm \|\| 29 \|\|*

*āraktavarṇaṃ lalitamalaktakasamaprabham \|*  
*sthalapadmaiśca jalajaiḥ padmarāgavirājitām \|\| 30 \|\|*

22-30. But because of getting infatuated with passion the hair of her body stood on end. Thereafter she started staring at the lotus-like face of Saihkhacuda. Samkhacuda on his part also saw the lonely damsel in the forest; she was lying in a flower bed clad in all the clothes. She was quite beautiful and was smiling while looking at the face of Sarnkhactida. Her body was quite developed and stiff, her loins were well-developed and the breasts were quite stiff. The lines of teeth appeared like the lines of jewels and were shining, the lips resembled the colour of the ripe wood-apple. She had a beautiful nose and her complexion resembled that of molten gold. She wore the lustre of the rays of moon on her face. She was surrounded by her own lustre, her appearance was graceful and was quite charming to look at. Her body was painted with spots of kastiirl, sandal-paste and vennilion. The middle part of the hair on her head looked quite charming and her navel was quite deep. She had three lines on the belly and her palm and soles were red. She had nails like those of the moon and her feet emitted the lustre of lotus flower. Both her feet bore the red paint. She had been beautified with white and red lotus flowers. Her nails were beautiful like the moon of the winter season.

## \|\| 16.31-35 \|\|

*śaradinduvinindyaikanakhendvoghavirājitām \|*  
*amūlyaratna saṃmiśrayāvakena svalaṃkṛtām \|\| 31 \|\|*

*maṇīndramukhyakhacitakvaṇanmañjīrarañjitām \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dadhatīṃ kabarībhāraṃ mālatīmālyasaṃyutam \|*  
*amūlya ratnasaṃklṛptamakarākṛtirūpiṇā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*citrakuṇḍalayugmaśrīsuṣumāpariśobhitām \|*  
*ratnendramuktāhāraśrīstanamadhyasthalojjvalām \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ratnakaṃkaṇakeyūraśaṃkhabhūṣaṇabhūṣitām \|*  
*ratnāṃgulīyakairdivyairaṃgulyāvalibhiryutām \|\| 35 \|\|*

31-35. She was adorned with many ornaments studded with gems. The anklets worn by her on the feet were emitting the lustre of gems. She wore a garland of jasmine flowers on her breasts, besides all the gem-studded annlets, anklets, Samkha and finger rings were dazzling with gems. Thus the beautiful damsel who was quite humble, having attractive teeth was spotted by Samkhacuda. He came quietly to her and spoke in a sweet voice.

## \|\| 16.36 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ lalitāṃ ramyāṃ suśīlāṃ sudatīṃ satīm \|*  
*uvāsa tatsamīpe ca madhuraṃ tāmuvāca saḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Saihkhacuda said — О beautiful uiie, you are the best of the ladies and graceful too. Who are you? Who is your father? О damsel, О charming one, you bestow welfare to all. You tell me who you are?

## \|\| 16.37-38 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*kā tvaṃ kasya ca kanyā'si dhanye mānye suyoṣitām \|*  
*kā tvaṃ kāmini kalyāṇi sarvakalyāṇadāyini \|\| 37 \|\|*

*svargabhogādisaritivihāre hārarūpiṇi \|*  
*saṃsāradārasāre ca māyādhāre manohare \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Are you the result of heavenly pleasures? Do you roam about freely? You are adorned with a garland. Are you the essence of the universe or the base of illusion? You are quite attractive and unprecedented in the universe. You have a lean and thin body and can attract even the sages. Now breaking the silence you speak out a few words to a servant like me”.

## \|\| 16.39 \|\|

*jagadvilakṣaṇe kṣāme munīnāṃ mohakāriṇi \|*  
*maunaṃ tyaktvā kiṃkaraṃ māṃ sambhāṣāṃ kuru sundari \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. On hearing these words of Samkhacuda, the beautiful-eyed and passionate Tulasi smiled lowering her head and she spoke to the passionate youth thus.

## \|\| 16.40 \|\|

*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā sakāmā vāmalocanā \|*  
*sasmitā namravadanā sakāmaṃ tamuvāca sā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Tulasi said — “I am the daughter of Dharmadhvaja and have arrived here in this forest for performing tapas as an ascetic. Who are you? You please leave this place with comfort.

## \|\| 16.41-43 \|\|

*tulasyuvāca \|*  
*dharmadhvajasutā'haṃ ca tapāmyasyāṃ tapovane \|*  
*tapasvinīha tiṣṭhāmi kastvaṃ gaccha yathāsukham \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kāminīṃ kulajātāṃ ca rahasyekākinīṃ satīm \|*  
*na pṛcchati kule jāta evameva śrutau śrutam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*lampaṭo'satkule jāto dharmaśāstrārthavarjitaḥ \|*  
*yenāśrutaḥ śruterarthaḥ sa kāmīcchati kāminīm \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. It is usually heard that no person belonging to high race should talk to a girl in a lonely place. The one who is a cheat, born in a degraded race, unaware of the religious scriptures and the Vedas, such a passionate person becomes desirous of women. A woman seems attractive at that very moment but ultimately she proves harmful to the men because the ladies are like the pitchers filled with poison but their mouth appears to be filled with nectar.

## \|\| 16.44 \|\|

*āpāta madhurāmante cāntakāṃ puruṣasya tām \|*  
*viṣakumbhākārarūpāmamṛtāsyāṃ ca santatam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The heart of a damsel is like a sharp-edged weapon but she always speaks sweet words. She always engages herself in the successful completion of her task.

## \|\| 16.45 \|\|

*hṛdaye kṣuradhārābhāṃ śaśvanmadhurabhāṣiṇīm \|*  
*svakāryyapariniṣpattitatparāṃ satataṃ sadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In order to meet her selfish ends only she remains with her husband, otherwise, her mind is never without blemish but she wears a serene smile on her face.

## \|\| 16.46-47 \|\|

*kāryyārthe svāmivaśagāmanyathaivāvaśāṃ sadā \|*  
*svāntarmalinarūpāṃ ca prasannavadanekṣaṇām \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śrutau purāṇe yāsāṃ ca caritramanirūpitam \|*  
*tāsu ko viśvasetprājño hyaprājña iva sarvadā \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. The Vedas and the Puranas are not in favour of describing her character. And no wise person could ever believe in them. There is no one friendly or enemical to the ladies. They are always desirous of new company and always look for a beautiful person to keep their company.

## \|\| 16.48-49 \|\|

*tāsāṃ ko vā ripurmitraṃ prārthayantīṃ navaṃ navam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā suveśaṃ puruṣamicchantīṃ hṛdaye sadā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*bāhye svātmasatītvaṃ ca jñāpayantīṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*śaśvatkāmāṃ ca rāmāṃ ca kāmādhārāṃ manoharām \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. But they are always engaged in exhibiting their inward and outward chastity. The ladies are always passionate, beautiful and pleasant to look at. They always conceal their desire for union with others quite skilfully. Thus outwardly they are full of shyness but in seclusion they bite their husband.

## \|\| 16.50 \|\|

*bāhye chalācchādayantīṃ svāntarmaithunalālasām \|*  
*kāntaṃ grasantīṃ rahasi bāhye'tīva sulajjitām \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This type of women, when dissatisfied with their union becomes immensely enraged. This gives rise to their quarrelsome nature. They find delight in the excess of conjugal pleasure and feel sad when they have little of it.

## \|\| 16.51 \|\|

*māninīṃ maithunābhāve kopinīṃ kalahāṃkurām \|*  
*saṃbhītāṃ bhūrisambhogātsvalpamaithunaduḥkhitām \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. In their mind, they always desire for the best of food, the cool water, the beautiful, passionate, young and virtuous husband.

## \|\| 16.52 \|\|

*sumṛṣṭānnaṃ śītatoyamākāṃkṣantīṃ ca mānase \|*  
*sundaraṃ rasikaṃ kāntaṃ yuvānaṃ guṇinaṃ sadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The person with whom they enjoy conjugal pleasure; they love him much better than their own sons. Such of the people as are well-versed in the love-sports are quite dear to them.

## \|\| 16.53-54 \|\|

*sutātparamatisnehaṃ kurvantīṃ ratikartari \|*  
*prāṇādhikaṃ priyatamaṃ sambhoga kuśalaṃ priyam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*paśyantīṃ riputulyaṃ ca vṛddhaṃ vā maithunākṣamam \|*  
*kalahaṃ kurvatī śaśvattena sārddhaṃ sukopanām \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. They consider the old and the weak people as their enemies. Getting annoyed with them they always keep on quarrelling. While quarrelling, they intend to deal with them like the god of death. Thus becoming the figure of discourage, they admit all the evils in themselves.

## \|\| 16.55-57 \|\|

*carcayā bhakṣayantīṃ taṃ kīnāśa iva gorajaḥ \|*  
*dussāhasasvarūpāṃ ca sarvadoṣāśrayāṃ sadā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śaśvatkapaṭarūpāṃ ca sarvadoṣāśrayāṃ sadā \|*  
*brahma viṣṇuśivādīnāṃ dustyājyāṃ moharūpiṇīm \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tapomārgārgalāṃ śaśvanmuktidvārakapāṭikām \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. Turning to a deceitful form, the ladies are unmanageable and get beyond control. They are considered to be beyond the control of Brahma. Vishnu and Shiva. They are full of illusion. They are best suited to obstruct the path of performing lapas and they are quite competent to close the doors of salvation. They are obstruction in the devotion of lord Vishnu and are filled with illusion. They serve as a bondage in the captivity of the universe.

## \|\| 16.58-61 \|\|

*harerbhaktivyavahitāṃ sarvamāyā karaṇḍikām \|*  
*saṃsārakārāgāre ca śaśvannigaḍarūpiṇīm \|\| 58 \|\|*

*indrajālasvarūpāṃ ca mithyāvādisvarūpiṇīm \|*  
*bibhratīṃ bāhya saundaryaṃ madhyāṅgamatikutsitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*nānāviṇmūtrapūyānāmādhāraṃ malasaṃyutam \|*  
*durgandhi doṣasaṃyuktaṃ raktāktaṃ cāpyasaṃskṛtam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*māyārūpaṃ māyināṃ ca vidhinā nirmitaṃ purā \|*  
*viṣarūpāṃ mumukṣūṇāmadṛśyāṃcaiva sarvadā \|\| 61 \|\|*

58-61. Therefore a woman is like the magic and indeed is the form of untruth. She remains completely beautiful outwardly but she conceals her evil design in her own mind. Her body is filled with refuse, urine, puss and dirt besides other troublesome elements. Soaked in blood and filled with evil, her body never remains purified. At the time of the creation of the universe, Brahma created the woman who is filled with illusion for the illusory people. She serves as a poison for the people who are desirous of achieving salvation. Therefore such of the people as are desirous of achieving salvation should never look at them.” О Narada, after thus speaking to Sarirkhacuda, Tulasi kept quiet. Thereafter Samkhacuda said.

## \|\| 16.62-64 \|\|

*ityuktvā tulasī taṃ ca virarāma ca nārada \|*  
*sasmitaḥ śaṃkhacūḍaśca pravaktumupacakrame \|\| 62 \|\|*

*śaṃkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*tvayā yatkathitaṃ devi na ca sarvamalīkakam \|*  
*kiṃcitsatyamalīkaṃ ca kiṃcinmatto niśāmaya \|\| 63 \|\|*

*nirmitaṃ dvividhaṃ dhātrā strīrūpaṃ sarvamohanam \|*  
*kṛtyārūpaṃ vāstavaṃ ca praśasyaṃ cāpraśaṃsitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. Samkhacuda said — “О goddess whatever you have spoken is not totally untrue. Some of it is tmthful while some of it is untruthful. I also now tell you something, you please listen to me. Brahma the creator of the universe divided women into two parts: one was her true form and the other was her illusory form. The first one is praise-worthy. The creator, at the beginning of creation, created first of all Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Durga, Savitri, Radhika and other goddesses who represent the true form of the universe besides being the source for the creation of the universe.

## \|\| 16.65 \|\|

*lakṣmī sarasvatī durgā sāvitrī rādhikādikam \|*  
*sṛṣṭisūtrasvarūpaṃ cāpyādyaṃ sraṣṭvā tu nirmitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Whatever female forms were created out of these goddesses are really commendable, glorious and bestower of welfare.

## \|\| 16.66-71 \|\|

*etāsāmaṃśarūpaṃ yatstrīrūpaṃ vāstavaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tatpraśaṃsyaṃ yaśorūpaṃ sarvamaṅgalakāraṇam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*śatarūpā devahūtissvadhā svāhā ca dakṣiṇā \|*  
*chāyāvatī rohiṇī ca varuṇānī śacī tathā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*kuberavāyupatnī sā'pyaditiśca ditistathā \|*  
*lopāmudrā'nasūyā ca kaiṭabhī tulasī tathā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ahalyā'rundhatī menā tārā mandodarī parā \|*  
*damayantī vedavatī gaṃgā ca yamunā tathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*puṣṭistuṣṭiḥ smṛtirmedhā kālikā ca vasundharā \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhī maṃgalacaṇḍī ca mūrtirvai dharmakāminī \|\| 70 \|\|*

*svastiḥ śraddhā ca kāntiśca tuṣṭiḥ śāntistathā parā \|*  
*nidrā tandrā kṣutpipāsā sandhyā rātrirdināni ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

66-71. All the forms of the goddesses like Satarupa, DevahutI, Svadha, Svaha, tlaksina, Chayavati, Rohini, VarunanI, IndranT, spouse of Kubera, spouse of Vayu, Aditi, Diti, Lopamudra, AnusOya, Kaitabhl, Tulasi, Ahalya, Arundhati, Mena, Tara, Mandodarl, Damayanti, Vedavati, Ganga, Yamuna, Pusti, Tusti, Smrti, Medha, Kalika, Vasundhara, MangalachandT, SasthI, Mtirti wife of Dhanna, Svasti, Sraddha, Kanti, Santi, Nidra, Tandra, Ksudha, Pipasa, sandhya, Ratri, Dina, Sampatti, Vrlti, Klrti, Kriya, Sobha, Prabha and others who emerged in the universe, are considered to be the best of the female forms and they have been considered to be those who always bestow pleasures.

## \|\| 16.72 \|\|

*sampattivṛttikīrtyaśca kriyāśobhāprabhāṃśakam \|*  
*yatstrīrūpaṃ ca sambhūtamuttamaṃ tadyuge yuge \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Therefore the other female form represents the illusion in her. The Apsaras of the heaven are also considered to be illusory. They are known as wicked women devoid of grace in the entire universe.

## \|\| 16.73-74 \|\|

*kṛtyāsvarūpaṃ tadyattu svarveśyādikameva ca \|*  
*tadapraśaṃsyaṃ viśveṣu puṃścalīrūpameva ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

*sattvapradhānaṃ yadrūpaṃ tacca śuddhaṃ svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*taduttamaṃ ca viśveṣu sādhvīrūpaṃ praśaṃsitam \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. Such of the goddesses who represent the Sattvagunu, are by nature taken to be quite pure. Being quite chaste and the best in the universe, they are always praised by the people. Therefore, they are called as the images of reality by the intellectuals. On the other hand, the Krtyas (or the evil women) have two forms representing Rajoguna and Tamoguna.

## \|\| 16.75-77 \|\|

*tadvāstavaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*rajorūpaṃ tamorūpaṃ kṛtyāsu dvividhaṃ smṛtam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*sthānābhāvātkṣaṇābhāvānmadhyavṛtterabhāvataḥ \|*  
*dehakleśena rogeṇa satsaṃsargeṇa sundari \|\| 76 \|\|*

*bahugoṣṭhā vṛtenaiva ripurājabhayena ca \|*  
*rajorūpasya sādhvītvamatainaivopajāyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. О beautiful one. because of the shortage of time and space, non-availability of male or female messenger, pain of the body, disease, good company, surrounded by the many people, the fear of the enemy of the king, these are the reasons by which the chaste ladies protect their chastity. Such ladies are called the mediocre. Such of the ladies in whom the Tamoguna predominates are quite wicked by nature and they are called as degraded ones by the wise people.

## \|\| 16.78-80 \|\|

*idaṃ madhyamarūpaṃ ca pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*tamorūpaṃ durnivāryyamadhamaṃ tadvidurbudhāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*na pṛcchati kule jātaḥ paṇḍitaśca parastriyam \|*  
*nirjane durjane vā'pi rahasye vacasāṃ striyam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*āgacchāmi tvatsamīpamājñayā brahmaṇo'dhunā \|*  
*gāndharveṇa vivāhena tvāṃ grahīṣyāmi śobhane \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. Though the people of the higher strata of the society never prefer to talk to lonely ladies in a scheduled place yet I have arrived here at the command of Brahma to meet you. О beautiful one, 1 intend to marry you by the Gandharva method. I am born in the race of Manu and have subjugated many of the gods. I am known by the name of Samkhacuda. I am the one who was known as cowherd 3udama in the Goloka during earlier times.

## \|\| 16.81-82 \|\|

*ahameva śaṅkhacūḍo devavidrāvakārakaḥ \|*  
*danuvaṃśodbhavo viśve sudāmā'haṃ hareḥ pure \|\| 81 \|\|*

*ahamaṣṭasu gopeṣu gogopīpārṣadeṣu ca \|*  
*adhunā dānavendro'haṃ rādhikāyāśca śāpataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. I am one of the eight prominent cowherds of the lord. I became the king of Danavas with the curse of the goddess Radhika. I remember the happenings of my earlier birth because of the influence of the mantra of lord Krishna. You are also aware of the events of your past life because you have also been Tulasi a cowherdesses of Krishna in your earlier life.

## \|\| 16.83-84 \|\|

*jātismaro'haṃ jānāmi kṛṣṇamantraprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*jātismarā tvaṃ tulasī saṃsaktā hariṇā purā \|\| 83 \|\|*

*tvameva rādhikākopājjātā'si bhārate bhuvi \|*  
*tvāṃ sambhoktumicchako'haṃ nālaṃ rādhābhayāttataḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. You have also arrived on earth because of the curse of Radhika. In the Goloka I was extremely desirous of your company. I could not get my wish fulfilled because of the fear of Radhika.” О great sage, after speaking these words Saihkhacuda kept quiet. Thereafter Tulasi started speaking delightfully wearing a smile on her face.

## \|\| 16.85 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā sa pumānvirarāma mahāmune \|*  
*sasmitā tulasī hṛṣṭā pravaktumupacakrame \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Tulasi said — Only such types of noble people are praised in the universe and a lady always becomes desirous of having such a person as her husband.

## \|\| 16.86 \|\|

*tulasyuvāca \|*  
*evaṃvidho budho viśve budheṣu ca praśaṃsitaḥ \|*  
*kāntamevaṃvidhaṃ kāntā śaśvadicchati kāmataḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. At the moment I have been defeated by your arguments. Such of the persons who are defeated by the ladies are denounced and are considered to be unclean.

## \|\| 16.87 \|\|

*tvayā'hamadhunā satyaṃ vicāreṇa parājitā \|*  
*sa ninditaścāpyaśuciryaḥ pumāṃśca striyā jitaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The gods and the manes denounce the persons who are defeated by their wives. The father and brothers also denounce them in their mind as well as in speech.

## \|\| 16.88-91 \|\|

*nindanti pitaro devā bāndhavāḥ strījitaṃ janam \|*  
*strījitaṃ manasā vācā pitā bhrātā ca nindati \|\| 88 \|\|*

*śudhyedvipro daśāhena jātake mṛtake tathā \|*  
*bhūmipo dvādaśāhena vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhataḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*śūdro māsena vedeṣu mātṛvadvarṇasaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*aśuciḥ strījitaḥ śudhyeccitādahanakālataḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*na gṛhṇantīcchayā tasya pitaraḥ piṇḍatarpaṇam \|*  
*na gṛhṇantīcchayā devāsta sya puṣpajalādikam \|\| 91 \|\|*

88-91. At the time of birth and death a Brahmana is purified after ten days, a Kshatriya after twelve days, a Vaishya in fifteen days and a Sitdra in a month, but the illegitimate sons, his mother and the unclean person defeated by his wife can be purified only at the fire altar. This is what has been ordained in the Vedas. The Pindas and Tarpana offered by such people are not accepted by manes willingly and the flowers and other offerings given by such people to the gods are not accepted by them willingly. Therefore the performing of tapas, japam, achieving of knowledge, performing of homa and the adorations, are of no consequence. Therefore their education and glory are of no consequence who are controlled by the lady.

## \|\| 16.92 \|\|

*kiṃ tasya jñānatapasā japahomaprapūjanaiḥ \|*  
*kiṃ vidyayā vā yaśasā strībhiryasya mano hṛtam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. I had put you to test in order to know your education and influence because a damsel accepts one as her husband only after fully examining him.

## \|\| 16.93-95 \|\|

*vidyāprabhāvajñānārthaṃ mayā tvaṃ ca parīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā parīkṣāṃ kāntasya vṛṇoti kāminī varam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*varāya guṇahīnāya vṛddhāyājñānine tathā \|*  
*daridrāya ca mūrkhāya rogiṇe kutsitāya ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

*atyantakopayuktāya cātyantadurmukhāya ca \|*  
*paṃgulāyāṅgahīnāya cāndhāya badhirāya ca \|\| 95 \|\|*

93-95. The one who is devoid of virtues, is old, foolish, a pauper, devoid of wisdom, suffering from ailment, denounced, immensely enraged, indulging in ill talk, deformed, blind, absolutely foolish, dumb, devoid of strength or a sinner, cannot be given a daughter in marriage and the one who does so, attracts the sin of Brahmahatya.

## \|\| 16.96 \|\|

*jaḍāya caiva mūkāya klībatulyāya pāpine \|*  
*brahmahatyāṃ labhetso'pi yaḥ svakanyāṃ dadāti ca \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The one who is peaceful, virtuous, young, educated and a Vaishnava should be given the daughter in maniage and whosoever does so he earns the merit of Asvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 16.97 \|\|

*śāntāya guṇine caiva yūne ca viduṣe'pi ca \|*  
*vaiṣṇavāya sutāṃ dattvā daśavājiphalaṃ labhet \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The one who after bringing up a daughter, influenced by a calamity or greed, sells away the daughter, lie is thrown into the terrific hell.

## \|\| 16.98-99 \|\|

*yaḥ kanyāpālanaṃ kṛtvā karoti vikrayaṃ yadi \|*  
*vipadā dhanalobhena kumbhīpākaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 98 \|\|*

*kanyāmūtrapurīṣaṃ ca tatra bhakṣati pātakī \|*  
*kṛmibhirdaśitaḥ kākairyāvadindrāścaturdaśa \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. And that sinner by the suffering in hell has to be content with the refuse of the same girl as his food. He is tortured by insects and crows till the age of fourteen Indras. Ultimately he is reborn in the family of a hunter, where he has to carry the meat or flesh on his head for selling it day and night.

## \|\| 16.100 \|\|

*tadante vyādhayonau ca labhate janma niścitam \|*  
*vikrīṇāti māṃsabhāraṃ vahatyeva divāniśam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Thus speaking Tulasi kept quiet in the hermitage. In the meantime Brahma arrived there in front of both of them.

## \|\| 16.101 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā tulasī virarāma tapovane \|*  
*etasminnantare brahmā tayorantikamāyayau \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. О Narada, both Tulasi and Samkhacuda bowed in reverence to him, Brahma then spoke to them the beneficial words.

## \|\| 16.102-104 \|\|

*mūrdhnā nanāma tulasī śaṅkhacūḍaśca nārada \|*  
*uvāsa tatra deveśaścovāca ca tayorhitam \|\| 102 \|\|*

*kiṃ karoṣi śaṅkhacūḍa saṃvādamanayā saha \|*  
*gāndharveṇa vivāhena tvamasyā grahaṇaṃ kuru \|\| 103 \|\|*

*tvaṃ ca puruṣaratnaṃ ca strīratnaṃ strīṣviyaṃ satī \|*  
*vidagdhāyā vidagdhena saṅgamo guṇavānbhavet \|\| 104 \|\|*

102-104. Brahma said — О Samkhacuda, why are you entering in discussion with her? You perform a Gandharva marriage with her because you are the gem of the men folks and she happens to be the gem of a lady. The union of the passionate couple is always pleasant. О king, the pleasure without the obstruction is difficult to get. Therefore who can disown it. On the other hand the one who ignores such a type of pleasure is considered to be a fool. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 16.105 \|\|

*nirvirodhasukhaṃ rājanko vā tyajati durlabham \|*  
*yo'virodhasukhatyāgī sa paśurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. On the other hand, why do you neglect such a competent person after getting him. He is beautiful, virtuous and has defeated all the gods and the demons.

## \|\| 16.106-111 \|\|

*kimupekṣasi tvaṃ kāntamīdṛśaṃ guṇinaṃ satī \|*  
*devānāmasurāṇāṃ ca dānavānāṃ vimardanam \|\| 106 \|\|*

*yathā lakṣmīśca lakṣmīśe yathā kṛṣṇe ca rādhikā \|*  
*yathā mayi ca sāvitrī bhavānī ca bhave yathā \|\| 107 \|\|*

*yathā dharā varāhe ca yathā menā himālaye \|*  
*yathā'trāvanasūyā ca damayantī nale yathā \|\| 108 \|\|*

*rohiṇī ca yathā candre yathā kāme ratiḥ satī \|*  
*yathā ditiḥ kaśyape ca vaśiṣṭhe'rundhatī yathā \|\| 109 \|\|*

*yathā'halyā gautame ca devahūtiśca kardame \|*  
*yathā bṛhaspatau tārā śatarūpā manau yathā \|\| 110 \|\|*

*yathā ca dakṣiṇā yajñe yathā svāhā hutāśane \|*  
*yathā śacī mahendre ca yathā puṣṭirgaṇeśvare \|\| 111 \|\|*

106-111. As the goddess Lakshmi is devoted to Vishnu, Radha is devoted to Shri Krishna, Savitri to me, BhavanI to Shiva, PrthivT to lord Varaha, Mena to Himalaya, Anusuya to Atri, Damayanti to Nala, Rohini to Chandrama, Rati to Kamadeva, Diti to Kashyapa, Arundhatl to Vasistha, Ahalya to Gautama, Devahuti to Kardama, Tara to Brihaspati, Satarupa to Manu, daksina to yajna, Svaha to Agni, IndranI to Indra, Push to Ganesha, Devsena to Skanda, Murti to Dharma, similarly Sarirkhaciida will be immensely loved by you and you should become his beloved.

## \|\| 16.112 \|\|

*devasenā yathā skande dharme mūttiryathā satī \|*  
*saubhāgyā supriyā tvaṃ ca śaṅkhacūḍe tathā bhava \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. О beautiful one, with Samkhacirda you go at any place of your choice.

## \|\| 16.113 \|\|

*anena sārddhaṃ suciraṃ sundareṇa ca sundari \|*  
*sthāne sthāne vihāraṃ ca yathecchaṃ kuru santatam \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. At the end of the life of Samkhacuda you will proceed Vaikuntha and achieve the four-armed lord Vishnu and in Goloka you achieve Govind again.

## \|\| 16.114 \|\|

*paścātprāpsyasi govindaṃ goloke punareva ca \|*  
*caturbhujaṃ ca vaikuṇṭhe śaṃkhacūḍe mṛte sati \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Thus speaking lord Brahma left for his abode. Thereafter, SamkhacQda and Tulasi were married in the Gandharva style.

## \|\| 16.115-118 \|\|

*ityevamāśiṣaṃ kṛtvā svālayaṃ prayayau vidhiḥ \|*  
*gāndharveṇa vivāhena jagṛhe tāṃ ca dānavaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*svarge dundubhivādyaṃ ca puṣpavṛṣṭirbabhūva ha \|*  
*sa reme ramayā sārddhaṃ vāsagehe manohare \|\| 116 \|\|*

*mūrcchāṃ samprāpa tulasī navasaṅgamasaṅgatā \|*  
*nimagnā nirjane sādhvī sambhogasukha sāgare \|\| 117 \|\|*

*catuḥṣaṣṭikalāmānaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭividhaṃ sukham \|*  
*kāmaśāstraṃ yanniruktaṃ rasikānāṃ yathepsitam \|\| 118 \|\|*

115-118. At the time of festivities, the gods started playing on the drums and showered flowers on them. Thereafter Samkhactida enjoyed the company of his beloved in his abode. During the new union, Tulasi fainted but afterwards when she regained her consciousness the chaste lady roamed about in the forest with her husband enjoying all the conjugal pleasures. The Kdmasiilra has defined sixty four types of conjugal pleasures for the lovers and they enjoyed all of them in practice.

## \|\| 16.119-121 \|\|

*aṅgapratyaṃga saṃśleṣapūrvakaṃ strīmanoharam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ sukhaśṛṃgāraṃ cakāra rasikeśvaraḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

*atīva ramyedeśe ca sarvajantuvivarjite \|*  
*puṣpacandanatalpe ca puṣpacandanavāyunā \|\| 120 \|\|*

*puṣpodyāne nadītīre puṣpacandanacarcite \|*  
*gṛhītvā rasikāṃ rāmāṃ puṣpacandanacarcitām \|\| 121 \|\|*

119-121. They visited extremely charming places, devoid of all creatures on the beds of flowers, in the air scented with sandal-paste, they enjoyed themselves pretty well. Besides they roamed about on the banks of the rivers, in the flower orchards, the beds decorated with flowers and sandal-paste, decorating Tulasi with all the ornaments. They went on enjoying themselves and their joy knew no bounds.

## \|\| 16.122 \|\|

*bhūṣitāṃ bhūṣaṇaiḥ sarvairatīva sumanoharām \|*  
*suraterviratirnāsti tayoḥ suratavijñayoḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. The chaste Tulasi attracted the mind of her husband with her performance and the lover on the other hand attracted the mind of Tulasi to him immensely.

## \|\| 16.123 \|\|

*jahāra mānasaṃ bharturlīlayā tulasī satī \|*  
*cetanāṃ rasikāyāśca jahāra rasabhāvavit \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. The chaste Tulasi then while engaged in the love-sport removed the sandal-paste on the chest and arms of SamkhacOda and then took away her Bindupaira.

## \|\| 16.124 \|\|

*vakṣasaścandanaṃ bāhvostilakaṃ vijahāra sā \|*  
*sa ca jagrāha tasyāśca sindūrabindupatrakam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Filled with pleasure, he drew lines over her breasts while she on her part carved his arms with her ornaments.

## \|\| 16.125 \|\|

*sa tadvakṣasi tasyāśca nakharekhāṃ dadau mudā \|*  
*sā dadau tadvāmapārśve karabhūṣaṇalakṣaṇam \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Her back was beaten by the king while his cheeks were bitten by Tulasi.

## \|\| 16.126-130 \|\|

*rājā tadoṣṭhapuṭake dadau daśanadaṃśanam \|*  
*tadgaṇḍayugale sā ca pradadau taccaturguṇam \|\| 126 \|\|*

*suraterviratau tau ca samutthāya parasparam \|*  
*suveśaṃ cakratustatra yattanmanasi vāñchitam \|\| 127 \|\|*

*kuṅkumāktacandanena sā tasmai tilakaṃ dadau \|*  
*sarvāṅge sundare ramye cakāra cānulepanam \|\| 128 \|\|*

*suvāsitaṃ ca tāmbūlaṃ vahniśuddhe ca vāsasī \|*  
*pārijātasya kusumaṃ mālyaṃ caiva suśobhanam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnanirmāṇamaṃgulīyakamuttamam \|*  
*sundaraṃ ca maṇivaraṃ triṣu lokeṣu durlabham \|\| 130 \|\|*

126-130. After enjoying the love-sport both of them got up and started decorating each other. Tulasi then applied the tilakam of saffron mixed with sandal-paste over his entire body. Thereafter she offered pure and beautiful betel to him besides two garments and a garland of Parijata flowers. She also offered the gem-studded valuable ring which was difficult to get in the three worlds. The best of gems was studded in it. After making Sarnkhacuda wear the ornaments, she repeated to him again and again that she was his slave. Thereafter she bowed in reverence to her husband with great devotion.

## \|\| 16.131 \|\|

*dāsī tavāhamityevaṃ samuccārya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*nanāma parayā bhaktyā svāminaṃ guṇaśālinam \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Tulasi then started staring with side glances at the lotus-like face of SamkhacOda.

## \|\| 16.132 \|\|

*sasmitā tanmukhāṃbhojaṃ locanābhyāṃ papau punaḥ \|*  
*nimeṣarahitābhyāṃ ca sakaṭākṣaṃ ca sundaram \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. At that point of time the youth pushed her towards himself and embraced her looking at the lotus-like face of his beloved who was covered with cloth.

## \|\| 16.133-134 \|\|

*sa ca tāṃ ca samākṛṣya cakāra vakṣasi priyām \|*  
*sasmitaṃ vāsasā''cchannaṃ dadarśa mukhapaṅkajam \|\| 133 \|\|*

*cucumba kaṭhine gaṇḍe bimboṣṭhe punareva ca \|*  
*dadau tasyai vastrayugmaṃ varuṇādāhṛtaṃ ca yat \|*  
*tadāhṛtāṃ ratnamālāṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutām \|\| 134 \|\|*

133-134. Thereafter he kissed her temples and lips which were like the ripe wood-apple fruit. Thereafter he offered her the costumes brought by him from the place of Varuna and the garland of gems which was praised in the three worlds.

## \|\| 16.135-139 \|\|

*dadau mañjīrayugmaṃ ca svāhāyāśca hṛtaṃ ca yat \|*  
*keyūrayugmaṃ chāyāyā rohiṇyāścaiva kuṇḍalam \|\| 135 \|\|*

*aṃgulīyakaratnāni ratyāśca varabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*śaṅkhaṃ suruciraṃ citraṃ yaddattaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 136 \|\|*

*vicitrapīṭhakaśreṇīṃ śayyāṃ cāpi sudurlabhām \|*  
*bhūṣaṇāni ca dattvā ca parīhāraṃ cakāra ha \|\| 137 \|\|*

*nirmāya kabarībhāraṃ tasyāśca mālyasaṃyutam \|*  
*sucitraṃ patrakaṃ gaṇḍe jayalekhasamaṃ tathā \|\| 138 \|\|*

*candralekhātribhiryuktaṃ candanena sugandhinā \|*  
*paritaḥ paritaścitraiḥ sārddhaṃ kuṃkumabindubhiḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

135-139. He also handed over to her two nupuras (anklets) which he had snatched from Svaha, two armlets he snatched from chayci, the kundalas of Rohini, the finger ring and other ornaments from Rati, the Sarhkha from Vishvakarma besides beautiful paintings and several other beautiful types of beads and beds. She was adorned with several ornaments. He provided her with three fragrant lines of moon. He decorated her person with several types of spots of saffron.

## \|\| 16.140-151 \|\|

*jvalatpradīpākāraṃ ca sindūratilakaṃ dadau \|*  
*tatpādapadmayugale sthalapadmavinindite \|\| 140 \|\|*

*citrālaktakarāgaṃ ca nakhareṣu dadau mudā \|*  
*svavakṣasi muhurnyastaṃ sarāgaṃ caraṇāmbujam \|\| 141 \|\|*

*he devi tava dāso'hamityuccāryya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*ratnanirmāṇayānena tāṃ ca kṛtvā svavakṣasi \|\| 142 \|\|*

*tapovanaṃ parityajya rājāsthānāntaraṃ yayau \|*  
*malaye devanilaye śaile śaile vane vane \|\| 143 \|\|*

*sthāne sthāne'tiramye ca puṣpodyāne'tinirjane \|*  
*kandare kandare sindhutīre ca sundare vane \|\| 144 \|\|*

*puṣpabhadrānadītīre nīravātamanohare \|*  
*puline puline divye nadyāṃ nadyāṃ nade nade \|\| 145 \|\|*

*madhau madhukarāṇāṃ ca madhuradhvaninādite \|*  
*vinisyande supavane nandane gandhamādane \|\| 146 \|\|*

*devodyāne devavane citre candanakānane \|*  
*campakānāṃ ketakīnāṃ mādhavīnāṃ ca mādhave \|\| 147 \|\|*

*kundānāṃ mālatīnāṃ ca kumudāmbhojakānane \|*  
*kalpavṛkṣe kalpavṛkṣe pārijātavane vane \|\| 148 \|\|*

*nirjane kāñcanīsthāne dhanye kāñcanaparvate \|*  
*kāñcīvane kiñcanake kañcake kāñcanākare \|\| 149 \|\|*

*puṣpacandanatalpe ca puṃskokilarutaśrute \|*  
*puṣpacandanasaṃyuktaḥ puṣpacandanavāyunā \|\| 150 \|\|*

*kāmukyā kāmukaḥ kāmātsa reme rāmayā saha \|*  
*na tṛpto dānavendraśca tṛptiṃ naiva jagāma sā \|\| 151 \|\|*

140-151. He made a tilakam on the forehead of Tulasi of the type of the flame of the burning lamp and also plastered her feet with the red paint. Thereafter placing her feet on his chest he spoke out again and again, “O goddess I am your slave”. Thereafter, embracing her, SamkhacCtda took her to the gem-studded plane and boarded it. He then left the Tapovana for some other place in the plane and they roamed about over Malaya mountain, places of the gods, the mountain, the forest, the charming places and the orchards situated in the lonely places, the caves, the beautiful Sindhu river with the beautiful forests on its banks, on the banks of river Puspabhadra, the river banks having a pleasant climate, divine rivers and rivulets, in the gardens filled with the black wasps creating hissing sounds, in the Nandana forest, on the Gandhamadana mountain, divine orchards, the Chitraratha forest, sandal-wood forest, the forest of jasmine plants, Madhavi creepers, the lotuses, the jasmine, the kalpavrksa and Parijata forest, in the scheduled golden places, beautiful Sumeru mountain, Kahcl forest, Kinjalaka forest, the places having gold mines, sleeping on the beds of flowers and sandal-paste, hearing the sweet tones of cuckoo, enjoying breeze filled with the fragrance of flowers and sandal-wood, places decorated with flowers and sandal-paste, both the passionate lovers enjoyed the conjugal pleasures without getting any satisfaction.

## \|\| 16.152-153 \|\|

*haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva vavṛdhe madanastayoḥ \|*  
*tayā saha samāgatya svāśramaṃ dānavastataḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*ramyaṃ krīḍālayaṃ kṛtvā vijahāra punastataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ saṃbubhuje rājyaṃ śaṅkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 153 \|\|*

152-153. As the ghee ignites flames in the fire, similarly by keeping constant company of each other both of them became more and more passionate. Thereafter the demon king returned to his own home with Tulasi and resided in a separate palace built with the specific purpose and continued enjoying love sports with her. The entire kingdom of glorious Sarhkbacuda experienced great pleasure.

## \|\| 16.154-155 \|\|

*ekamanvantaraṃ pūrṇaṃ rājarājeśvaro balī \|*  
*devānāmasurāṇāṃ ca dānavānāṃ ca santatam \|\| 154 \|\|*

*gandharvāṇāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca śāstidaḥ \|*  
*hatādhikārā devāśca caranti bhikṣukā yathā \|\| 155 \|\|*

154-155. The great, king of the demons ruled over the countries of gods, Asuras, Danavas, Gandharvas and Kinnaras for a memvantara. Having been deprived of the kingdom by SamkhacQda, the gods became a wandering lot and they roamed about everywhere like beggars.

## \|\| 16.156 \|\|

*pūjāhomādikaṃ teṣāṃ jahāra viṣayaṃ balāt \|*  
*āśrayaṃ cādhikāraṃ ca śastrāstrabhūṣaṇādikam \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. Sarnkhactida on his part had usurped from the gods the performing of puja, their kingdom, their homes, their rights, their weapons and ornaments forcibly.

## \|\| 16.157 \|\|

*nirudyamāḥ surāḥ sarve citraputtalikā yathā \|*  
*te ca sarve viṣaṇṇāśca prajagmurbrahmaṇaḥ sabhām \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. As a result of this, the dejected gods became like puppets. Thereafter, they felt grieved and they went to the court of Brahma.

## \|\| 16.158 \|\|

*vṛttāntaṃ kathayāmāsū ruruduśca bhṛśaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*tadā brahmā suraiḥ sārddhaṃ jagāma śaṅkarālayam \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. After narrating the tale of their suffering they started crying. Thereafter Brahma accompanied them to lord Shiva.

## \|\| 16.159 \|\|

*sarvaṃ saṃkathayāmāsa vidhātā candraśekharam \|*  
*brahmā śivaśca taiḥ sārddhaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ ca jagāma ha \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. Brahma narrated the entire tale of the suffering of the gods to lord Shiva, as a result of which Shiva took them all to Vaikuntha.

## \|\| 16.160 \|\|

*sudurlabhaṃ paraṃ dhāma jarāmṛtyuharaṃ param \|*  
*samprāpa ca varaṃ dvāramāśramāṇāṃ hareraho \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. Lord Shiva took them all to Vaikuntha where the death, old age has no place and reached the great abode of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 16.161-162 \|\|

*dadarśa dvārapālāṃśca ratnasiṃhāsanasthitān \|*  
*śobhitānpītavastraiśca ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitān \|\| 161 \|\|*

*vanamālānvitānsarvānśyāmasundaravigrahān \|*  
*śaṃkhacakragadāpadmadharāṃścaiva caturbhujān \|\| 162 \|\|*

161-162. He found the gatekeepers seated on the gem-studded lion-thrones, who were clad in yellow lower garments and adorned with gem-studded ornaments. They were also wearing long garland of flowers and were holding shamkha, gada, padma in their four arms.

## \|\| 16.163 \|\|

*sasmitānpadmavaktrāṃśca padmanetrānmanoharān \|*  
*brahmā tānkathayāmāsa vṛttāntaṃ gamanārthakam \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. Brahma then spoke to the gate-keeper having lotus-like faces and lotus-like eyes about the reason for their arrival.

## \|\| 16.164-165 \|\|

*te'nujñāṃ ca dadustasmai praviveśa tadājñayā \|*  
*evaṃ ca ṣoḍaśa dvārānnirīkṣya kamalodbhavaḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

*devaḥ sārddhaṃ tānatītya praviveśa hareḥ sabhām \|*  
*devarṣibhiḥ parivṛtāṃ pārṣadaiśca caturbhujaiḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

164-165. Thereafter both of them permitted the gods to enter the chamber of Vishnu. Thereafter Brahma crossing sixteen gates reached the assembly of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 16.166-167 \|\|

*nārāyaṇasvarūpaiśca sarvaiḥ kaustubhabhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*pūrṇendumaṇḍalākārāṃ caturasrāṃ manoharām \|\| 166 \|\|*

*maṇīndrasāranirmāṇāṃ hīrāsārasuśobhitām \|*  
*amūlyaratnakhacitāṃ racitāṃ svecchayā hareḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

166-167. All the courtiers of that place appeared in the form of lord Vishnu and wore the kaustubha gems. They were seated like full moon, in a circular as well as square arrangements and looked quite charming, adorned with all the gems. They were seated on the thrones studded with precious gems which were arranged as per the desire of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 16.168-171 \|\|

*māṇikyamālājālāḍhyāṃ muktāpaṃktivibhūṣitām \|*  
*maṇḍitāṃ maṇḍalākārai ratnadarpaṇakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

*vicitraiścitrarekhābhirnānācitravicitritām \|*  
*padmarāgendraracitai racitāṃ padmakṛtrimaiḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

*sopānaśatakairyuktāṃ syamantakavinirmitaiḥ \|*  
*paṭṭasūtragranthiyutaiścārucandanapallavaiḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

*indranīlamaṇistambhairveṣṭitāṃ sumanoramām \|*  
*sadratnapūrṇakumbhānāṃ samūhaiśca samanvitām \|\| 171 \|\|*

168-171. They were wearing garlands of rubies and strings of pearls which added to their beauty. The court of lord Vishnu was also decorated with crores of mirrors resembling gems. Many of the paintings hung on the walls were adding to its beauty. It was beautified with lotus-like gems and artificial lotuses which looked quite charming, the steps which were made of Syamantaka gems added to the beauty of the place. Tied in the silken cord, the sandal-wood leaves were looking like gates. The pillars of the place were studded with Indranila gems. The place was flooded with vases of gems which were adding to the beauty of the court.

## \|\| 16.172-173 \|\|

*pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālājālairvirājitām \|*  
*kastūrīkuṅkumāktaiśca sugandhicandanadravaiḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

*susaṃskṛtāṃ tu sarvatra vāsitā gandhavāyunā \|*  
*vidyādharīsamūhānāṃ saṅgītaiśca manoharam \|\| 173 \|\|*

172-173. There were several garlands of Parijata (undecaying) flowers. The fragrance of kastUrl and saffron pervaded the entire court. The place was scented with beautiful fragrance and the sweet music of Vidyadharis.

## \|\| 16.174-177 \|\|

*sahasrayojanāyāmāṃ paripūrṇāṃ ca kiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*dadarśa śrīhariṃ brahmā śaṅkaraiśca suraiḥ saha \|\| 174 \|\|*

*vasantaṃ tanmadhyadeśe yathendraṃ tārakāvṛtam \|*  
*amūlyaratnanirmāṇacitrasiṃhāsanasthitam \|\| 175 \|\|*

*kirīṭinaṃ kuṇḍalinaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*śaṅkhacakragadāpadmadhāriṇaṃ ca caturbhujam \|\| 176 \|\|*

*navīnanīradaśyāmaṃ sundaraṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*amūlyaratnanirmāṇasarvābharaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 177 \|\|*

174-177. It was spread over an area of a thousand yojanas which was fully guarded with guards. Thus lord Shiva had an audience with lord Vishnu together with Brahma and other gods. He was seated in the court like the moon surrounded by the stars and was seated on the beautiful lion-throne studded with precious gems. He wore a kirlita mukuta on his head and a long garland of forest flowers round his neck. He had in all his four arms samkha, cakra, gad a and padma having the complexion of a fresh cloud. He was quite charming and was adorned with all the ornaments studded with gems.

## \|\| 16.178 \|\|

*candanokṣitasarvāṅgaṃ bibhrataṃ kelipaṅkajam \|*  
*purato nṛtyagītaṃ ca paśyantaṃ sasmitaṃ mudā \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. All his limbs bore the sandal-paste. In one hand the lotus was held, the body of the lord was quite peaceful.

## \|\| 16.179-180 \|\|

*śāntaṃ sarasvatīkāntaṃ lakṣmīdhṛtapadāmbujam \|*  
*bhaktapradattatāmbūlaṃ bhuktavantaṃ suvāsitam \|\| 179 \|\|*

*gaṅgayā parayā bhaktyā sevitaṃ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|*  
*sarvaiśca stūyamānaṃ ca bhaktinamrātmakandharaiḥ \|\| 180 \|\|*

179-180. Lakshmi was engaged in serving at his feet. Lord Vishnu was chewing the betel offered to him by his devotee. Ganga was fanning with the white fly-whisk with devotion. The people present there were reciting his glory with devotion.

## \|\| 16.181 \|\|

*evaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā paripūrṇatamaṃ vibhum \|*  
*brahmādayaḥ surāḥ sarve praṇamya tuṣṭuvustadā \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. Reaching before such a great prosperious lord, Brahma and other gods started praising him.

## \|\| 16.182 \|\|

*pulakāṅkitasarvāṅgāḥ sāśrunetrāḥ sagadgadāḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā paramayā bhaktā bhītā namrātmakandharāḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. The hair of the bodies of all the gods stood on end. The eyes were flooded with tears and the voice was choked. All the devotees stood before him with devotion bowing their heads.

## \|\| 16.183 \|\|

*puṭāñjaliyuto bhūtvā vidhātā jagatāmapi \|*  
*vṛttāntaṃ kathayāmāsa vinayena hareḥ puraḥ \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. Thereafter, the lord of the universe was addressed by Brahma, the god of creation, with folded hands. He narrated the entire tale of the suffering of the gods.

## \|\| 16.184 \|\|

*haristadvacanaṃ śrutvā sarvajñaḥ sarvabhāvavit \|*  
*prahasyovāca brahmāṇaṃ rahasyaṃ ca manoharam \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. The omniscient lord Vishnu understood the feelings of all the gods and then smiled. Thereafter he spoke to Brahma a matter of secret.

## \|\| 16.185-186 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*śaṅkhacūḍasya vṛttāntaṃ sarvaṃ jānāmi padmaja \|*  
*madbhaktasya ca gopasya mahātejasvinaḥ purā \|\| 185 \|\|*

*surāḥ śṛṇuta tatsarvamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*golokasyaiva caritaṃ pāpaghnaṃ puṇyakāraṇam \|\| 186 \|\|*

185-186. Lord Vishnu said — О creator of the universe I am well-aware of the stoiy of Sarhkhacuda who was one of my great devotees and a glorious cowherd. О gods, I am narrating to you his earlier story which is one of the sacred stories of Goloka and removes the sins, creating merits at the same time. You please listen to it.

## \|\| 16.187-189 \|\|

*sudāmā nāma gopaśca pārṣadapravaro mama \|*  
*sa prāpa dānavīṃ yoniṃ rādhāśāpātsudāruṇāt \|\| 187 \|\|*

*tatraikadā'hamagamaṃ svālayādrāsamaṇḍalam \|*  
*vihāya māninīṃ rādhāṃ mama prāṇādhikāṃ parām \|\| 188 \|\|*

*sā māṃ virajayā sārddhaṃ vijñāya kiṃkarīmukhāt \|*  
*paścātkrudhā sā''jagāma māṃ dadarśa ca tatra ca \|\| 189 \|\|*

187-189. There was a cowherd named Sudama, who was the best of my courtiers. He had to be born in the form of a demon as a result of a terrific curse pronounced on him by Radha. Once I leaving my beloved, Radha in my abode, went to the dancing hall. At that point of time Radhika was enraged about the hearing of my association with Viraja. She saw both of us together.

## \|\| 16.190 \|\|

*virajāṃ ca nadīrūpāṃ māṃ jñātvā ca tirohitam \|*  
*punarjagāma sā ruṣṭā svālayaṃ sakhibhiḥ saha \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. But finding Viraja in the form of a river and myself disappearing from that place, the enraged Radhika went back to her abode.

## \|\| 16.191-193 \|\|

*māṃ dṛṣṭvā mandire devī sudāma sahitaṃ purā \|*  
*bhṛśaṃ māṃ bhartsayāmāsa maunībhūtaṃ ca susthiram \|\| 191 \|\|*

*tac tvā ca sumahāṃśca sudāmā tāṃ cukopa ha \|*  
*sa ca tāṃ bhartsayāmāsa kopena mama sannidhau \|\| 192 \|\|*

*tacchrutvā sā kopayuktā raktapaṅkajalocanā \|*  
*bahiṣkartuṃ cakārājñāṃ saṃtrastā mama saṃsadi \|\| 193 \|\|*

191-193. Thereafter, finding me in the house with Sudama, she started denouncing me but I remained quiet and peaceful. But my courtier Sudama could not tolerate her. He got enraged and denounced Radha in my presence. On hearing his words, the eyes of Radha became red with anger and she asked him to leave my court at once.

## \|\| 16.194 \|\|

*sakhīlakṣaṃ samuttasthau durvāraṃ tejasojjvalam \|*  
*bahiścakāra taṃ tūrṇaṃ jalpantaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. At once a group of lakh of my friends got up and turned out that cowherd from the court who was crying again and again.

## \|\| 16.195 \|\|

*sā ca tadvacanaṃ śrutvā samāruṣṭā śaśāpa tam \|*  
*yāhi re dānavīṃ yonimityevaṃ dāruṇaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. Thereafter, hearing his words, Radha spoke in anger these words, “O wicked one, you are condemned to the race of the demons.”

## \|\| 16.196 \|\|

*taṃ gacchantaṃ śapantaṃ ca rudantaṃ māṃ praṇamya ca \|*  
*vārayāmāsa sā tuṣṭā rudantī kṛpayā punaḥ \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. Thus having been cursed, he looked at me pathetically and left the place looking back at me. In the meantime Radha too was moved with his plight and getting some what satisfied, she intended to prevent him from leaving the place.

## \|\| 16.197-201 \|\|

*he vatsa tiṣṭha mā gaccha kva yāsīti punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*samuccāryya ca tatpaścājjagāma sā ca vismitā \|\| 197 \|\|*

*gopyaśca ruruduḥ sarvā gopāśceti suduḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*te sarve rādhikā cāpi tatpaścādbodhitā mayā \|\| 198 \|\|*

*āyāsyati kṣaṇārdhena kṛtvā śāpasya pālanam \|*  
*sudāmaṃstvamihāgacchetyuvāca sā nivāritā \|\| 199 \|\|*

*golokasya kṣaṇārddhena caikamanvantaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ jagatāṃ dhātarityevaṃ vacanaṃ dhruvam \|\| 200 \|\|*

*sa eva śaṃkhacūḍaśca punastatraiva yāsyati \|*  
*mahābaliṣṭho yogīśaḥ sarvamāyāviśāradaḥ \|\| 201 \|\|*

197-201. She said — “O son, you stop for a moment. Where are you going? Don't go.” She started repeating these words again and again. Soon after finding Radha so crying, the mind of all the cowherds and cowherdesses were filled with grief. Thereafter I pacified Radhika and all others, saying, “He will obey the command of the curse and return to this place in a moment but Radha continued saying, “O Sudama, you come here and don't leave the place.” О Brahmana, the protector of the universe, half a movement of a Goloka is equated with a manvantara on earth. О Brahman, this is happening as ordained earlier. Therefore, Samkhactida who is well-versed in all the illusions and possesses great prowess, beside being well-versed in the Yogic practices, shall revert to Goloka again.

## \|\| 16.202 \|\|

*mama śūlaṃ gṛhītvā ca śīghraṃ gacchata bhāratam \|*  
*śivaḥ karotu saṃhāraṃ mama śūlena rakṣasaḥ \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. Therefore, lord Shiva should go on earth with my trident and should kill him with it.

## \|\| 16.203 \|\|

*mamaiva kavacaṃ kaṇṭhe sarvamaṅgalamaṅgalam \|*  
*bibharti dānavaḥ śaśvatsaṃpāravijayī tataḥ \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. My kavacha is held by that demon in his neck which has made him always victorious on earth.

## \|\| 16.204-205 \|\|

*tatra brahmansthite kaṇṭhe na ko'pi hiṃsituṃ kṣamaḥ \|*  
*tadyāñcāṃ ca kariṣyāmi viprarūpo'hameva ca \|\| 204 \|\|*

*satītvabhaṅgastatpatnyā yatra kāle bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tatraiva kāle tanmṛtyuriti datto varastvayā \|\| 205 \|\|*

204-205. О Brahmana, till such time the kavacha is worn by him, no one on earth can kill him. Therefore I shall beg it from him in the fonn of an ascetic. The moment the chastity of his wife is broken he will be killed. You have also given him a boon accordingly.

## \|\| 16.206 \|\|

*tatpatnyāścodare vīryyamarpayiṣyāmi niścitam \|*  
*tatkṣaṇenaiva tanmṛtyurbhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. For this purpose I shall implant my semen in the womb of his wife and he will meet with his end at the same moment. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 16.207-208 \|\|

*paścātsā dehamutsṛjya bhaviṣyati priyā mama \|*  
*ityuktvā jagatāṃ nātho dadau śūlaṃ harāya ca \|\| 207 \|\|*

*śūlaṃ dattvā yayau śīghraṃ harirabhyantaraṃ mudā \|*  
*bhārataṃ ca yayurdevā brahmarudrapurogamāḥ \|\| 208 \|\|*

207-208. Thereafter shedding the form of a woman she would become a beloved of mine.” Thus speaking lord Vishnu handed over the trident delightfully to lord Shiva and returned to his abode. Thereafter making Shiva to lead the gods, he left the place. All the gods also reached the land of Bharatavarsa.

## Chapter 17

## \|\| 17.1 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*brahmā śivaṃ saṃniyojya saṃhāre dānavasya ca \|*  
*jagāma svālayaṃ tūrṇaṃ yathāsthānaṃ mahāmune \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narayana said — О great sage, Brahma after entrusting Shiva with the tasks of killing SamkhacOda, he himself went to his own abode.

## \|\| 17.2-3 \|\|

*candrabhāgānadītīre vaṭamūle manohare \|*  
*tatra tasthau mahādevo devanistārahetave \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dūtaṃ kṛtvā puṣpadantaṃ gandharveśvaramīpsitam \|*  
*śīghraṃ prasthāpayāmāsa śaṃkhacūḍāntikaṃ mudā \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Thereafter Shiva took his seat on the bank of the river Chandrabhaga with the resolve of uplifting the gods. He then sent Puspadanta the king of the Gandharvas as the messenger to Samkhaciida.

## \|\| 17.4 \|\|

*sa ceśvarājñayā śīghraṃ yayau tannagaraṃ varam \|*  
*mahendranagarotkṛṣṭaṃ kuberabhavanādhikam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the command of Shiva, the messenger moved towards that city, which was more beautiful than Amaravati the capital of Indra or the city of Kubera.

## \|\| 17.5-6 \|\|

*pañcayojanavistīrṇaṃ dairghye taddviguṇaṃ mune \|*  
*sphāṭikākāramaṇibhissamantātpariveṣṭitam \|*  
*saptabhiḥ parikhābhiśca durgamābhiḥ samanvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*jvaladagninibhairnityaṃ śobhitaṃ ratnakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*yuktaṃ ca vīthiśatakairmaṇivedisamanvitaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. О sage, the city was five yojana in width and ten yojanas in length. It was surrounded by crystal gems on all sides and had seven castles in it. It illuminated with studded gems and hundreds of lanes.

## \|\| 17.7-9 \|\|

*parito vaṇijāṃ saṃghairnānāvastuvirājitaiḥ \|*  
*sindūrākāramaṇibhirnirmitaiśca vicitritaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhūṣitaṃ bhūṣitairdivyairāśramaiḥ śatakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*gatvā dadarśa tanmadhye śaṅkhacūḍālayaṃ varam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*atīva valayākāraṃ yathā pūrṇendumaṇḍalam \|*  
*jvaladagniśikhābhiśca parikhābhiścatasṛbhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. There were the commercial establishments of Vaishyas scattered everywhere and were filled with commodities. It had a hundred crores of beautiful and astonishing buildings which emitted the lustre of rubies. Reaching there the messengers looked at such a type of gigantic buildings which were circular in shape and were shinning like fire flames and surrounded by four moat.

## \|\| 17.10-13 \|\|

*sudurgamaṃ ca śatrūṇāmanyeṣāṃ sugamaṃ sukham \|*  
*atyuccairgaganasparśyamaṇiprācīraveṣṭitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*rājitaṃ dvādaśadvārairdvārapālasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*ratnakṛtrimapadmāḍhyai ratnadarpaṇabhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*maṇīndrasārakhacitaiḥ śobhitaṃ lakṣamandiraiḥ \|*  
*śobhitaṃ ratnasopānai ratnastambhavirājitaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ratnacitrakapāṭādyaiḥ sadratnakalaśānvitaiḥ \|*  
*ratnendracitrarājībhiḥ sudīptābhirvirājitaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. It was beyond the access of the enemies but was quite pleasant for others. It was surrounded by high boundary walls. It had many gates guarded by the gate-keepers and the doors were painted with gems, lotuses and mirrors besides the precious gems. It had a lakh of temples in it. It had the steps made of gems, the pillars were studded with gems. The doors and gates were studded with gems. The best of the vases were studded with gems. Even the lotuses, the mirrors and the astonishing lines were decorated with gems, adding to the beauty of the place.

## \|\| 17.14-15 \|\|

*parito rakṣitaṃ śaśvaddānavaiḥ śatakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*divyāstradhāribhiḥ śūrairmahābalaparākramaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sundaraiśca suveṣaiśca nānālaṅkārabhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā puṣpadanto'pi varadvāraṃ dadarśa saḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Crores of Danvas were guarding the place holding divine weapons in their hands. They were quite brave, valorous and possessed great powers. They were also adorned with beautiful ornaments and clad in charming clothes. After looking at all of them, Puspadanta looked at the main gate.

## \|\| 17.16 \|\|

*dvāre niyuktaṃ puruṣaṃ śūlahastaṃ ca sasmitam \|*  
*tiṣṭhantaṃ piṅgalākṣaṃ ca tāmravarṇaṃ bhayaṅkaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The god of the gate was seated holding a trident in his hand and wearing a smile on his face. His eyes were pinkish and had a complexion of copper. He looked terrific in appearance.

## \|\| 17.17 \|\|

*kathayāmāsa vṛttāntaṃ jagāma tadanujñayā \|*  
*atikramya navadvāraṃ jagāmābhyantaraṃ puram \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Disclosing to him the cause of his arrival, Pus padanta entered into the palace with his permission. Thereafter crossing nine gates he reached the court.

## \|\| 17.18-19 \|\|

*na kaiścidvārito dūto dūtarūpeṇa tasya ca \|*  
*gatvā so'bhyantaraṃ dvāraṃ dvārapālamuvāca ha \|\| 18 \|\|*

*raṇasya sarvavṛttāntaṃ vijñāpayitumīśvaram \|*  
*sa ca taṃ kathayitvā ca dūtaṃ gantumuvāca ha \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Considering him to be a messenger, no one stopped him. Reaching the inner court, he conveyed to the gate-keeper the purpose of his arrival and whatever his lord had told him. After hearing the message the gate-keeper permitted him to enter.

## \|\| 17.20-21 \|\|

*sa gatvā śaṃkhacūḍaṃ taṃ dadarśa sumanoharam \|*  
*rāsamaṇḍalamadhyasthaṃ svarṇasiṃhāsanasthitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*maṇīndrakhacitaṃ citraṃ ratnadaṇḍasamanvitam \|*  
*ratnakṛtrimapuṣpaiśca praśastaṃ śobhitaṃ sadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Reaching inside, he saw the most beautiful Samkhacuda who was seated in his court together with all his courtiers on a lion throne studded with precious gems.

## \|\| 17.22-25 \|\|

*bhṛtyena hastavidhṛtaṃ svarṇacchatraṃ manoharam \|*  
*sevitaṃ pārṣadagaṇairvyajanaiḥ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*suveṣaṃ sundaraṃ ramyaṃ ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*mālyānulepanaṃ sūkṣmavastraṃ ca dadhataṃ mune \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dānavendraiḥ parivṛtaṃ suveṣaṃ ca trikoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*śatakoṭibhiranyaiśca bhramadbhiśśastradhāribhiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*evaṃbhūtaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṣpadantaḥ savismayaḥ \|*  
*uvāca raṇavṛttāntaṃ yaduktaṃ śaṅkareṇa ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. A golden umbrella with its rod was also studded with gems. Besides, artificial flowers were also studded in the umbrella. The white and glittering fly-whisks were held by the attendants and moved over Samkhacuda. He looked very beautiful because he was adorned with all kinds of ornaments. He wore a garland around his neck. His body was plastered with sandal-paste. He was clad in two fine garments and was surrounded by innumerable and famous demons, while the other demons guarded the place holding the weapons in their hands. Finding such a glorious Samkhacuda, Puspadanta was surprised. Thereafter he started narrating to him the tale of the battle as spoken to him by lord Shiva.

## \|\| 17.26 \|\|

*puṣpadanta uvāca \|*  
*rājendra śivadūto'haṃ puṣpadantābhidhaḥ prabho \|*  
*yaduktaṃ śaṅkareṇaiva tadbravīmi niśāmaya \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Puspadanta said — “O king, I am the messenger of lord Shiva and known by the name of Puspadanta. О lord, I am repeating to you whatever has been ordained by Shiva to be spoken to you. You kindly listen to me.

## \|\| 17.27 \|\|

*rājyaṃ dehi ca devānāmadhikāraṃ ca sāmpratam \|*  
*devāśca śaraṇāpannā deveśe śrīharau pare \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. You better return the rights and the kingdom of the gods because all the gods had reached the abode of Vishnu to take his refuge.

## \|\| 17.28 \|\|

*dattvā triśūlaṃ hariṇā tubhyaṃ prasthāpitaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*candrabhāgānadītīre vaṭamūle trilocanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He has handed over his trident to lord Shiva for killing you. Lord Shiva is turn in currently lodged on the bank of river Chandrabhaga under a banyan tree.

## \|\| 17.29 \|\|

*viṣayaṃ dehi teṣāṃ ca yuddhaṃ vā kuru niścitam \|*  
*gatvā vakṣyāmi kiṃ śambhuṃ tadbhavānvaktumarhati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You will, therefore, either return the kingdom of the gods to them or get ready for a battle. Now you tell me everything that I have to tell to lord Shiva on my return.”

## \|\| 17.30-31 \|\|

*dūtasya vacanaṃ śrutvā śaṅkhacūḍaḥ prahasya ca \|*  
*prabhāte hyāgamiṣyāmi tvaṃ ca gacchetyuvāca ha \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sa gatvovāca tūrṇaṃ taṃ vaṭamūlasthamīśvaram \|*  
*śaṅkhacūḍasya vacanaṃ tadīyaṃ yatparicchadam \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. On hearing the words of the messenger, Samkhacuda smiled and said: “I shall go there in the morning. You can go now”. On hearing this the messenger went back at once to lord Shiva and conveyed to him the message of Samkhacuda together with the news about his soldiers.

## \|\| 17.32-39 \|\|

*etasminnantare skanda ājagāma śivāntikam \|*  
*vīrabhadraśca nandī ca mahākālaḥ subhadrakaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*viśālākṣaśca bāṇaśca piṅgalākṣo vikampanaḥ \|*  
*virūpo vikṛtiścaiva maṇibhadraśca bāṣkalaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kapilākṣo dīrghadaṃṣṭro vikaṭastāmralocanaḥ \|*  
*kālaṅkaṭo balībhadraḥ kālajihvaḥ kuṭīcaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*balonmatto raṇaślāghī durjayo durgamastathā \|*  
*aṣṭau ca bhairavā raudrā rudrāścaikādaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 35\|\|*

*vasavo vāsavādyāśca ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*hutāśanaśca candraśca viśvakarmā'śvinau ca tau \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kuberaśca yamaścaiva jayanto nalakūbaraḥ \|*  
*vāyuśca varuṇaścaiva budho vai maṃgalastathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dharmaśca śanirīśānaḥ kāmadevaśca vīryyavān \|*  
*ugradaṃṣṭrā cogracaṇḍā koṭṭarī kaiṭabhī tathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*svayaṃ śatabhujā devī bhadrakālī bhayaṃkarī \|*  
*ratnendrarājakhacitavimānopari saṃsthitā \|\| 39 \|\|*

32-39. In the meantime, Karttikeya also reached with his army before Shiva. He was accompanied by Virabhadra, Nandi, Mahakala, Subhadra, Vishalaksa, Bana, Pingalaksa, Vikampana, Niriipa, Vikrti, Manibhadra, Vaskala, Kapilaksa, Dlrghadamstra, Vikata, Tamralocana, Kalankata, Ballbhadra, Kalajivha, Kuticara, Balonmatta, RanaslaghI, Durjaya, Durgama, eight horrible Bhairvas, eleven Rudras, eight Vasus, Vasava, twelve Adityas, Agni, the moon, Vishvakarma, Asvinlkumara, Kubera, Yama, Jayanta, NalakObara, Vayu, Vanina, Budha, Mangala, Dhanna, Isan, Saturn, the powerful god of love (Ramadeva), Ugradanstra, Ugrachanda, RottarT, Raitabhl, the hundred armed and terrific BhadrakalT. The great goddess was seated on a plane studded with the dust of gems.

## \|\| 17.40 \|\|

*raktavastraparīdhānā raktamālyānulepanā \|*  
*nṛtyantī ca hasantī ca gāyantī susvaraṃ mudā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. She was clad in red garments and a garland of the same colour, her body was plastered with red paste. She was dancing, laughing and singing in sweet tones.

## \|\| 17.41 \|\|

*abhayaṃ dadatī bhaktamabhayā sā bhayaṃ ripum \|*  
*bibhratī vikaṭāṃ jihvāṃ sulolāṃ yojanāyatām \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. She removed the fear of her devotees and was terrific for the enemies. The goddess had a terrific tongue which was a yojana in length.

## \|\| 17.42-43 \|\|

*kharparaṃ vartulākāraṃ gambhīraṃ yojanāyatam \|*  
*triśūlaṃ gaganasparśiṃ śaktiṃ vai yojanāyatām \|\| 42 \|\|*

*śaṃkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ śarāṃścāpaṃ bhayaṃkaram \|*  
*mudgaraṃ muśalaṃ vajraṃ khaḍgaṃ phalakamujjvalam \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Her hands were a yojana in length and she was holding a begging bowl which was wavering in shape. Her trident was almost touching the sky and her satoi was a yojana long. Her other attributes were a samkha, a cakra, a gada, a lotus, horrible bow, a club, a gada, vajra and a shining sword.

## \|\| 17.44-46 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavāstraṃ vāruṇāstramāgneyaṃ nāgapāśakam \|*  
*nārāyaṇāstraṃ brahmāstraṃ gāndharvaṃ gāruḍaṃ tathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*pārjanyaṃ vai pāśupataṃ jṛmbhaṇāstraṃ ca pārvatam \|*  
*māheśvarāstraṃ vāyavyaṃ daṇḍaṃ sammohanaṃ tathā \|*  
*nānāvidhānyāyudhāni divyāstraśatakaṃ param \|\| 45 \|\|*

*āgatya tatra tasthau sā yoginīnāṃ trikoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*sārddhaṃ vai ḍākinīnāṃ ca vikaṭānāṃ trikoṭibhiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. She also had Vaishnavastra, Vdrumstra, Agneyastra, Nagapasa, Ndrayanastra, Brahmastra, Gandharvastra, Garuda, Parjanya, Pasupata, Mahesavarastra, Jrmbhnastra, Parvata, Vayavya, Danda, Sammohanastra and hundreds of weapons which could never be infructuous. Besides she had a hundred divine weapons held by her and three crores of Yoginls and three crores of Dakinls supported her.

## \|\| 17.47-48 \|\|

*bhūtapretapiśācāśca kūṣmāṇḍabrahmarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*vetālāścaiva yakṣāśca rākṣasāścaiva kinnarāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tābhiścaiva saha skando natvā vai candraśekharam \|*  
*pituḥ pārśve sabhāyāṃ ca samuvāsa bhavājñayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Thus all the goblins, pretas, pisdeas, kds mandas, brahmaraksas, vetalas, yaksas, raks asas and kinnars also arrived there in the company of Rarttikeya who bowed in reverence to lord Shiva and all of them were seated beside him.

## \|\| 17.49 \|\|

*atha dūte gate tatra śaṃkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*uvāca tulasīṃ vārttāṃ gatvā'bhyantarameva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. After the return of the messenger, Samkhacuda went to the inner apartment and narrated to Tulasi everything about the messenger of Shiva.

## \|\| 17.50 \|\|

*raṇavārttāṃ ca sā śrutvā śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukā \|*  
*uvāca madhuraṃ sādhvī hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Learning about the battle, the throat, the lips and tongue of the damsel were dried up. She was pained at heart and then spoke to her husband in a sweet tone.

## \|\| 17.51 \|\|

*tulasyuvāca \|*  
*he prāṇanātha he bandho tiṣṭha me vakṣasi kṣaṇam \|*  
*he prāṇādhiṣṭhātṛdeva rakṣa me jīvanaṃ kṣaṇam \|\| 51\|\|*

51\. Tulasi said — О lord of my life, О closest of my relatives, you remain in my embrace for some time. You are lord of my life and protect my life for a moment.

## \|\| 17.52 \|\|

*bhuṃkṣva janmasu bhogyaṃ tadyadvai manasi vāṃchitam \|*  
*paśyāmi tvāṃ kṣaṇaṃ kiñcillocanābhyāṃ pipāsitā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Let me enjoy all the desired pleasures of my life and let me have a graceful look at you for some time.

## \|\| 17.53 \|\|

*āndolayanti prāṇā me mano dagdhaṃ ca santatam \|*  
*dussvapnaṃ ca mayā dṛṣṭaṃ cādyaiva carame niśi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Му mind is fluttering and burning at the same time. I have witnessed a horrible dream at the end of tonight.

## \|\| 17.54 \|\|

*tulasīvacanaṃ śrutvā bhuktvā pītvā nṛpeśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ prājño hitaṃ satyaṃ yathocitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On hearing these words of Tulasi, Samkhacuda the king of kings after finishing his meals, spoke truthful, beneficial and realistic words of her.

## \|\| 17.55 \|\|

*śaṅkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*kālena yojitaṃ sarvaṃ karma bhoganibandhane \|*  
*śubhaṃ harṣaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhayaṃ śokamamaṃgalam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Samkhacuda said — “The result of all the deeds is tied up in a cord of time. The auspices, pleasure, joy, pain, tear and grief besides harm or all influenced the time.

## \|\| 17.56 \|\|

*kāle bhavanti vṛkṣāśca śākhāvantaśca kālataḥ \|*  
*krameṇa puṣpavantaśca phalavantaśca kālataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A tree grows according to the time, in time its branches grow and in time it bears flowers and fruits.

## \|\| 17.57 \|\|

*teṣāṃ phalāni pakvāni prabhavantyeva kālataḥ \|*  
*te sarve phalinaḥ kāle kāle kālaṃ prayānti ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The time makes the fruits grow and ripen. With the passage of time, after bearing flowers and fruits, it meets with its end.

## \|\| 17.58 \|\|

*bhavanti kāle bhūtāni kāle kālaṃ prayānti ca \|*  
*kāle bhavanti viśvāni kāle naśyanti sundari \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. О beautiful one, similarly people are born under the influence of lime and are also destroyed by the influence of the same. The entire universe emerges under the influence of the time and it also gets destroyed by the influence of the same.

## \|\| 17.59 \|\|

*sraṣṭā ca kāle sṛjati pātā pāti ca kālataḥ \|*  
*saṃharttā saṃharetkāle saṃcaranti krameṇa te \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Under the influence of time Brahma indulges himself in creation, Vishnu preserves it and Rudra destroys the same under the influence of time. All of them perform their respective duties under the influence of time.

## \|\| 17.60 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāmīśvaraḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ \|*  
*sraṣṭā pātā ca saṃharttā sa kṛtsnāṃśena sarvadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Lord Krishna is beyond Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva besides the gods and the Prakriti and one of his amshas becomes the preserver of the universe.

## \|\| 17.61 \|\|

*kāle sa eva prakṛtiṃ nirmāya svecchayā prabhuḥ \|*  
*nirmāya prākṛtānsarvānviśvasthāṃśca carācarān \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The same lord under the influence of time creates the Prakriti and through Prakriti he creates all moveable and immovable things of the world.

## \|\| 17.62-63 \|\|

*ābrahmastaṃbaparyyantaṃ sarvaṃ kṛtrimameva ca \|*  
*pravadanti ca kālena naśyatyapi hi naśvaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

*bhaja satyaṃ paraṃ brahma rādheśaṃ triguṇātparam \|*  
*sarveśaṃ sarvarūpaṃ ca sarvātmānantamīśvarama \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Because of this all the space between my loka and Brahmaloka is considered to be artificial, they are created at times and are also destroyed in due course of time. Therefore, you adore the truthful, eternal Brahman, the lord of Radha who is beyond all the three gunas, the lord of everyone, the form of everyone, the soul of everyone, beyond measure and is the lord.

## \|\| 17.64 \|\|

*jalaṃ jalena sṛjati jalaṃ pāti jalena yaḥ \|*  
*harejjalaṃ jalenaiva taṃ kṛṣṇaṃ bhaja santatam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He creates a creature from a creature and also protects a creature from a creature. Then he puts an end to a creature by a creature. Therefore you should recite the name of lord Krishna alone.

## \|\| 17.65 \|\|

*yasyājñayā vāti vātaḥ śīghragāmī ca santatam \|*  
*yasyājñayā ca tapanastapatyeva yathākṣaṇam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The wind blows and is moved at great speed at the command of lord Krishna, at whose command the sun burns at mid-day.

## \|\| 17.66 \|\|

*yathākṣaṇaṃ varṣatīndro mṛtyuścarati jantuṣu \|*  
*yathākṣaṇaṃ dahatyagniścandro bhramati bhītavat \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Indra showers rain in time and death overpowers all creatures, the fire consumes everything and the moon getting terrified always moves.

## \|\| 17.67-68 \|\|

*mṛtyormūlaṃ kālamūlaṃ yamasya ca yamaṃ param \|*  
*sraṣṭāraṃ sraṣṭurapi ca pātuḥ pālakameva ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

*saṃharttāraṃ ca saṃhartustaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja \|*  
*ko bandhuścaiva keṣāṃ vā sarvabandhuṃ bhaja priye \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Therefore, О beloved one, Krishna happens to be the death for the death and for the time, the best controller of Yama, all-pervading, is creator of Brahma, is the preserver of the preserver and also the killer of the god of death. You therefore take refuge under such a lord Krishna. О beloved, who is the brother of whom in this universe? The one who is the brother of everyone you better adore him.

## \|\| 17.69-70 \|\|

*ahaṃ ko vā tvaṃ ca kā vā vidhinā yojitaḥ purā \|*  
*tvayā sārddhaṃ karmaṇā ca punastena viyojitaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*ajñānī kātaraḥ śoke vipattau ca na paṇḍitaḥ \|*  
*sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhramatyeva cakranemikrameṇa ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Look here, who was I and who were you but Brahma united both of us on the basis of our deeds and he is going to separate both of us again on the basis of our deeds. At the approaching of grief and misfortune a person with little knowledge feels helpless but an intellectual person does not feel like that because pleasure and pain have to be faced by a person in his life cycle like a wheel.

## \|\| 17.71 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ taṃ sarveśaṃ kāntaṃ prāpsyasi niścitam \|*  
*tapaḥ kṛtaṃ yadarthe ca purā badarikāśrame \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Therefore, you will surely achieve lord Krishna as your husband sometime or the other for whose sake you had performed severe austerities at Badrikasrama.

## \|\| 17.72 \|\|

*mayā tvaṃ tapasā labdhā brahmaṇaśca vareṇa hi \|*  
*harerarthe tava tapo hariṃ prāpsyasi kāmini \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. О beautiful one, I achieved you after performing tapas for Brahma but your tapas was for the lord and as such you are sure to achieve the lord.

## \|\| 17.73 \|\|

*vṛndāvane ca govindaṃ goloke tvaṃ labhiṣyasi \|*  
*ahaṃ yāsyāmi tallokaṃ tanuṃ tyaktvā ca dānavīm \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. You will meet lord Govinda at Vrindavana and Goloka. I also after shedding this body shall proceed to Goloka.

## \|\| 17.74 \|\|

*tatra drakṣyasi māṃ tvaṃ ca tvāṃ ca drakṣyāmi santatam \|*  
*āgamaṃ rādhikāśāpādbhārataṃ ca sudurlabham \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. You will meet me there and I will always be looking at you in Goloka. Both of us had reached the country of Bharata because of the curse of Radhika.

## \|\| 17.75-77 \|\|

*punaryāsyāmi tatraiva kaḥ śoko me śṛṇu priye \|*  
*tvaṃ hi dehaṃ parityajya divyarūpaṃ vidhāya ca \|\| 75 \|\|*

*tatkālaṃ prāpsyasi hariṃ mā kānte kātarā bhava \|*  
*ityuktvā ca dinānte ca tayā sārddhaṃ manohare \|\| 76 \|\|*

*suṣvāpa śobhane talpe puṣpacandanacarcite \|*  
*nānāprakāravibhave cacāra ratnamandire \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. О dear one, we shall have to go there again. Therefore, there appears to be no cause for grief. You will also achieve the abode of the great lord after discarding this body. Therefore, О beautiful one, don't get disgusted for nothing.” Thus speaking Sariikhacuda enjoyed the company of Tulasi in the divine bed decorated with flowers and sandal-paste. His bedroom was decorated with gems and all the articles of worldly pleasures were stored therein.

## \|\| 17.78-80 \|\|

*ratnapradīpasaṃyukte strīratnaṃ prāpya sundarīm \|*  
*nināya rajanīṃ rājā krīḍākautukamaṃgalaiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kṛtvā vakṣasi kāntāṃ tāṃ rudantīmatiduḥkhitām \|*  
*kṛśodarīṃ nirāhārāṃ nimagnāṃ śokasāgare \|\| 79 \|\|*

*punastāṃ bodhayāmāsa divyajñānena bodhavit \|*  
*purā kṛṣṇena yaddattaṃ bhāṇḍīre tattvamuttamam \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. Both of them spent the night together while the lamps of gems continued burning. The king Samkhacuda enjoyed various love-sports with Tulasi during the night. Thereafter Tulasi who was slender-waisted with an extremely painful heart remained without food and was engrossed in the deep ocean of grief. Samkhacuda embraced her affectionately and started imparting to her the divine knowledge which he had received in the earlier times from lord Krishna himself.

## \|\| 17.81 \|\|

*sa ca tasyai dadau tacca sarvaśokaharaṃ param \|*  
*jñānaṃ saṃprāpya sā devī prasannavadanekṣaṇā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. After receiving the divine knowledge the damsel was immensely pleased and her face and eyes felt delighted.

## \|\| 17.82 \|\|

*krīḍāṃ cakāra harṣeṇa sarvaṃ matvā'tinaśvaram \|*  
*tau dampatī ca krīḍārttau nimagnau sukhasāgare \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Considering everything to be perishable, the couple enjoyed love-sports and were drawn in supreme ecstasy.

## \|\| 17.83 \|\|

*pulakāṅkitasarvāṅgau mūrcchitau nirjane mune \|*  
*aṃgapratyaṃgasaṃyuktau suprītau suratotsukau \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. О sage, the hair of the bodies of both of them stood on end and for enjoying the conjugal pleasures both of them were united.

## \|\| 17.84-87 \|\|

*ekāṃgau ca tathā tau dvau cārddhanārīśvarau yathā \|*  
*prāṇeśvaraṃ ca tulasī mene prāṇādhikaṃ param \|\| 84 \|\|*

*prāṇādhikāṃ ca tāṃ mene rājā prāṇādhikeśvarīm \|*  
*tau sthitau sukhasuptau ca tantritau sundarau samau \|\| 85 \|\|*

*suveṣau sukhasambhogādaceṣṭau sumanoharau \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ sacetanau tau ca kathayantau rasāśrayām \|*  
*kathāṃ manoharāṃ divyāṃ hasantau ca kṣaṇaṃ punaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*bhuktavantau ca tāmbūlaṃ pradataṃ ca parasparam \|\| 87 \|\|*

84-87. Both of them became one like Ardhanarlsvara Shiva. At that point of time Tulasi considered his beloved to be more important than her own life and the king Samkhacuda felt in the same way. Both of them slept delightfully. Both of them looked fine in sleep. Both of them were clad in the best of costumes. Both of them looked pleasant after enjoying the company of each other. They regained consciousness after a moment and narrated a divine story to each other. Simultaneously they were chewing the betels offered by each other.

## \|\| 17.88-90 \|\|

*parasparaṃ sevitau ca suprītyā śvetacāmaraiḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ śayānau sānandau vasantau ca kṣaṇaṃ punaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*kṣaṇaṃ keliniyuktau ca rasabhāvasamanvitau \|*  
*suratādviratirnāsti tau tadviṣayapaṇḍitau \|\| 89 \|\|*

*satataṃ jayayuktau dvau kṣaṇaṃ naiva parājitau \|\| 90 \|\|*

88-90. They were moving white fly whisks over each other. In a moment they lay down together and in the next moment, they sat up and in another moment they behaved passionately. Thus both of them who were well-versed in the love-sports could never get fully satisfied. Both of them were always victorious and never felt defeated.

## Chapter 18

## \|\| 18.1-2 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇaṃ manasā dhyātvā rājā kṛṣṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*brāhme muhūrtte cotthāya puṣpatalpānmanoharāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*rātrivāsaḥ parityajya snātvā maṅgalavāriṇā \|*  
*dhaute ca vāsasī dhṛtvā kṛtvā tilakamujjvalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Shri Narayana said — Samkhacuda the devotee of lord Krishna got up in the early morning and with his mind devoted towards lord Krishna, he left the bed. He discarded the sleeping clothes and took a bath with sweet water and clad himself in two washed clothes.

## \|\| 18.3-7 \|\|

*cakārāhnikamāvaśyamabhīṣṭaguruvandanam \|*  
*dadhyājyaṃ madhu lājāṃśca so'paśyadvastu maṅgalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ratnaśreṣṭhaṃ maṇiśreṣṭhaṃ vastraśreṣṭhaṃ ca kāñcanam \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyo dadau bhaktyā yathānityaṃ ca nārada \|\| 4 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnaṃ yatkiñcinmuktāmāṇikyahīrakam \|*  
*dadau viprāya gurave yātrāmaṅgalahetave \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gajaratnaṃ cāśvaratnaṃ dhenuratnaṃ manoharam \|*  
*dadau sarvaṃ daridrāya viprārthaṃ maṅgalāya ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kośāgārasahasraṃ ca nagarāṇāṃ trilakṣakam \|*  
*grāmāṇāṃ śatakoṭiṃ ca brāhmaṇebhyo dadau mudā \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. О Narada, he relieved himself of all the morning routines, bowing himself to his family gods and the teacher and had a look at curd, ghee, honey, fried rice and other things of bodily welfare. He then gave away in charity the best of gems, clothes and gold with devotion. Thereafter, for performing a peaceful journey, he offered invaluable gems, jewels, articles made of gem and ruby to the Brahmanas and the teacher. Again for the purpose of welfare he gave away in charity the best of the elements, horses, cows to the needy Brahmanas. He then distributed a thousand of his treasures, three lakhs of cities and a hundred crores of the villages to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 18.8-9 \|\|

*putraṃ kṛtvā ca rājendraṃ sucandraṃ dānaveṣu ca \|*  
*putre samarpya bhāryāṃ ca rājyaṃ vai sarvasampadam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*prajānucarasaṃghaṃ ca kośaughaṃ vāhanādikam \|*  
*svayaṃ sannāhayuktaśca dhanuṣpāṇirbabhūva ha \|\| 9 \|\|*
