8-9. He collected all the soldiers, three lakhs of horses, five lakhs of elephants, ten thousand chariots, three crores of archers, three crores of warriors holding swords and shields. Three crores of trident bearers accompanied him.

## \|\| 18.10-11 \|\|

*bhṛtyadvārā krameṇaiva sa cakre sainyasaṃcayam \|*  
*aśvānāṃ ca trilakṣeṇa pañcalakṣeṇa hastinām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*rathānāmayutenaiva dhānuṣkāṇāṃ trikoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*trikoṭibhiścarmiṇāṃ ca śūlināṃ ca trikoṭibhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. О Narada, thus the king of the demons commissioned a vast army, the commander of which was well-versed in the science of archery and battle field. Only such of the warriors could be considered as the chief charioteers as could be the best in the driving of the chariot. The king Samkhaciida placed the vast army under the charge of the commander accompanied with thirty Aksauhinl, war-bands; he marched ahead reciting the name of Hari, from his kingdom.

## \|\| 18.12-14 \|\|

*kṛtā senā'parimitā dānavendreṇa nārada \|*  
*yasyāṃ senāpatiścaiva yuddhaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mahārathaḥ sa vijñeyo rathināṃ pravaro raṇe \|*  
*trilakṣākṣauhiṇī senāpatiṃ kṛtvā narādhipaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*triṃśadakṣauhiṇīvādyabhāṇḍaughaṃ ca cakāra saḥ \|*  
*bahirbabhūva śibirānmanasā śrīhariṃ smaran \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Не declared his son Suchandra as the king of the demon and handed over to his son the care of his own wife, the kingdom, entire wealthy the people, the servants, the treasures, the vehicles and everything else. He himself wore a kavacha, holding a bow. and arrow in his hands.

## \|\| 18.15-16 \|\|

*ratnendrasārakhacitaṃ vimānaṃ hyāruroha saḥ \|*  
*guruvargānpuraskṛtya prayayau śaṅkarāntikam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*puṣpabhadrānadītīre yatrākṣayavaṭaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*siddhāśramaṃ ca siddhānāṃ siddhikṣetraṃ ca nāmataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. He seated his teachers ahead of him in the plane and started to reach immediately lord Shiva. There is an eternal banyan tree on the bank of the Puspabhadra river, where a large number of the abodes of siddhas are available. As a result of this the place is known by the name of Siddhasrama.

## \|\| 18.17-18 \|\|

*kapilasya tapasthānaṃ puṇyakṣetraṃ ca bhārate \|*  
*paścimodadhipūrve ca malayasya ca paścime \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śrīśailottarabhāge ca gandhamādanadakṣiṇe \|*  
*pañcayojanavistīrṇā dairghye śataguṇā tathā \|*  
*śāśvatī jalapūrṇā ca puṣpabhadrānadī śubhā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. In the country of Bharata the place is known as the abode of sage Kapila. It is located between the western sea and the Malaya mountain. It is located to the north of Shri Saila mountain and Gandhamadana mountain on the south, spreading over to five yojanas in width and five hundred yojanas in length, where the Puspabhadra river flows which is always filled with water.

## \|\| 18.19-21 \|\|

*lavaṇodapriyā bhāryyā śaśvatsaubhāgyasaṃyutā \|*  
*śuddhasphaṭikasaṅkāśā bhārate ca supuṇyadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śarāvatīmiśritā ca nirgatā sā himālayāt \|*  
*gomantaṃ vāmataḥ kṛtvā praviṣṭā paścimodadhau \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tatra gatvā śaṃkhacūḍo luloke candraśekharam \|*  
*vaṭamūle samāsīnaṃ sūryyakoṭisamaprabham \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. She happens to be the spouse of the salty ocean. It is always filled with virtues and is quite meritorious of the land of Bharatavarsa and shines like the a crystal stone. It emerges from the Himalaya and after crossing some distance, a river named Sarasvati falls into it. Flowing to the left of the Gomanta, mountain it proceeds towards three oceans. Reaching there, she has an audience with Chandras'ekhara Shiva the lord of Samkhacuda who always remains meditating, having the lustre of crores of suns seated under a banyan tree.

## \|\| 18.22-29 \|\|

*kṛtvā yogāsane sthitvā mudrāyuktaṃ ca sasmitam \|*  
*śuddhasphaṭika saṅkāśaṃ jvalantaṃ brahmatejasā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*triśūlapaṭṭiśadharaṃ vyāghracarmāmbaraṃ varam \|*  
*taptakāñcanavarṇābhaṃ jaṭājālaṃ ca bibhratam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*trinetraṃ pañcavaktraṃ ca nāgayajñopavītinam \|*  
*mṛtyuñjayaṃ kālamṛtyuṃ viśvamṛtyukaraṃ param \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bhaktamṛtyuharaṃ śāntaṃ gaurīkāntaṃ manoramam \|*  
*tapasāṃ phaladātāraṃ dātāraṃ sarvasampadām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*āśutoṣaṃ prasannāsyaṃ bhaktānugrahakārakam \|*  
*viśvanāthaṃ viśvarūpaṃ viśvabījaṃ ca viśvajam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*viśvambharaṃ viśvavaraṃ viśvasaṃhārakāraṇam \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ kāraṇānāṃ ca narakārṇavatāraṇam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*jñānapradaṃ jñānabījaṃ jñānānandaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*avaruhya vimānācca sa dṛṣṭvā dānaveśvaraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sarvaiḥ sārddhaṃ bhaktiyuktaḥ śirasā praṇanāma saḥ \|*  
*vāmato bhadrakālīṃ ca skandaṃ tatpurataḥ sthitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

22-29. He was seated in yogasana, displaying vara and abhaya mudras in his hands, wearing a smile on his face emitting the divine lustre. His limbs always remain shining like crystal gems and he holds a trident and a pattisa in his hands clad in tiger skin. The lord is dear to goddess Gauri and looked quite beautifi.il. His body is peaceful and removes all danger of death from his devotees. His natural instinct is to provide the fruits of the tapas and to fill the treasures of his devotees. He gets easily pleased. He never feels sad and bestows his grace on his devotees also. He is called the lord of the universe, the seed of the universe, the form of the universe, Vishvaja, one who feeds the universe, Vishvavara and the destroyer of the universe. He is the cause of the causes and is quite competent to rescue one from the hell. He is the eternal lord, the bestower of knowledge and all knowledgeable. Samkhacuda the king of the demons got down from his plane and had an audience with him. He along with the others stood before lord Shiva and bowed in reverence to him. The goddess Bhadrakali appeared on his left and Skanda was seated in front of him.

## \|\| 18.30-32 \|\|

*āśiṣaṃ ca dadau tasmai kālī skandaśca śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*uttasthurdānavaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve nandīśvarādayaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*parasparaṃ ca sambhāṣāṃ te cakustatra sāmpratam \|*  
*rājā kṛtvā ca sambhāṣāmuvāsa śivasannidhau \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prasannātmā mahādevo bhagavāṃstamuvāca ha \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. He was blessed by Kali, Skanda and Shiva while Nandlsvara and others welcomed him. Looking at the demon king all the people conversed quietly among themselves. Thereafter the demon king took his seat in.front of lord Shiva. Thereafter lord Shiva delightfully spoke to him.

## \|\| 18.33-35 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*vidhātā jagatāṃ brahmā pitā dharmasya dharmavit \|*  
*marīcistasya putraśca vaiṣṇavaścāpi dhārmikaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kaśyapaścāpi tatputro dharmiṣṭhaśca prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*dakṣaḥ prītyā dadau tasmai bhaktyā kanyāstrayodaśa \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tāsvekā ca danuḥ sādhvī tatsaubhāgyena varddhitā \|*  
*catvāriṃśaddanoḥ putrā dānavāstejasojjvalāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Lord Shiva said — Brahma happens to be the creator of the universe, is well-versed in dharma besides being the father of Dharma. He had a religious-minded son named Marlci. Marlci had a son named Kashyapa. Daksha married his thirteen daughters to Kashyapa. One of them is known by the name of Danu who had been quite chaste. In due course of time Danu gave birth to forty demon sons who were quite valorous.

## \|\| 18.36-38 \|\|

*teṣveko vipracittiśca mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*tatputro dhārmiko dambho viṣṇubhakto jitendriyaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*jajāpa paramaṃ mantraṃ puṣkare lakṣavatsaram \|*  
*śukācāryyaṃ guruṃ kṛtvā kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tadā tvāṃ tanayaṃ prāpa paraṃ kṛṣṇaparāyaṇam \|*  
*purā tvaṃ pārṣado gopo gopeṣvaṣṭasu dhārmikaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. The great warrior Vipracitti happens to be one of the Danavas. He had a son named Dambha who was quite religious-minded, self-controlled and a devotee of Vishnu. He under the guidance of his teacher Sukracarya performed tapas at Pus kara for a lakh of years by reciting the mantra of lord Krishna. You were therefore born to him as a son and are devoted to lord Krishna. In your earlier life you were the courtier of lord Krishna and quite a religious cowherd. You had earned great glory among the cowherds.

## \|\| 18.39-40 \|\|

*adhunā rādhikāśāpādbhārate dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*ābrahmastambaparyantaṃ bhramaṃ mene ca vaiṣṇavaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sālokyasārṣṭisārūpyasāmīpyaikyaṃ harerapi \|*  
*dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇanti vaiṣṇavāḥ sevanaṃ vinā \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Thereafter, you were cursed by Radhika and had to be born on earth at the Vaishnava Danava. The Vaishnavas consider the lokas between the earth and the Brahmaloka to be of no consequence, except for the only devotion of the lord they do not consider any other type of salvation to be of no consequence.

## \|\| 18.41-45 \|\|

*brahmatvamamaratvaṃ vā tucchaṃ mene ca vaiṣṇavaḥ \|*  
*indratvaṃ vā kuberatvaṃ na mene gaṇanāsu ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇabhaktasya te kiṃ vā devānāṃ viṣaye bhrame \|*  
*dehi rājyaṃ ca devānāṃ matprītiṃ kuru bhūmipa \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sukhaṃ svarājye tvaṃ tiṣṭha devāssantu svake pade \|*  
*alaṃ bhrātṛvirodhena sarve kaśyapavaṃśajāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*yāni kāni ca pāpāni brahmahatyādikāni ca \|*  
*jñātidrohasya pāpasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 44 \|\|*

*svasampadāṃ ca hāniṃ ca yadi rājendra manyase \|*  
*sarvāvasthāsu samatā keṣāṃ yāti ca sarvadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

41-45. The Vaishnava people consider that to become Brahman or eternal is of no consequence. They care the least for the kingdom of Indra or Kubera. Therefore you are a devotee of lord Krishna. As such the kingship of the gods is like an illusion for you, how can you have any belief in that? You return the kingdom of the gods to them and please me. You enjoy your country with pleasure and let the god live in their own abodes, because you happen to be the sons of the same Kashyapa and as such it would not be proper to have a conflict between the two brothers. The sins of Brahmahatya and other horrible sins are of no consequence as compared to the sin committed to your own brother. О king of the kings, if you consider this to be a loss of your riches, then you just think with whom are these riches to remain forever?

## \|\| 18.46-47 \|\|

*brahmaṇaśca tirobhāvo laye prākṛtike sati \|*  
*āvirbhāvaḥ punastasya prabhavedīśvarecchayā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*jñānaṃ buddhiśca tapasā smṛtirlokasya niścitam \|*  
*karoti sṛṣṭiṃ jñānena sraṣṭā so'pi krameṇa ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. At the time of dissolution even Brahma has to disappear and by the grace of the god he reappears again. There is an increase in intelligence because of his tapas and he is adored in the universe because of the same. Thereafter Brahma with his divine knowledge creates the universe.

## \|\| 18.48-51 \|\|

*paripūrṇatamo dharmaḥ satye satyāśrayaḥ sadā \|*  
*so'pi tribhāgastretāyāṃ dvibhāgo dvāpare smṛtaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*ekabhāgaḥ kaleḥ pūrve taddhrāsaśca krameṇa ca \|*  
*kalāmātraṃ kaleḥ śeṣe kuhvāṃ candrakalā yathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*yādṛktejo ravergrīṣme na tādṛkśiśire punaḥ \|*  
*dine ca yādṛṅ madhyāhne sāyaṃprātarna tatsamam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*udayaṃ yāti kālena bālyatāṃ ca krameṇa ca \|*  
*prakāṇḍatāṃ ca tatpaścātkāle'staṃ punareva saḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

48-51. In the Satyayuga, dharma is all powerful and is always based on truth. In the Tretayuga only the three amsas of dharma remain, while in the Dvapara only two of them are to be seen. At the start of the age of kaliyuga, he is seen in one part only and it goes on declining gradually. Ultimately only a small ray of dharma remains on earth like the light of the moon on a moonless night. The lustre of the sun is never the same in the winter season as is found in the summer season. The position the sun achieves during the noon is not to be found during the morning or the evenings. The sun rises in due course of time, crosses infancy and then reaches the maximum height in the noon and ultimately it sets in the evening.

## \|\| 18.52-53 \|\|

*dine pracchannatāṃ yāti kāle vai durdine ghane \|*  
*rāhugraste kampitaśca punareva prasannatām \|\| 52 \|\|*

*paripūrṇatamaścandraḥ pūrṇimāyāṃ ca yādṛśaḥ \|*  
*tādṛśo na bhavennityaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti dinedine \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Because of the constant movement of the cycle of time, when one meets with misfortune, then it has to disappear even during the day, at the sight of Rahu. The sun gets terrified and then after some time, it reappears delightfully. Similarly the moon on the full-moon night appears in a complete form but cannot remain the same all throughout the night. He goes on reducing itself gradually.

## \|\| 18.54-55 \|\|

*punaḥ sa puṣṭatāṃ yāti parakuhvā dinedine \|*  
*sampadyuktaḥ śuklapakṣe kṛṣṇe mlānaśca yakṣmaṇā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*rāhugraste dine mlāno durdine nibiḍe ghane \|*  
*kāle candro bhavecchuddho bhraṣṭaśrīḥ kālabhedake \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Thereafter by gradually increasing it appears in its full and complete form. Therefore the people during the bright fortnight get nourishment while during the dark fortnight, they are infested with diseases. Thus having been eclipsed by Rahu and having been covered by the cloud, both the sun and the moon lose their pristine glory and after the passage of time, the moon gets purified. Again in the course of time its glory again subsides.

## \|\| 18.56-60 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati baliścendro bhraṣṭaśrīḥ sutale'dhunā \|*  
*kālena pṛthvī sasyāḍhyā sarvādhārā vasundharā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kāle jale nimagnā sā tirobhūtā vipadgatā \|*  
*kāle naśyanti viśvāni prabhavantyeva kālataḥ \|\| 57\|\|*

*carācarāśca kālena naśyanti prabhavanti ca \|*  
*īśvarasyaiva samatā kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ahaṃ mṛtyuñjayo yasmādasaṃkhyaṃ prākṛtaṃ layam \|*  
*adṛśyaṃ cāpi paśyāmi vāraṃ vāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sa ca prakṛtirūpaśca sa eva puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa cātmā sarvajīvaśca nānārūpadharaḥ paraḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

56-60. Look, currently Bali is living in the nether world losing all his glory and in due course of time he would become Indra. The earth which happens to be the base of all, is filled with greenery in due course of time and eventually it gets submerged in water and in misfortune she disappears also. Thus the entire universe is destroyed in due course of time and it re-emerges. All the moveable or immovable things appear and disappear according to the time. Only lord Krishna remains eternal at all the times. I am the one, who has over powered the death, therefore I have witnessed innumerable dissolutions. I have also witnessed its disappearance again and again. The same lord Krishna happens to be the form of Prakriti and Purusa, soul and the great-soul. He takes to many forms and is the best of all.

## \|\| 18.61 \|\|

*karoti satataṃ yo hi tannāmaguṇakīrttanam \|*  
*kālaṃ mṛtyuṃ sa jayati janma rogaṃ jarāṃ bhayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The one who recites his name always with devotion, overpowers the time, the death, birth, disease, old age and danger.

## \|\| 18.62 \|\|

*sraṣṭā kṛto vidhistena pātā viṣṇuḥ kṛto bhave \|*  
*ahaṃ kṛtaśca saṃharttā vayaṃ viṣayiṇo yataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Brahma happens to be the creator of universe while Vishnu happens to be the preserver and I myself become the destroyer because all of us appear in material form.

## \|\| 18.63 \|\|

*kālāgnirudraṃ saṃhāre niyujya viṣaye nṛpa \|*  
*ahaṃ karomi satataṃ tannāmaguṇakīrttanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О king, Rudra named Kalagni, engages Rudra in destruction. He thus engages himself reciting the name of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 18.64 \|\|

*tena mṛtyuñjayo'haṃ ca jñānenānena nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*mṛtyurmatto bhayādyāti vainateyādivoragaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Because of that the death has no influence over me. The death flies away in panic from me as the serpents disappear in panic at the sight of Garuda.

## \|\| 18.65 \|\|

*ityuktvā sa ca sarveśaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*virarāmātha śarvaśca sabhāmadhye ca nārada \|\| 65\|\|*

65\. О Narada, lord Shiva who is compassionate to all and is the form of all besides being the lord of all, kept quiet after speaking these words.”

## \|\| 18.66 \|\|

*rājā tadvacanaṃ śrutvā praśaśaṃsa punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*uvāca suṃdaraṃ devaṃ paraṃ vinayapūrvakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On hearing these words, the king praised lord Shiva immensely and spoke to him in a sweet and beautiful voice.

## \|\| 18.67 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍa uvāca \|*  
*tvayā yatkathitaṃ nātha sarvaṃ satyaṃ ca nānṛtam \|*  
*tathā'pi kiñcidyatsatyaṃ śrūyatāṃ mannivedanam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Sarnkhacuda said — Though whatever you have spoken is completely true and there is no untruth in it, yet still I want to submit truthfully everything before you, you kindly listen to me.

## \|\| 18.68-69 \|\|

*jñātidrohe mahatpāpaṃ tvayoktamadhunā trayam \|*  
*gṛhītvā tasya sarvasvaṃ kutaḥ prasthāpito baliḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*mayā samuddhṛtaṃ sarvamaiśvaryyaṃ vikrameṇa ca \|*  
*sutalācca samuddhartuṃ nālaṃ so'pi gadādharaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. You have just now stated that there are three types of great sins in betraying one's race. Why did the gods drive out Bali after snatching his entire position. I have achieved these riches with the strength of my own prowess. I redeemed the riches of the earlier demon race. Lord Vishnu is also not in favour of the removal of the demon race from the earth.

## \|\| 18.70-71 \|\|

*sabhrātṛko hiraṇyākṣaḥ kathaṃ devaiśca hiṃsitaḥ \|*  
*śumbhādayaścāsurā vai kathaṃ devairnipātitāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*purā samudramathane pīyūṣaṃ bhakṣitaṃ suraiḥ \|*  
*kleśabhājo vayaṃ tatra taiḥ sarvaphalabhājanaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. Why did the gods kill Hiranyaksa together with his brothers? Why were the demons like Sumbha and others killed. Similarly in the earlier times when the ocean was churned and amrta emerged out of it, it was consumed totally by the gods. And the labour of churning the ocean was performed by the demons but the fruits were reaped by the gods alone.

## \|\| 18.72-73 \|\|

*krīḍābhāṇḍamidaṃ viśvaṃ kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*yadā dadāti yasmai sa tasyaiśvaryaṃ bhavettadā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*devadānavayorvādaḥ śaśvannaimittikaḥ sadā \|*  
*parājayo jayasteṣāṃ kāle'smākaṃ krameṇa ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. The entire universe is like the play ground of lord Krishna. He grants riches to someone at sometime and he becomes the lord of riches accordingly. The controversy between the gods and demons is eternal and therefore both of us had to face victory and defeat according to the times.

## \|\| 18.74-75 \|\|

*tatrāvayorvirodhe ca gamanaṃ niṣphalaṃ tava \|*  
*sama sambandhinorbandhvorīśvarasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*jāyate mahatī lajjā sparddhā'smābhiḥ sahādhunā \|*  
*tato'dhikā ca samare kīrtti hāniḥ parājaye \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. Therefore it is not proper for you to interfere in this conflict between the gods and the demons because you are the one who has the best of the relations with both of us and are adorable by us being a great lord. It will be a shameful thing for you to interfere in the conflict between two of us and still worse would be to get defeated in the battle field.

## \|\| 18.76 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍavacaḥ śrutvā prahasyāha trilocanaḥ \|*  
*yathocitaṃ sumadhuramatyugraṃ dānaveśvaram \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. On hearing the words of Samkhacuda, lord Shiva spoke to the kings of Danavas quite appropriate words thus.

## \|\| 18.77 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*yuṣmābhiḥ saha yuddhaṃ me brahmavaṃśasamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*kā lajjā mahatī rājannakīrtirvā parājaye \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Lord Mahadeva said — О king, you were born of the race of Brahma. In case I fight with you there will no loss of grace. Shall it be disgraceful to get defeated at your hands?

## \|\| 18.78 \|\|

*yuddhamādau harereva madhunā kaiṭabhena ca \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipoścaiva saha tenātmanā nṛpa \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. О king, the lord has already fought the battle with Madhu and Kaitabha who had also fought with Hiranyakasipu.

## \|\| 18.79 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣasya yuddhaṃ ca punastena gadābhṛtā \|*  
*tripuraiḥ saha yuddhaṃ ca mayā cāpi purā kṛtam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Again the mace-holder lord Vishnu had a fight with Hiranyaksa and in earlier times I had to fight with Tripura.

## \|\| 18.80 \|\|

*sarveśvaryyāḥ sarvamātuḥ prakṛtyāśca babhūva ha \|*  
*saha śumbhādibhiḥ pūrvaṃ samaraṃ paramādbhutam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. In earlier times the mother of all beings, the goddess Prakriti had to fight with Sumbha and other demons.

## \|\| 18.81-82 \|\|

*pārṣadapravarastvaṃ ca kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*ye ye hatāśca te daityā nahi ke'pi tvayā samāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*kā lajjā mahatī rājanmama yuddhe tvayā saha \|*  
*surāṇāṃ śaraṇasyaiva preṣitasya hareraho \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. You are also the best of the courtiers of lord Krishna and all the demons who were killed earlier can hardly be compared with your prowess. Therefore why would I be ashamed of getting engaged in a fight with you? It is the lord himself who happens to be the protector of the gods who had sent me to fight with you.

## \|\| 18.83-84 \|\|

*dehi rājyaṃ ca devānāṃ vāgvyaye kiṃ prayojanam \|*  
*yuddhaṃ mā kuru matsārddhamiti me niścitaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*ityuktvā śaṃkarastatra virarāma ca nārada \|*  
*uttasthau śaṃkhacūḍaśca svāmānyaiḥ saha satvaraḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. Therefore, I am of the firm opinion that you should not engage yourself in fight with me and will not enter into further controversies. О Narada, after speaking thus, Shiva kept quiet and Samkhacuda also got up at once with his courtiers.

## Chapter 19

## \|\| 19.1 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*śivaṃ praṇamya śirasā dānavendraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*samāruroha yānaṃ ca svāmātyaiḥ saha satvaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narayana said — The glorious king of demons named Samkhaciida bowed in reverence to lord Shiva, left the place together with his courtiers and boarded the plane.

## \|\| 19.2-4 \|\|

*babhūvuste ca saṃkṣubdhāḥ skandaśaktyā'rditāstadā \|*  
*nedurdundubhayaḥ svarge puṣpavṛṣṭirbabhūva ha \|\| 2 \|\|*

*skandasyopari tatraiva samare ca bhayaṅkare \|*  
*skandasya samaraṃ dṛṣṭvā mahadadbhutamulbaṇam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dānavānāṃ kṣayakaraṃ yathā prākṛtikaṃ layam \|*  
*rājā vimānamāruhya śaravarṣaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. The battle started between both the sides. The Danavas suffered Considerably with the prowess of Skanda. A commotion was created among them. On the other hand the drums were beaten in the heaven. In that terrific war the gods started showering flowers over Skanda. The war of Skanda was quite astonishing and terrific; it was proving to be destructive for the demons like the natural dissolution. Thereafter Saihkhacuda started showering arrows.

## \|\| 19.5 \|\|

*nṛpasya śaravṛṣṭiśca ghanavṛṣṭiryathā tathā \|*  
*mahānghorāndhakāraśca vahnyutthānaṃ babhūva ha \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The showering of arrows by the demon king appeared like the fall of rain which created darkness everywhere. Thereafter the fire appeared.

## \|\| 19.6 \|\|

*devāḥ pradudruvuścānye sarve nandīśvarādayaḥ \|*  
*ekākī kārttikeyastu tasthau samaramūrddhani \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All the gods including Nandlsvara fled away from the place in terror. Karttikeya alone continued to face the battle as before.

## \|\| 19.7 \|\|

*parvatānāṃ ca sarpāṇāṃ śilānāṃ śākhināṃ tathā \|*  
*śaśvaccakāra vṛṣṭiṃ ca durvāhyāṃ ca bhayaṅkarīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the battle field the mountains, the serpents, the rocks and the trees were continuously being showered in a horrible manner.

## \|\| 19.8 \|\|

*nṛpasya śaravṛṣṭyā ca pracchannaḥ śivanandanaḥ \|*  
*nīradena ca sāndreṇa saṃcchanno bhāskaro yathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Skanda appeared like the sun which is covered by the clouds and he became invisible with the showering of arrows by the demon king.

## \|\| 19.9 \|\|

*dhanusskandasya ciccheda durvahaṃ ca bhayaṅkaram \|*  
*babhañja ca rathaṃ divyaṃ ciccheda rathaghoṭakān \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The demon king then cut-off the horrible bow of Skanda held by him in his hand. He also shattered the divine chariot of Skanda, together with the horses of his chariot and charioteer.

## \|\| 19.10 \|\|

*mayūraṃ jarjjarībhūtaṃ divyāstreṇa cakāra saḥ \|*  
*śaktiṃ cikṣepa sūryyābhāṃ tasya vakṣovibhedinīm \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereafter Samkhacuda with the use of a divine weapon, injured the peacock of Skanda. With the intention of tearing out the chest of Skanda he shot a Sakti which had the lustre of the sun.

## \|\| 19.11 \|\|

*kṣaṇaṃ mūrchāṃ ca saṃprāpya cetanāmupalabhya saḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā'nyaddhanurdivyaṃ yaddattaṃ viṣṇunā purā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. With the attack of the Sakti, Skanda fainted for a moment. Thereafter he regained consciousness and again held another divine bow in his hand, which was handed over to him by lord Visnu in earlier times.

## \|\| 19.12 \|\|

*ratnendrasārakhacitaṃ yānamāruhya cāgnibhūḥ \|*  
*śastramastraṃ gṛhītvā ca cakāra raṇamulbaṇam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereafter Skanda mounted on another chariot which was built with the gist of gem. Skanda then equipped himself with all the weapons and started a great war.

## \|\| 19.13 \|\|

*sarpāṃśca parvatāṃścaiva vṛkṣāṃśca prastarāṃstathā \|*  
*sarvāṃściccheda kopena divyāstreṇa śivātmajaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Skanda the son of Shiva destroyed in anger all the snakes, the mountains, the trees and the rocks showered by the demons on him.

## \|\| 19.14-15 \|\|

*āgneyaṃ vāruṇāstreṇa vārayāmāsa vai guhaḥ \|*  
*rathaṃ dhanuśca ciccheda śaṃkhacūḍasya līlayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*savāhaṃ sārathiṃ caiva kirīṭaṃ mukuṭojjvalam \|*  
*cikṣepa śaktimulkābhāṃ dānavendrasya vakṣasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The fire weapon of Sarhkhacuda was neutralised by Skanda with his Varuna-weapon and simultaneously he destroyed his bow quite easily besides his chariot and the horses. Thereafter his charioteer, the horses and the kirit a crown were destroyed. This attack of Skanda appeared like the fall of a planet over the demon king.

## \|\| 19.16 \|\|

*mūrcchāṃ saṃprāpya rājopalabhya vai cetanāṃ punaḥ \|*  
*āruhya vai yānamanyaṃ dhanurjagrāha satvaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The demon king fainted with that attack. After regaining consciousness, he boarded another chariot holding a bow in his hand.

## \|\| 19.17-21 \|\|

*cakāra śarajālaṃ ca māyayā māyināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*guhaṃ cācchādya samare śarajālena nārada \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jagrāha śaktimavyarthāṃ śatasūryyasamaprabhām \|*  
*pralayāgniśikhārūpāṃ viṣṇorvai tejasā vṛtām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*iti śrī brahmavaivarte mahāpurāṇe dvitīye prakṛtikhaṇḍe nāradanārāyaṇasaṃvāde tulasyupākhyāne kālīśaṃkhacūḍayuddha ekonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*mūrcchāṃ saṃprāpa śaktyā ca kārttikeyo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*kālī gṛhītvā taṃ kroḍe nināya śivasannidhau \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śivastaṃ darśanādeva jīvayāmāsa līlayā \|*  
*dadau balamanantaṃ ca sa cottasthau pratāpavān \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. О Narada, SamkhacQda who was well-versed in the best of illusion covered Skanda in the battle field with the shooting of innumerable arrows. Thereafter he took up his invisible sakti which having the lustre of crores of suns and appeared like the fire of dissolution was also covered with the glory of lord Vishnu. He took out the Sakti in his hand and in anger he shot at Karttikeya with great force. The Sakti struck the body of Skanda like a burning fire. Karttikeya the great warrior fainted at this. Thereafter the goddess Kali picked him up in her lap and took him to lord Shiva. Lord Shiva on his part brought him back to life with a mere glance at him, restoring the immense strength possessed by him. The glorious Skanda got up at once thereafter.

## \|\| 19.22-25 \|\|

*śivaḥ svasainyaṃ devāṃśca prerayāmāsa satvaraḥ \|*  
*dānavendraiḥ sasainyaiśca yuddhārambho babhūva ha \|\| 22 \|\|*

*svayaṃ mahendro yuyudhe sārddhaṃ ca vṛṣaparvaṇā \|*  
*bhāskaro yuyudhe vipracittinā saha satvaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dambhena saha candraśca cakāra samaraṃ param \|*  
*kāleśvareṇa kālaśca gokarṇena hutāśanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kuberaḥ kālakeyena viśvakarmā mayena ca \|*  
*bhayaṅkareṇa mṛtyuśca saṃhāreṇa yamastathā \|\| 25\|\|*

22-25. Lord Shiva then deputed several of his soldiers and gods to fight with the demon king. The battle between the gods and the demon king again started with their armies. In the battle Vrsaparva fought with Mahendra, Vipracitti with Surya, Dambha with the moon, Kaleshvara with Kala, Gokarana with Agni, Kalakeya with Kubera, Maya with Vishvakarma, the terrific demon called Bhayankara with Mrtyu and Yama with Samhara.

## \|\| 19.26-30 \|\|

*kalaviṅkena varuṇaścañcalena samīraṇaḥ \|*  
*budhaśca dhṛtapuṣṭena raktākṣeṇa śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*jayanto ratnasāreṇa vasavo varcasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|*  
*aśvinau vai dīptimatā dhūmreṇa nalakūbaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dhanurddhareṇa dharmaśca maṇḍūkākṣeṇa maṅgalaḥ \|*  
*śobhākareṇaiveśānaḥ piṭhareṇa ca manmathaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ulkāmukhena dhūmreṇa khaṅgenāpi dhvajena ca \|*  
*kāṃcīmukhena piṇḍena dhūmreṇa saha nandinā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*viśvena ca palāśena cādityā yuyudhuḥ param \|*  
*ekādaśa mahārudrāścaikādaśa bhayaṅkaraiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

26-30. Similarly Kalavinka fought with Varuna, Cancala with Vayu, Ghrtapusta with Budha, Raktaksa with Saturn, Ratnasara with Jayanta, Varcasva with Vasus, Dlptiman with Asvini kumara, Dhumra with Nalakubara, Dhanurddhara with Dharma, Mandukaksa with Mars, Sobhakarana with Tsana, Pithara with the god of love and Ulkamukha, Dhumra, Khanga, Dhvaja, Kanclmukha, Pinda, Dhumra and Nandi with Vishvedeva, Palasa with Aditya and the eleven Rudras fought with eleven terrific Danavas.

## \|\| 19.31 \|\|

*mahāmārī ca yuyudhe cogradaṇḍādibhiḥ saha \|*  
*nandīśvarādayaḥ sarve dānavānāṃ gaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Ugradanda and others fought with Mahamar! (epidemic) and Nandi and others fought with other demon warriors.

## \|\| 19.32 \|\|

*yuyudhuśca mahadyuddhe pralaye ca bhayaṅkare \|*  
*vaṭamūle ca śambhuśca tasthau kālyā sutena ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In that terrific battle which had commenced only lord Shiva was seated under the banyan tree accompanied by Kali and Skanda.

## \|\| 19.33-36 \|\|

*sarve ca yuyudhuḥ sainyasamūhāḥ satataṃ mune \|*  
*ratnasiṃhāsane ramye koṭibhirdānavaiḥ saha \|\| 33 \|\|*

*uvāsa śaṃkhacūḍaśca ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*śaṅkarasya ca yodhāśca yuddhe sarve parājitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*devāśca dudruvuḥ sarve bhītāśca kṣatavikṣatāḥ \|*  
*cakāra kopaṃ skandaśca devebhyaścābhayaṃ dadau \|\| 35\|\|*

*balaṃ ca svagaṇānāṃ vai varddhayāmāsa tejasā \|*  
*svayamekaśca yuyudhe dānavānāṃ gaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. О sage, many of the warriors were engaged in the battle at that point of time, while Samkhacuda adorned with all the ornaments was seated on a gem-studded lion throne accompanied by crores of demons. In the battle field all the ganas of Shiva were defeated. Getting injured, all of them fled from the battle field in terror. Thereafter, Skanda felt enraged and challenged the demons, boosting the morale of his soldiers. He himself then proceeded alone to fight the demon in the battle field.

## \|\| 19.37-39 \|\|

*akṣauhiṇīnāṃ śatakaṃ samare sa jaghāna ha \|*  
*kharparaṃ pātayāmāsa kālī kamalalocanā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*papau raktaṃ dānavānāṃ kruddhā sā śatakharparam \|*  
*daśalakṣaṃ gajendrāṇāṃ śatalakṣaṃ ca vājinām \|\| 38 \|\|*

*samādāyaikahastena mukhe cikṣepa līlayā \|*  
*kabandhānāṃ sahasraṃ ca nanartta samare mune \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Skanda then destroyed a hundred alcsauhinJ demon army. The lotus-eyed Kali also got enraged and drank a hundred skulls full of the blood of demons and playfully held ten lakhs of elephants and a hundred lakhs of horses and playfully swallowed them all. Thus she consumed thousands of dead bodies and she then started dancing in the battle field.

## \|\| 19.40 \|\|

*skandasya śarajālena dānavāḥ kṣatavikṣatāḥ \|*  
*bhītāśca dudruvuḥ sarve mahābalaparākramāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. On the other.hand the demon warriors were badly" injured with the showering of the arrows by Skanda. The demon army fled in terror.

## \|\| 19.41 \|\|

*vṛṣaparvā vipracittirdambhaścāpi vikaṅkanaḥ \|*  
*skandena sārddhaṃ yuyudhuste ca sarve krameṇa ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All the great demon warriors like Vrsaparva, Vipracitti, Dambha and Vikankana fought a terrific battle with Skanda.

## \|\| 19.42-44 \|\|

*kālī jagāma samaramarakṣatkārttikaṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*vīrāstāmanujagmuśca te ca nandīśvarādayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sarve devāśca gandharvā yakṣarākṣasakinnarāḥ \|*  
*rājyabhāṇḍāśca bahuśaḥ śatakoṭirbalāhakāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sā ca gatvā ca saṃgrāmaṃ siṃhanādaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*devyā vai siṃhanādena prāpurmūrcchāṃ ca dānavāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. Shiva was protecting Karttikeya and Kali was engaged in the battle field. He was followed by Nandlsvara and several other great warriors. The gods, Gandharvas, Yaksas, Raksasas, Kinnaras besides many of the court jesters and crores of Balahakas were also there. The goddess uttered a lion's roar, reaching the battle field which made the demon army to lose their senses.

## \|\| 19.45-47 \|\|

*aṭṭāṭṭahāsamaśivaṃ cakāra ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭā papau ca mādhvīkaṃ nanartta raṇamūrddhani \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ugradaṃṣṭrā cogracaṇḍā kauṭṭarī ca papau madhu \|*  
*yoginīnāṃ ḍākinīnāṃ gaṇāḥ suragaṇādayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā kālīṃ śaṅkhacūḍaḥ śīghramājiṃ samāyayau \|*  
*dānavāśca bhayaṃ prāpū rājā tebhyo'bhayaṃ dadau \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. The goddess then uttered a terrific laughter and delightfully started drinking the wine, dancing in the battle field at the same time. Thereafter Ugradanstra, Ugrachanda and Kauttarl started consuming honey, besides the innumerable Yoginls, Dakinis. The ganas of Shiva and many other gods also participated in it. Finding Kali there Samkhacuda at once rushed to the battle field and started reassuring the panicky demons.

## \|\| 19.48 \|\|

*kālī cikṣepa cāgneyaṃ pralayāgniśikhopamam \|*  
*rājā nirvāpayāmāsa vāruṇena sa līlayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Kali then used the fire of dissolution.. The demon king on his part neutralised this by shooting a Varunastra.

## \|\| 19.49 \|\|

*cikṣepa vāruṇaṃ sā ca tattīvraṃ mahadadbhutam \|*  
*gāndharveṇa ca ciccheda dānavendraśca līlayā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The goddess then started using extremely sharp and astonishing type of arrows which destroyed the Gandharvastra and other weapons shot by the demon king.

## \|\| 19.50-56 \|\|

*māheśvaraṃ pracikṣepa kālī vahniśikhopamam \|*  
*rājā jaghāna tacchīghraṃ vaiṣṇavena ca līlayā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇāstraṃ sā devī cikṣipe mantrapūrvakam \|*  
*rājā nanāma taṃ dṛṣṭvā cāvaruhya rathādaho \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ūrdhvaṃ jagāma tacchastraṃ pralayāgniśikhopamam \|*  
*papāta śaṅkhacūḍaśca bhaktyā vai daṇḍavadbhuvi \|*  
*brahmāstraṃ sā ca cikṣepa yatnato mantrapūrvakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*brahmāstreṇa mahārāja nirvāṇaṃ ca cakāra ha \|*  
*cikṣepātīva divyāstraṃ sā devī mantrapūrvakam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*rājā divyāstrajālena nirvāṇaṃ ca cakāra ha \|*  
*devī cikṣepa śaktiṃ ca yatnato yojanāyatām \|\| 54 \|\|*

*rājā tīkṣṇāstrajālena śatakhaṇḍaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*jagrāha mantrapūrvaṃ ca devī pāśupataṃ ruṣā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*nikṣeptuṃ sā niṣiddhā ca vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī \|*  
*mṛtyuḥ pāśupate nāsti nṛpasya ca mahātmanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

50-56. The goddess Kali then used the Maheshvarastra which was like a fire flame. The king neutralised the same with the use of Vais navastra. The goddess then shot Narayanastra reciting the mantras. The king bowed in reverence before it and at once got down from the chariot. The weapon rushed like the fire of dissolution and reached before the demon king who in utter devotion prostrated before it on the ground. Thereafter the goddess with great efforts shot the Bralvnastra which was neutralised by the demon king by shooting another Brahmastra. The Goddess again used the divine weapon, which was neutralised by the demon king by shooting another divine weapon. The goddess then rpade use of Sakti which was a yojana in length. The king on the other hand broke it into a hundred pieces with the use his sharp weapons. The goddess getting enraged intended to use Pasupata weapon, but before she could do so, there was a divine voice from the sky warning her against its use saying, “The noble king cannot die with the use of Pas'upata weapon.

## \|\| 19.57-58 \|\|

*yāvadastyeva kaṇṭhe'sya kavacaṃ hi hareriti \|*  
*yāvatsatītvamastīha satyāśca nṛpayoṣitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tāvadasya jarā mṛtyurnāstīti brahmaṇo varaḥ \|*  
*ityākarṇya mahākālī na taccikṣepa sā satī \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. Till such time the kavacha of lord Vishnu was adorning his neck and his wife maintains her chastity, old age and death ban never influence the noble demon king. This is the boon granted to him by Brahma.” On hearing this the chaste Mahakall did not use the Pasupata weapon.

## \|\| 19.59 \|\|

*śatalakṣaṃ dānavānāmagrahīllīlayā krudhā \|*  
*attuṃ jagāma vegena śaṃkhacūḍaṃ bhayaṃkarī \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. But in anger she swallowed a hundred lakhs of demons. She then rushed towards Samkhaciida in order to swallow him.

## \|\| 19.60-61 \|\|

*divyāstreṇa sutīkṣṇena vārayāmāsa dānavaḥ \|*  
*khaṅgaṃ cikṣepa sā devī grīṣmasūryopamaṃ param \|\| 60 \|\|*

*divyāstrairdānavendro'yaṃ śatakhaṇḍaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*punarattuṃ mahādevī vegena ca jagāma tam \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. The demon king obstructed her forward movement by shooting a sharp divine arrow. The goddess then made use of her sword, which was shining like the sun of the summer season. The demon king reduced it into a hundred pieces with the use of his divine weapon. Thereafter Mahadevi rushed towards the demon king to swallow him.

## \|\| 19.62-65 \|\|

*sarvasiddheśvaraḥ śrīmānvavṛdhe dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*nivārayāmāsa ca tāṃ sarvasiddheśvaro varaḥ \|*  
*vegena muṣṭinā kālī kopayuktā bhayaṃkarī \|\| 62 \|\|*

*babhañjātha rathaṃ tasya cāhanatsārathiṃ satī \|*  
*sā ca śūlaṃ ca cikṣepa pralayāgniśikhopamam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*vāmahastena jagrāha śaṃkhacūḍaśca līlayā \|*  
*muṣṭyā jaghāna taṃ devī mahākopena vegataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*babhrāma vyathayā daityaḥ kṣaṇaṃ mūrcchāmavāpa ha \|*  
*kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya samuttasthau pratāpavān \|\| 65\|\|*

62-65. Thereafter Samkhacuda, the king of the demons who was bestowed with all success, started moving forward and because of the boon of Sarvasiddheshvara, defeated the goddess. The goddess Kali was again enraged and attacked him with her fist as a result of which the chariot and the charioteer of the demon king were shattered. The goddess then took up a trident in her hand which emitted flames like the fire of dissolution but the demon king Saifikhacuda playfully held it in his hand kept and it aside. At that point of time the goddess was immensely enraged and she attacked the demon king with her fist with great force. It struck heavily the demon king, who fell down on the ground unconscious. He regained consciousness in a moment and sat down in the battle field.

## \|\| 19.66 \|\|

*na cakre bāhuyuddhaṃ sa devyā saha nanāma tām \|*  
*devyāścāstraṃ ca ciccheda cāgrahītsvena tejasā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Inspite of that, the demon king never fought with the goddess and on the other hand he bowed in reverence to her. He caught the weapons of the goddess and also caught them in his hands with his prowess.

## \|\| 19.67-69 \|\|

*nāstraṃ cikṣepa tāṃ bhaktyā mātṛbuddhyā ca vaiṣṇavaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*gṛhītvā dānavaṃ devī bhrāmayitvā punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ ca prerayāmāsa mahāvegena kopataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ūrdhvātpapāta vegena śaṃkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*nipatya ca samuttasthau sa natvā bhadrakālikām \|\| 69 \|\|*

67-69. The great Vaishnava king of the demons bowed before her in reverence and never attacked her with any weapon. But the goddess caught hold of him in rage and moved him round and round throwing him in the sky with great force. The demon king, however, could save himself with the influence of his tapas and descending on earth he stood before the goddess Kali and bowed in reverence to her.

## \|\| 19.70 \|\|

*ratnendrasārakhacitaṃ vimānāgryaṃ manoharam \|*  
*āruroha rathaṃ hṛṣṭo na viśrānto mahāraṇe \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He then mounted his chariot which was built of the best of the gems and he never felt fatigued.

## \|\| 19.71-72 \|\|

*kṣatajaṃ dānavānāṃ ca māṃsaṃ ca vipulaṃ kṣudhā \|*  
*pītvā bhuktvā bhadrakālī yayau sā śaṃkarāntikam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*uvāca raṇavṛttāntaṃ paurvāparyyaṃ yathākramam \|*  
*śrutvā jahāsa śambhuśca dānavānāṃ vināśanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. Thereafter Bhadrakall consuming the flesh of the killed demons went back to lord Shiva. Reaching there, she narrated the entire story of the battle field which had happened there. Shiva then smiled on hearing the news about the destruction of the demons.

## \|\| 19.73 \|\|

*lakṣaṃ ca dānavendrāṇāmavaśiṣṭaṃ raṇe'dhunā \|*  
*udvṛttaṃ bhūbhṛtā sārddhaṃ tadanyaṃ bhuktamīśvara \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. She again said to Shiva, “О lord presently only a lakh of demons are left in the battle field who are devoted to the demon king. I have consumed the remaining demons. I have consumed the rest of them.

## \|\| 19.74-75 \|\|

*saṃgrāme dānavendraṃ ca hantuṃ pāśupatena vai \|*  
*avadhyastava rājeti vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī \|\| 74 \|\|*

*rājendraśca mahājñānī mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*na ca cikṣepa mayyastraṃ ciccheda mama sāyakam \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. In the battle field I intended to kill the demon king with the Pas'upata weapon but a divine voice from the sky was heard declaring that the death of the demon king is not destined at my hands. Thereafter the most intelligent, strong and valorous demon king never used any weapons against me. He only engaged himself in neutralising the weapons shot by me.

## Chapter 20

## \|\| 20.1 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*śivastattvaṃ samākarṇya tattvajñānaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*yayau svayaṃ ca samaraṃ svagaṇaiḥ saha nārada \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narayana said — О Narada, Shiva who is well-versed in the knowledge of tattva, leamt about the factual position from Bhadrakall and he went to the battle field himself.

## \|\| 20.2-3 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍaḥ śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimānādavaruhya ca \|*  
*nanāma parayā bhaktyā daṇḍavatpatito bhuvi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*taṃ praṇamya ca vegena vimānaṃ hyāruroha saḥ \|*  
*tūrṇaṃ cakāra sannāhaṃ dhanurjagrāha durvaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Finding Shiva approaching the battle field Samkhaciida descending, from the plane prostrated before Shiva, bowing in reverence to him. He at once mounted his chariot and alerted his demon soldiers. He then picked up his invisible bow.

## \|\| 20.4-6 \|\|

*śivadānavayoryuddhaṃ pūrṇamabdaṃ babhūva ha \|*  
*na vai babhūvaturbrahmaṃstayorjayaparājayau \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nyastaśastraśca bhagavānnyastaśastraśca dānavaḥ \|*  
*rathasthaḥ śaṃkhacūḍaśca vṛṣastho vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dānavānāṃ ca śatakamudvṛttaṃ ca babhūva ha \|*  
*raṇe ye mṛtāḥ śaṃbhorjīvayāmāsa tānvibhuḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. О Brahmana, the battle between Shiva and the demon continued for a year but no one could be victorious. Thereafter lord Shiva disowning his weapons stood there without them. The demon too stood there quietly. Thereafter Saihkhacuda mounted on his chariot and Shiva on his bull Nandi. The innumerable demons were killed in the battle field. Such of the soldiers of Shiva's army as were killed in the battle field were brought back to life by him.

## \|\| 20.7 \|\|

*tato viṣṇurmahāmāyo vṛddhabrāhmaṇarūpadhṛk \|*  
*āgatya ca raṇasthānamavocaddānaveśvaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereafter lord Vishnu taking to the form of an old Brahmana reached the battle field and said to the demon king.

## \|\| 20.8-10 \|\|

*vṛddhabrāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*dehi bhikṣāṃ ca rājendra mahyaṃ viprāya sāmpratam \|*  
*tvaṃ sarvasampadāṃ dātā yanme manasi vāñchitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nirāhārāya vṛddhāya tṛṣitāyāturāya ca \|*  
*paścāttvāṃ kathayiṣyāmi puraḥ satyaṃ ca kurviti \|\| 9 \|\|*

*omityuvāca rājendraḥ prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*kavacārthī janaścāhamityuvāca sa māyayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. The old Brahmana said — “О demon, king you give an old Brahmana the alms desired by him, since you are the possessor of immense riches and I have not eaten for many days. I am old, thirsty and am a helpless Bfflhmana. In case you give me a solemn promise that you will give away whatever is begged by me, only then shall I disclose the same. The delighted demon king Samkhaciida reciting '…’ promised to give him the desired things. Thereafter lord Vishnu said — “I am desirous of your kavacha".

## \|\| 20.11 \|\|

*tacchrutvā dānavaśreṣṭho dadau kavacamuttamam \|*  
*gṛhītvā kavacaṃ divyaṃ jagāma harireva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing this the best of the demons took out the kavacha and handed it over to the beggar who left the place at once.

## \|\| 20.12 \|\|

*śaṅkhacūḍasya rūpeṇa jagāma tulasīṃ prati \|*  
*gatvā tasyāṃ māyayā ca vīryyādhānaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereafter taking to the form of Saihkhacuda, Vishnu went to Tulasi and with an illusion implanted his seed into the womb of Tulasi.

## \|\| 20.13 \|\|

*atha śambhurhareḥ śūlaṃ dānavārthaṃ samagrahīt \|*  
*grīṣmamadhyāhnamārttaṇḍaśatakaprabhamujjvalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At that very moment lord Shiva took up his trident in order to destroy the demon king. The trident was shining like hundreds of suns at noon in summer.

## \|\| 20.14 \|\|

*nārāyaṇādhiṣṭhitāgraṃ brahmādhiṣṭhitamadhyamam \|*  
*śivādhiṣṭhitamūlaṃ ca kālādhiṣṭhitadhārakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Over the fore part of the trident resided Narayana, Brahma in the eentre and lord Shiva at the rear end. It had very sharp edges.

## \|\| 20.15 \|\|

*kiraṇāvalisaṃyuktaṃ pralayāgniśikhopamam \|*  
*durnivāryaṃ ca durdharṣamavyarthaṃ vairighātakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It had the lustre of the fire of dissolution and was terrific and could never be wasted. It was fatal for the enemies.

## \|\| 20.16 \|\|

*tejasā cakratulyaṃ ca sarvaśastravighātakam \|*  
*śivakeśavayoranyad durvahaṃ ca bhayaṃkaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Like the Sudarsana-cakra it possessed lustre and could penetrate all the weapons and except Shiva and Vishnu no one could handle it.

## \|\| 20.17 \|\|

*dhanussahasraṃ dairghyeṇa vistṛtyā śatahastakam \|*  
*sajīvaṃ brahmarūpaṃ ca nityarūpamanirmitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. It was as long as a thousand bows and was a hundred feet in width. It had the figure of Brahman itself. Its form could never change and it was of divine origin.

## \|\| 20.18-20 \|\|

*saṃhartuṃ sarvavidhyaṇḍamekadā daivalīlayā \|*  
*cikṣepa ghūrṇanaṃ kṛtvā śaṃkhacūḍe ca nārada \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rājā cāpaṃ parityajya śrīkṛṣṇacaraṇāmbujam \|*  
*dhyānaṃ cakāra bhaktyā ca kṛtvā yogāsanaṃ dhiyā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śūlaṃ ca bhramaṇaṃ kṛtvā nyapataddānavopari \|*  
*cakāra bhasmasāttaṃ ca sarathaṃ caiva līlayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. О Narada, the trident had the capacity to destroy the entire universe. Lord Shiva playfully held it and moved it round and round and then threw it at Sarhkhacuda. The intelligent demon king realised the entire secret of it and intelligently sat in Yogasana and devoted his mind to the lotus-like feet of lord Krishna. The trident after taking many rounds, ultimately fell on the demon king who was reduced to ashes together with his chariot and horses.

## \|\| 20.21-26 \|\|

*rājā dhṛtvā divyarūpaṃ bālakaṃ gopaveṣakam \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ muralīhastaṃ ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nānāratnasubhūṣāḍhyagopakoṭibhirāvṛtam \|*  
*golokādāgataṃ yānamāruhya tatpuraṃ yayau \|\| 22 \|\|*

*gatvā nanāma śirasā rādhāmādhavayormune \|*  
*bhaktyā taccaraṇāmbhojaṃ rāse vṛndāvane mune \|*  
*sudāmānaṃ tau ca dṛṣṭvā prasanna vadanekṣaṇau \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tadā ca cakratuḥ kroḍe snehena parisaṃplutau \|*  
*atha śūlaśca vegena prayayau śūlinaḥ karam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śaṅkarastena śūlena dānavasyāsthijālakam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*premṇā ca prerayāmāsa lavaṇode ca sāgare \|*  
*asthibhiḥ śaṃkhacūḍasya śaṃkhajātirbabhūva ha \|\| 26 \|\|*

21-26. Thereafter the demon king was turned into the form of a cowherd boy. He had two arms and held a flute in his hand. He was adorned with all the ornaments and was surrounded by crores of cowherds. He then mounted on the divine plane and went to Goloka. О sage, reaching Rasamandala in Goloka, he bowed in reverence at the lotus-like feet of Radha and Madhu. Thereafter he prostrated before them. Finding Sudama there both Radha and Krishna felt delighted. With their minds filled with love and affection, the lord lifted him up in his lap. On the other hand the trident shot by Shiva returned to his hand with great force. Lord Shiva then carried the bones of the demon king and consigned them to the ocean of salt water. From the bones several types of samkha emerged.

## \|\| 20.27 \|\|

*nānāprakārarūpā ca śreṣṭhā pūtā surārcane \|*  
*praśastaṃ śaṃkhatoyaṃ ca devānāṃ prītidaṃ param \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. These samkha which emerged in several forms were used for performing puja of the gods. The water of the samkha offered to the gods is immensely liked by them.

## \|\| 20.28 \|\|

*tīrthatoyasvarūpaṃ ca pavitraṃ śaṃkaraṃ vinā \|*  
*śaṃkhaśabdo bhavedyatra tatra lakṣmīśca susthirā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The water of the samkha is offered to all the gods except lord Shiva. Wherever the sound of the samkha echoes, the goddess Lakshmi resides there.

## \|\| 20.29 \|\|

*sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu yaḥ snātaḥ śaṃkhavāriṇā \|*  
*śaṃkhaṃ hareradhiṣṭhānaṃ yatra śaṃkhastato hariḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Whosoever takes a bath with the water of scunkha, earns the merit of having a bath in all the sacred places. Indeed satiikha represents lord Vishnu and wherever samkha lives, it becomes the abode of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 20.30-31 \|\|

*tatraiva satataṃ lakṣmīrdūrībhūtamamaṅgalam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*strīṇāṃ ca śaṃkhadhvanibhiḥ śūdrāṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*bhītā ruṣṭā yāti lakṣmīḥ sthalamanyaṃ sthalāttataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The goddess Lakshmi also resides there continuously and all the evils are removed, but the goddess Lakshmi is adverse to the blowing of the conches by the ladies as w^ell as the Sfldras and leaves the place at once.

## \|\| 20.32 \|\|

*śivaśca dānavaṃ hatvā śivalokaṃ jagāma saḥ \|*  
*prahṛṣṭo vṛṣamāruhya svagaṇaiśca samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thus with the killing of the demon king, Shiva was extremely pleased and mounting on his bull, he returned to his abode together with his ganas.

## \|\| 20.33 \|\|

*surāḥ svaviṣayaṃ prāpuḥ paramānandasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*nedurdundubhayaḥ svarge jagurgandharvakinnarāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The gods felt delighted at getting back their kingdoms. The sound of dundubhl echoed in the heavens. The Gandharvas and ICinnaras started singing and dancing.

## \|\| 20.34 \|\|

*babhūva puṣpavṛṣṭiśca śivasyopari santatam \|*  
*praśaśaṃsuḥ surāstaṃ ca munīndrapravarādayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The gods started showering flowers over Shiva. The gods and the sages immensely pleased lord Shiva.

## Chapter 21

## \|\| 21.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇaśca bhagavānvīryyādhānaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*tulasyā kena rūpeṇa tanme vyākhyātumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said — How did Narayana implant his seed into the womb of Tulasi, you kindly tell me?

## \|\| 21.2 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇaśca bhagavāndevānāṃ sādhanena ca \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍasya rūpeṇa reme tadrāmayā saha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Narayana said — Lord Narayana, for the benefice of the gods, took to the form of Samkhacflda and enjoyed the company of the damsel.

## \|\| 21.3-4 \|\|

*śaṃkhacūḍasya kavacaṃ gṛhītvā māyayā hariḥ \|*  
*punarvidhāya tadrūpaṃ jagāma tulasīgṛham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dundubhiṃ vādayāmāsa tulasīdvārasannidhau \|*  
*jayaśabdaravadvārā bodhayāmāsa sundarīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Vishnu on the other hand deceitfully took away the kavacha of Sarnkhacuda and taking to his fonn reached the abode of Tulasi. He arranged the drums to be beaten at the gate of the abode of Tulasi with the shouting of the slogans of victory. Tulasi was thus made to wake up.

## \|\| 21.5 \|\|

*tacchrutvā sā ca sādhvī ca paramānandasaṃyutā \|*  
*rājamārgagavākṣeṇa dadarśa paramādarāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hearing that her mind was filled with delight and with her mind filled with devotion she peeped through the window over the king's way.

## \|\| 21.6-7 \|\|

*brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṃ dattvā kārayāmāsa maṅgalam \|6 \|*  
*bandibhyo bhikṣukebhyaśca vācikebhyo dhanaṃ dadau \|\| 6 \|\|*

*avaruhya rathāddevo devyāśca bhavanaṃ yayau \|*  
*amūlyaratnasaṃklṛptaṃ sundaraṃ sumanoharam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Offering charity to the Brahmanas she awarded the beggars with enough riches. The king descended from the chariot and moved towards the palace which was studded with precious gems, was quite charming and beautiful.

## \|\| 21.8 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā ca purataḥ kāntaṃ śāntaṃ kāntā mudā'nvitā \|*  
*tatpādaṃ kṣālayāmāsa nanāma ca ruroda ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Finding her husband standing in a peaceful mood, the damsel felt delighted. She bowed in reverence to him and washed his feet. She made her tears to flow.

## \|\| 21.9-10 \|\|

*ratnasiṃhā sane ramye vāsayāmāsa kāmukī \|*  
*tāmbūlaṃ ca dadau tasmai karpūrādisuvāsitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*adya me saphalaṃ janma hyadya me saphalāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*raṇāgataṃ ca prāṇeśaṃ paśyantyāśca punargṛhe \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The damsel made him sit on the beautiful lion-throne and offered him a fragrant betel. She said — “My life is met with success today and all my efforts have borne fruit, because 1 find my lord coming as victorious from the battle field.

## \|\| 21.11 \|\|

*sasmitā sakaṭākṣaṃ ca sakāmā pulakāñcitā \|*  
*papraccha raṇavṛttāntaṃ kāntaṃ madhurayā girā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Therealter smilingly she looked at her lord with side glances with her hair standing on end. She spoke sweet words while asking about the news of the battle.

## \|\| 21.12 \|\|

*tulasyuvāca \|*  
*asaṃkhyaviśvasaṃhartrā sārddhamājau tava prabho \|*  
*kathaṃ babhūva vijayastanme brūhi kṛpānidhe \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Tulasi said — О lord, О compassionate one, how did you fight with lord Shiva who can destroy the entire universe? How did you become victorious? You please tell me.

## \|\| 21.13 \|\|

*tulasīvacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya kamalāpatiḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhacūḍasya rūpeṇa tāmuvācānṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On hearing the words of Tulasi lord Vishnu who had taken to the form of Sarhkhacuda smiled and said.

## \|\| 21.14 \|\|

*śrīhariruvāca \|*  
*āvayoḥ samaraṃ kānte pūrṇamabdaṃ babhūva ha \|*  
*nāśo babhūva sarveṣāṃ dānavānāṃ ca kāmini \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Lord Hari said — “O damsel, the battle between two of us continued for a year in which all the demons were destroyed.

## \|\| 21.15 \|\|

*prītiṃ ca kārayāmāsa brahmā ca svayamāvayoḥ \|*  
*devānāmadhikāraśca pradatto brahmaṇā purā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereafter, Brahma worked for a truce between us and the rights of both the sides were restored by him.

## \|\| 21.16 \|\|

*mayā''gataṃ svabhavanaṃ śivalokaṃ śivo gataḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā jagatāṃ nāthaḥ śayanaṃ ca cakāra ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereafter, I have returned to my abode and Shiva has returned to his abode. Thus speaking the lord of the universe slept there.

## \|\| 21.17 \|\|

*reme ramāpatistatra rāmayā saha nārada \|*  
*sā sādhvī sukhasambhogādākarṣaṇavyatikramāt \|*  
*sarvaṃ vitarkayāmāsa kastvamevetyuvāca ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О Narada, thereafter lord Vishnu enjoyed the company of the damsel. Tulasi felt more delighted than before and she ultimately came to know about the reality and said: “Who are you”?

## \|\| 21.18-21 \|\|

*tulasyuvāca \|*  
*ko vā tvaṃ vada māyeśo bhuktā'haṃ māyayā tvayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dūrīkṛtaṃ matsatītvamathavā tvāṃ śapāmahe \|*  
*tulasīvacanaṃ śrutvā hariḥ śāpabhayena ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dadhāra līlayā brahmansvāṃ mūrtiṃ sumanoharām \|*  
*dadarśa purato devī devadevaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*navīnanīrada śyāmaṃ śaratpaṅkajalocanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*koṭikandarpalīlābhaṃ ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*īṣaddhāsyaṃ prasannāsyaṃ śobhitaṃ pītavāsasā \|\| 21 \|\|*

18-21. Tulasi said — “Are you not the lord of illusion”? You tell me who you are? You have deceitfully enjoyed my company and have defiled my chastity. Therefore I shall pronounce a curse on you. О Brahmana, getting afraid of the curse of Tulasi, lord Vishnu playfully took to an extremely charming form. The queen saw that the lord of all the lords was standing before her who had the complexion of a new cloud, had the eyes like the lotuses of the winter season, had a beautiful body containing crores of gods of love, adorned with all ornaments, wearing a smile on his face and clad in a yellow lower garment.

## \|\| 21.22 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā kāminī kāmānmūrchāṃ saṃprāpa līlayā \|*  
*punaśca cetanāṃ prāpya punaḥ sā tamuvāca ha \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Finding him there, lustful Tulasi fainted with passion. On regaining consciousness she spoke.

## \|\| 21.23 \|\|

*he nātha te dayā nāsti pāṣāṇa sadṛśasya ca \|*  
*chalena dharmabhaṅgena mama svāmī tvayā hataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Tulasi said — О lord, you are heartless, having no compassion. You are hard like a stone. You have defiled my chastity deceitfully and have killed my husband.

## \|\| 21.24 \|\|

*pāṣāṇasadṛśastvaṃ ca dayāhīno yataḥ prabho \|*  
*tasmātpāṣāṇarūpa stvaṃ bhuvi deva bhavādhunā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О lord, therefore you are stone-hearted and devoid of compassion. You will therefore take the form of a stone on earth.

## \|\| 21.25-26 \|\|

*ye vadanti dayāsindhuṃ tvāṃ te bhrāntā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*bhakto vinā'parādhena parārthe ca kathaṃ hataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*durvṛttastvaṃ ca sarvajño na jānāsi paravyathām \|*  
*atastvamekajanuṣi svameva vismariṣyasi \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Those of the people who call you the ocean of mercy are misled. There is no doubt about it. Why did you kill your own sinless devotee who had committed no crime, for the sake of others? You are the soul of everyone still you are unaware of pain of others. Therefore in one of your births you will forget yourself.

## \|\| 21.27 \|\|

*ityuktvā ca mahāsādhvī nipatya caraṇe hareḥ \|*  
*bhṛśaṃ ruroda śokārttā vilalāpa muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus speaking the immensely chaste Tulasi fell at the feet of lord crying and was filled with grief lamenting again and again.

## \|\| 21.28 \|\|

*tasyāśca karuṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā karuṇāmayasāgaraḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇastāṃ bodhayitumuvāca kamalāpatiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The lord of Kamala finding her in a pathetic condition tried to assuage her feelings saying.

## \|\| 21.29 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*tapastvayā kṛtaṃ sādhvi madarthe bhārate ciram \|*  
*tvadarthe śaṅkhacūḍaśca cakāra suciraṃ tapaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The lord said — “O chaste lady, you have performed tapas in the land of Bharata for a long time to achieve me and on the other hand Samkhactida had performed tapas for a long time to achieve you.

## \|\| 21.30-31 \|\|

*kṛtvā tvāṃ kāminīṃ kāmī vijahāra ca tatphalāt \|*  
*adhunā dātumucitaṃ tavaiva tapasaḥ phalam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*idaṃ śarīraṃ tyaktvā ca divyaṃ dehaṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*rāse me ramayā sārddhaṃ tvaṃ ramāsadṛśī bhava \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. As a result of these tapas, the passionate Samkhacuda got you. Now I have considered it appropriate to award you the fruit of your tapas. Therefore putting an end to the present body you take to a divine form and come to Goloka in my Rasallla as Lakshmi in the company of lord Vis nu.

## \|\| 21.32-33 \|\|

*iyaṃ tanurnadīrūpā gaṇḍakīti ca viśrutā \|*  
*pūtā supuṇyadā nṛṇāṃ puṇyā bhavatu bhārate \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tava keśasamūhāśca puṇyavṛkṣā bhavantviti \|*  
*tulasīkeśasambhūtā tulasīti ca viśrutā \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Your body will now take to the form of GandakI river, which will be considered to be quite auspicious by the people. Besides your hair will become trees. Since the trees will be born of your hair they will be known by the name of Tulasi.

## \|\| 21.34 \|\|

*trilokeṣu ca puṣpāṇāṃ patrāṇāṃ devapūjane \|*  
*pradhānarūpā tulasī bhaviṣyati varānane \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О damsel, having the beautiful face, in all the three worlds the leaves of Tulasi would be considered to be the best and extremely meritorious as compared to any other leaves and flowers which are offered to the gods.

## \|\| 21.35-37 \|\|

*svarge martye ca pātāle vaikuṇṭhe mama sannidhau \|*  
*bhavantu tulasīvṛkṣā varāḥ puṣpeṣu sundari \|\| 35 \|\|*

*goloke virajātīre rāse vṛndāvane bhuvi \|*  
*bhāṇḍīre campakavane ramye candanakānane \|\| 36 \|\|*

*mādhavīketakīkundamallikāmālatīvane \|*  
*bhavantu taravastatra puṣpasthāneṣu puṇyadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. О beautiful one, the plant of Tulasi will always be considered to be the best of all the trees and flowers. The trees of sacred Tulasi will be grown in the heaven, the hell, the nether world, Vaikuntha, the Goloka, the banks of river Viraja, the land of Vmdavana, on the earth, forest, the campaka-vana, the beautiful sandalwood forest; besides the creepers like Madhavi, KetakI, Kunda, Mallika and Malati forest besides the sacred places.

## \|\| 21.38-39 \|\|

*tulasītarumūle ca puṇyadeśe supuṇyade \|*  
*adhiṣṭhānaṃ tu tīrthānāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca bhaviṣyati \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tatraiva sarvadevānāṃ samadhiṣṭhānameva ca \|*  
*tulasīpatrapatanaṃ prāyo yatra varānane \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. The plants of Tulasi will be grown in all the sacred places, the auspicious regions and the holy places. О damsel, having the beautiful face, the lord of all the gods resides at places, wherever the leaves of Tulasi fall.

## \|\| 21.40-41 \|\|

*sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvayajñeṣu dīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*tulasīpatratoyena yo'bhiṣekaṃ samācaret \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sudhāghaṭasahasreṇa sā tuṣṭirna bhaveddhareḥ \|*  
*yā ca tuṣṭirbhavennṝṇāṃ tulasīpatradānataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Whosoever is consecrated with the water of Tulasi plant, will be considered to have taken a bath in all the sacred places and also the performer of all the yajnas. Lord Vishnu never gets satisfied by consuming thousands of pitchers of nectar but he feels more satisfied with the Tulasi leaves offered to him.

## \|\| 21.42 \|\|

*gavāmayutadānena yatphalaṃ labhate naraḥ \|*  
*tulasīpatradānena tatphalaṃ labhate sati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The merit one earns by giving ten thousand cows in charity, can be achieved by just giving away a Tulasi leaf to someone.

## \|\| 21.43 \|\|

*tulasīpatratoyaṃ ca mṛtyukāle ca yo labhet \|*  
*sa mucyate sarvapāpādviṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. When the water together with the Tulasi leaf is poured into the mouth of a dying man, he is relieved of all the sins and proceeds to the abode of Tulasi.

## \|\| 21.44-46 \|\|

*nityaṃ yastulasī toyaṃ bhuṅkte bhaktyā ca yo naraḥ \|*  
*sa eva jīvanmuktaśca gaṃgāsnānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 44 \|\|*

*nityaṃ yastulasīṃ dattvā pūjayenmāṃ ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*lakṣāśvamedhajaṃ puṇyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tulasīṃ svakare dhṛtvā dehe dhṛtvā ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*prāṇāṃstyajati tīrtheṣu viṣṇu lokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. The one who consumes the water of Tulasi daily with devotion, is relieved of the cycle of birth and at the end achieves the merit of taking a bath in the Ganga. Such of the people who adore me daily offering Tulasi leaves, earn the merit of performing a lakh of Asvamedha sacrifices. There is no doubt about it. The one who proceeding to a sacred place meets with his end placing the Tulasi leaves over his body and hands and surely achieves the Vishnuloka.

## \|\| 21.47 \|\|

*tulasīkāṣṭhanirmāṇamālāṃ gṛhṇāti yo naraḥ \|*  
*pade pade'śvamedhasya labhate niścitaṃ phalam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The one who wears round his neck the garland of Tulasi gets entitled to performing the Asvamedha sacrifice at every step. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 21.48 \|\|

*tulasīṃ svakare dhṛtvā svīkāraṃ yo na rakṣati \|*  
*sa yāti kālasūtraṃ ca yāvaccandradivākarau \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. If one takes an oath holding a Tulasi leaf in his hand and then backs out, he falls in the terrific hell and remains there till the moon and the sun shine on earth.

## \|\| 21.49 \|\|

*karoti mithyāśapathaṃ tulasyā yo hi mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti kumbhīpākaṃ ca yāvadindrāścaturdaśa \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. One who makes a promise holding the Tulasi leaf in the hand and then backs out, he falls into Kumbhlpaka hell and remains there, up to the life of fourteen Indras.

## \|\| 21.50-51 \|\|

*tulasītoyakaṇikāṃ mṛtyukāle ca yo labhet \|*  
*ratnayānaṃ samāruhya vaikuṇṭhaṃ sa prayāti ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*pūrṇimāyāmamāyāṃ ca dvādaśyāṃ ravisaṃkrame \|*  
*tailābhyaṃge cāsnāte ca madhyāhne niśi sandhyayoḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. One who gets a Tulasi leaf at the time of his death, surely goes to the Vaikuntha mounted on a plane studded with gems on the days of the full moon, moonless day, twelfth day of the moon and the first day of the sun, whosoever, applying oil at the time of going to drop refuse in the morning and the evening or the midnight, remains without taking a bath or the one who removes a Tulasi leaf duly clad in all the sleeping garments, he acts like the killing of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 21.52-53 \|\|

*āśauce'śucikāle vā rātrivāsānvite narāḥ \|*  
*tulasīṃ ye ca chindanti te chindanti hareḥ śiraḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*trirātraṃ tulasīpatraṃ śuddhaṃ paryuṣitaṃ sati \|*  
*śrāddhe vrate vā dāne vā pratiṣṭhāyāṃ surārcane \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. A Tulasi leaf plucked three nights earlier is considered to be quite auspicious during the sraddha, vrata, the charity, glory and the adoration of the gods.

## \|\| 21.54 \|\|

*bhūgataṃ toyapatitaṃ yaddattaṃ viṣṇave sati \|*  
*śuddhaṃ tu tula sīpatraṃ kṣālanādanyakarmaṇi \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The Tulasi leave which falls on the ground, in the water or the one which is offered to lord Vishnu can be made use of the second time after washing it because it gets purified.

## \|\| 21.55-56 \|\|

*vṛkṣādhiṣṭhātrī devī yā goloke ca nirāmaye \|*  
*kṛṣṇena sārddhaṃ rahasi nityaṃ krīḍāṃ kariṣyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

*nadyadhiṣṭhātṛdevī yā bhārate ca supuṇyadā \|*  
*lavaṇodasya patnī ca madaṃśasya bhaviṣyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. О Tulasi, you are the sacred deity of the trees and you will always enjoy the company of lord Krishna in Goloka in seclusion. Thereafter you will emerge as a river from the amsha of lord Hari and will merge into the ocean who is also formed from my amsha. Thus you will become the wife of the ocean of salt and will be considered to be quite sacred.

## \|\| 21.57 \|\|

*tvaṃ ca svayaṃ mahāsādhvī vaikuṇṭhe mama sannidhau \|*  
*ramāsamā ca rāse ca bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. You yourself will reside in Vaikuntha in the form of the chaste Tulasi and you will shine there and will be honoured like Lakshmi. You will be present in the divine dance in Goloka. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 21.58 \|\|

*ahaṃ ca śailarūpī ca gaṇḍakītīrasannidhau \|*  
*adhiṣṭhānaṃ kari ṣyāmi bhārate tava śāpataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Because of the curse pronounced by you I shall appear in the form of a mountain near the river Gandakl.

## \|\| 21.59 \|\|

*vajrakīṭāśca kṛmayo vajradaṃṣṭrāśca tatra vai \|*  
*tacchilākuhare cakraṃ kariṣyanti madīyakama \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The insects will carve or cut the stones with their teeth besides my cakra on the stones.

## \|\| 21.60 \|\|

*ekadvāre catuścakraṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*navīnanīradaśyāmaṃ lakṣmīnārāyaṇābhidham \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Often the one having a single door, four cakras, wearing a long garland of flowers having the complexion of the fresh dark clouds, will be known as Lakshmi Narayana (Shalagrama).

## \|\| 21.61 \|\|

*ekadvāre catuścakraṃ navīnanīradopamam \|*  
*lakṣmījanārdanaṃ jñeyaṃ rahitaṃ vanamālayā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The one which has a single door, four cakras, having the complexion of the fresh cloud, wearing a Vanamcila, shall be known by the name of Lakshmi Janardana.

## \|\| 21.62 \|\|

*dvāradvaye catuścakraṃ goṣpadena samanvitam \|*  
*raghunāthābhidhaṃ jñeyaṃ rahitaṃ vanamālayā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The one which has two doors, four cakras, the mark of a cow's hoof and wearing the long garland of forest flowers, will be known as Raghunatha.

## \|\| 21.63 \|\|

*atikṣudraṃ dvicakraṃ ca navīnajaladaprabham \|*  
*dadhivāmanābhidhaṃ jñeyaṃ gṛhiṇāṃ ca sukhapradam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The one which has a small body, two cakras and the complexion of the fresh cloud, will be known by the name of Dadhivamana. It will provide welfare to the house-holder.

## \|\| 21.64 \|\|

*atikṣudraṃ dvicakraṃ ca vanamā lāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*vijñeyaṃ śrīdharaṃ devaṃ śrīpradaṃ gṛhiṇāṃ sadā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The one which is of tiny form having two cakras and the long garland of forest flowers round Ihe neck will be known by the name of Shridhara and will provide fortunes to the householders.

## \|\| 21.65 \|\|

*sthūlaṃ ca vartulākāraṃ rahitaṃ vanamālayā \|*  
*dvicakaṃ sphuṭamatyantaṃ jñeyaṃ dāmodarābhidham \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The one which is solid, round, without the one Mala and glitters, such a type of Shalagmma shall be known as Damodara.

## \|\| 21.66 \|\|

*madhyamaṃ vartulākāraṃ dvicakraṃ bāṇavikṣatam \|*  
*raṇarāmābhidhaṃ jñeyaṃ śaratūṇasamanvitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. One which is curly in appearance and is of medium type having the marks of cakra and quiver beside the arrow and the one over which is a sign of the cutting of an arrow, such a stone is known by the name of Ranarama.

## \|\| 21.67 \|\|

*madhyamaṃ saptacakraṃ ca chatratūṇasamanvitam \|*  
*rājarājeśvaraṃ jñeyaṃ rājasampatpradaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The stone which has seven cakras in the centre, an umbrella besides the quiver, is known by the name of Rajarajeshvara. Such a stone bestows kingdoms and wealth to the people.

## \|\| 21.68-69 \|\|

*dvisaptacakraṃ sthūlaṃ ca navīnajaladaprabham \|*  
*anantākhyaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ caturvargaphalapradam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*cakrākāraṃ dvicakraṃ ca saśrīkaṃ jaladaprabham \|*  
*sagoṣpadaṃ madhyamaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ madhusūda nam \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. The stone which has fourteen cakras, a quite solid and has the complexion of the fresh clouds, is known by the name of Ananta; it provides four types of merits like dharma, artha, kama and moksa. The one which is circular, having two discs and is bestowed with grace, having the complexion of the cloud, is shining and resembles the hoofs of a cow, belongs to a medium size and is known by the name of Madhustidana.

## \|\| 21.70 \|\|

*sudarśanaṃ caikacakraṃ guptacakraṃ gadādharam \|*  
*dvicakraṃ hayavaktrābhaṃ hayagrīvaṃ prakīrttitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The one having the Sudarsana-cakra, a secret cakra should be known as Gadadhara and the one having two cakras and the head of a horse, is known by the name of Hayagriva.

## \|\| 21.71 \|\|

*atīva vistṛtāsyaṃ ca dvicakraṃ vikaṭaṃ sati \|*  
*narasiṃhābhidhaṃ jñeyaṃ sadyo vairāgyadaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The one having a vast mouth, two cakras and is of terrific appearance, is known by the name of Narasimha who leads people to Vairagya.

## \|\| 21.72 \|\|

*dvicakraṃ vistṛtāsyaṃ ca vanamālāsamanvitam \|*  
*lakṣmīnṛsiṃhaṃ vijñeyaṃ gṛhiṇāṃ sukhadaṃ sadā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The one having two cakras, a vast mouth and adorned with a long garlands of flowers, is known by the name of Lakshmi-Narasimha. It provides pleasure to all the house-holders.

## \|\| 21.73 \|\|

*dvāradeśe dvicakraṃ ca saśrīkaṃ ca samaṃ sphuṭam \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The one which has two cakras and a mark of Shri engraved on it. Such a type of stone is given the name of Vasudeva. It fulfils all the desires of the people.

## \|\| 21.74 \|\|

*pradyumnaṃ sūkṣmacakraṃ ca navīnanīradaprabham \|*  
*suṣire cchidrabahulaṃ gṛhiṇāṃ ca sukhapradam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The one which has a fine cakra, has a lustre of new clouds having small holes, such a type of stone is known by the name Pradyumna and provides pleasure to all.

## \|\| 21.75 \|\|

*dve cakre caikalagne ca pṛṣṭhe yatra tu puṣkalam \|*  
*saṃkarṣaṇaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ sukhadaṃ gṛhiṇāṃ sadā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The one in which two wheels are joined and the back of which is quite vast is known by the name of Samkarsana. It provides pleasure to the house-holder.

## \|\| 21.76 \|\|

*aniruddhaṃ tu pītābhaṃ vartulaṃ cātiśobhanam \|*  
*sukhapradaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ pravadanti manī ṣiṇaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The one which has the yellow complexion, is round in nature, such a beautiful stone is known by the name of Aniruddha by the intellectuals which provides all the pleasure to the householders.

## \|\| 21.77-78 \|\|

*śālagrāmaśilā yatra tatra sannihito hariḥ \|*  
*tatraiva lakṣmīrvasati sarvatīrthasamanvitā \|\| 77 \|\|*

*yāni kāni ca pāpāni brahmahatyādikāni ca \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi naśyaṃti śālagrāmaśilārccanāt \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. Wherever the stone of Shalagrama is kept, lord Vishnu with Lakshmi also resides there. By adoring the stone of Shalagrama one is relieved of all the sins including that of Brahmahatyci.

## \|\| 21.79 \|\|

*chatrākāraṃ bhavedrājyaṃ vartule ca mahāśriyaḥ \|*  
*duḥkhaṃ ca śakaṭākāre śūlāgre maraṇaṃ dhuvam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. If the Shalagrama stone is like an umbrella, one gets the kingdom, if it is roundish, it provides the fortunes, if it is of the form of a cart it is painful and it is like the fore part of the trident, it surely brings death.

## \|\| 21.80 \|\|

*vikṛtāsye ca dāridryaṃ piṅgale hānireva ca \|*  
*lagnacakre bhavedvyādhirvidīrṇe maraṇaṃ dhuvam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If it is of a deformed face, it gives misfortune and in case of yellow colour, loss. With the broken cakra it causes ailment and the Shalagrama stone causes death.

## \|\| 21.81 \|\|

*vrataṃ dānaṃ pratiṣṭhā ca śrāddhaṃ ca devapūjanam \|*  
*śālagrāmaśilāyāścaivādhiṣṭhānātpraśastakam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. In case the Shalagrama stone remains consecrated during the vrata, perfonning charity, glorious deed, sraddha and the adoration of gods, one achieves great merit.

## \|\| 21.82 \|\|

*sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvayajñeṣu dīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*śālagrāmaśilātoyairyo'bhiṣekaṃ samācaret \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The one who consecrates with the water of the Shalagrama stone, earns the merit of having a bath in all the sacred places and makes the yajnas successful.

## \|\| 21.83-84 \|\|

*sarvadāneṣu yatpuṇyaṃ prādakṣiṇye bhuvo yathā \|*  
*sarvayajñeṣu tīrtheṣu vrateṣvanaśaneṣu ca \|\| 83 \|\|*

*tasya sparśaṃ ca vāñchanti tīrthāni nikhilāni ca \|*  
*jīvanmukto mahāpūto bhavedeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. The merit one earns by giving away all the riches in charity and by taking a round of the globe, he earns the merit of performing all the yajnas, visiting the holy places and the performing of tapas. He also becomes free from birth and death and becomes the great son of the soil. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 21.85 \|\|

*pāṭhe caturṇāṃ vedānāṃ tapasāṃ karaṇe sati \|*  
*tatpuṇyaṃ labhate nṛnaṃ śālagrāmaśilārcanāt \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. One derives the merit of reciting all the Vedas by worshipping the Shalagrama stone undoubtedly.

## \|\| 21.86-87 \|\|

*śālagrāmaśilātoyaṃ nityaṃ bhuṅkte ca yo naraḥ \|*  
*surepsitaṃ prasādaṃ ca janmamṛtyujarāharam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*tasya sparśaṃ ca vāñchanti tīrthāni nikhi lāni ca \|*  
*jīvanmukto mahāpūto'pyante yāti hareḥ padam \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. The one who sips the water of the Shalagrama stone and also consumes the prasada of the god, he remains without old age and is freed from birth and death. All the sacred places become desirous of touching such a person. Therefore the one having been relieved of birth and death gets purified and moves on to the abode of Vishnu.

## \|\| 21.88-89 \|\|

*tatraiva hariṇā sārddhamasaṃkhyaṃ prākṛtaṃ layam \|*  
*paśyatyeva hi dāsye ca nirmukto dāsyakarmaṇi \|\| 88 \|\|*

*yāni kāni ca pāpāni brahmahatyādikāni ca \|*  
*taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā bhiyā yānti vainateyamivo ragāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. Residing there with the lord Vishnu and providing setvices to him, he (devotee) looks innumberable Prakrta layas. He frees from bondage and spends much time there. At the sight of the Shalagrama stone, Brahmahatya and other sins, flee away as the serpent disappears at the sight of a Garuda.

## \|\| 21.90 \|\|

*tatpādapadmarajasā sadyaḥ pūtā vasundharā \|*  
*puṃsāṃ lakṣaṃ tatpitṝṇāṃ nistārastasya janmanaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The earth gets purified with the dust of his feet. A lakh of generations of such a person get redeemed.

## \|\| 21.91 \|\|

*śālagrāmaśilā toyaṃ mṛtyukāla ca yo labhet \|*  
*sarvapāpādvinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. At the time of death if one sips the water of the Shalagrama stone, one is relieved of all the sins and goes to the abode of Vishnu.

## \|\| 21.92 \|\|

*nirvāṇamuktiṃ labhate karmabhogādvimucyate \|*  
*viṣṇupāde pralīnaśca bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Thereafter facing the reward of his deeds he achieves salvation and gets merged into the feet of lord Vishnu. There is no doubt about it. Therefore the one who tells a lie after keeping the Shalagrama stone with him, has to suffer in the Kurmadamstra hell up to the age of Brahma.

## \|\| 21.93 \|\|

*śālagrāmaśilāṃ dhṛtvā mithyāvādaṃ vadettu yaḥ \|*  
*sa yāti kūrmadaṃṣṭraṃ ca yāvadvai brahmaṇo vayaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. If anyone takes an oath after touching the Shalagrama stone and then backs out, he has to suffer in a terrific hell for a lakh of manvantaras.

## \|\| 21.94-96 \|\|

*śālagrāmaśilāṃ spṛṣṭvā svīkāraṃ yo na pālayet \|*  
*sa prayātyasipatraṃ ca lakṣamanvantarādhikam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*tulasīpatra vicchedaṃ śālagrāme karoti yaḥ \|*  
*tasya janmāntare kāle strīvicchedo bhaviṣyati \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tulasīpatravicchedaṃ śaṃkhe yo hi karoti ca \|*  
*bhāryyāhīno bhavetso'pi rogī ca saptajanmasu \|\| 96 \|\|*

94-96. The one who separates the Tulasi leaf from Shalagrama, has to face the agony of the separation from the wife for many births. Similarly the one who separates the Tulasi leaf from the conch, meets with the grief of death of his wife and remains in the hell for seven births.

## \|\| 21.97 \|\|

*śālagrāmaṃ ca tulasīṃ śaṃkhamekatra eva ca \|*  
*yo rakṣati mahājñānī sa bhave cchrīharipriyaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The one who keeps Shalagrama stone, Tulasi and Samkha together, becomes a great intellectual and the beloved of the lord.

## \|\| 21.98 \|\|

*sakṛdeva hi yo yasyāṃ vīryyādhānaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*tadvicchede tasya duḥkhaṃ bhavedeva parasparam \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. If a person implants his seed in the womb of any woman, the separation of that lady even for a moment becomes unbearable for him.

## \|\| 21.99 \|\|

*tvaṃ priyā śaṃkhacūḍasya caikamanvantarāvadhi \|*  
*śaṃkhena sārddha tvadbhedaḥ kevalaṃ duḥkhadastava \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. You have become the beloved of Samkhacuda for a manvantara and as such to separate you from Samkhacuda would be quite painful for you.”

## \|\| 21.100 \|\|

*ityuktvā śrīharistāṃ ca virarāma ca sādaram \|*  
*sa ca dehaṃ parityajya divyarūpaṃ dadhāra ha \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Thus speaking lord Vishnu kept quiet and Tulasi met with the end of her life and took to the divine form.

## \|\| 21.101 \|\|

*yathā śrīśca tathā sā cāpyuvāsa harivakṣasi \|*  
*prajagāma tayā sārddhaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ kamalā patiḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Like Lakshmi she also started residing in the heart of lord Vishnu and lord Vishnu proceeded with her to Vaikuntha.

## \|\| 21.102 \|\|

*lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī gaṅgā tulasī cāpi nārada \|*  
*hareḥ priyāścatasraśca vabhūvurīśvarasya ca \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. O Narada, thus Vishnu had four spouses named Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Ganga and Tulasi.

## \|\| 21.103 \|\|

*sadyastaddehajātā ca babhūva gaṇḍakī nadī \|*  
*hareraṃśena śailaśca tattīre puṇyado nṛṇām \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. From the body of Tulasi at once appeared the river Gandakl. At the bank of the said river a huge mountain appeared from the amsha of lord Vishnu, which was quite sacred for the humans.

## \|\| 21.104 \|\|

*kurvanti tatra kīṭāśca śilāṃ bahuvidhāṃ mune \|*  
*jale patanti yā yāśca jaladābhāśca niścitam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. O sage, the insects make many types of stones there. The stones of dark complexion fall into the river daily.

## \|\| 21.105 \|\|

*sthalasthāḥ piṅgalā jñeyāścopatāpāddhareriti \|*  
*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. With the grace of the lord the stones of the river appear in red or brown colour. Thus I have told you everything and what more do you want to know?

## Chapter 22

## \|\| 22.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*
