23\. Vasus, the moon, Rudras, Stirya, the sages, Narada, Manu besides Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva were also present there beside the throne. In the meantime a Brahmana arrived here.

## \|\| 50.24 \|\|

*munināradamanvādibrahmaviṣṇuśivānvite \|*  
*etasminnantare tatra vipra ekaḥ samāyayau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He had dishevelled hair and wore dirty clothes. His throat, lips and tongue had dried up.

## \|\| 50.25-30 \|\|

*rūkṣo malinavāsāśca śuṣkakaṇṭhauṣṭhatālukaḥ \|*  
*ratnasiṃhāsanasthaṃ ca mālyacandanacarcitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*rājānamāśiṣaṃ cakre sasmitaḥ sampuṭāñjaliḥ \|*  
*praṇanāma nṛpastaṃ ca nottasthau kiṃcideva hi \|\| 26 \|\|*

*sabhāsadaśca nottasthurjahasuḥ svalpameva ca \|*  
*munibhyo'pi ca devebhyo namaskṛtya dvijottamaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śaśāpa nṛpatiṃ krodhāttatrātiṣṭhanniraṃkuśaḥ \|*  
*gaccha dūramato rājyādbhraṣṭaśrīrbhava pāmara \|\| 28 \|\|*

*bhavāciraṃ galatkuṣṭhī buddhihīno'pyupadrutaḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā kampitaḥ krodhātsabhāsthāñchaptumudyataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ye yatra jahasuḥ sarve samuttasthuḥ sabhāsadaḥ \|*  
*sarve cakruḥ praṇāmaṃ te krodhaṃ tatyāja vāḍavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

25-30. That Brahmana offered his blessing to the king raising his hand and then folding them, who was seated on the lion-throne decorated with many of the garlands. But the king on his part neither accepted the greetings of the ^Brahmana, nor did he get up from his seat to receive him. All his courtiers also did not show any respect to the Brahmana and on the contrary some of them laughed at him. The best of the Brahmana after bowing to the gods and the sages got enraged but stood there fearlessly in anger. Then he pronounced a curse on the king, “O degraded one, you will be deprived of all your glory and you will be driven away from your kingdom and you will soon suffer from leprosy in the neck. You will be deprived of your wisdom and become violent.” Thus speaking the enraged Brahmana was also getting ready to pronounce a curse on the courtiers as well. Thereafter all the people who were laughing at him got up in panic and started offering salutation to him. Finding this, the Brahmana was relieved of the anger.

## \|\| 50.31-43 \|\|

*praṇamyāgatya rājā taṃ ruroda bhayakātaraḥ \|*  
*nissasāra sabhāmadhyāddhṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇo gūḍharūpī ca prajvalanbrahmatejasā \|*  
*tatpaścānmunayaḥ sarve prayayurbhayakātarāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*he vipra tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti samuccāryya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*pulahaśca pulastyaśca pracetā bhṛguraṃgirāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*marīciḥ kaśyapaścaiva vasiṣṭhaḥ kratureva ca \|*  
*śukro bṛhaspati ścaiva durvāsā lomaśastathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*gautamaśca kaṇādaśca kaṇvaḥ kātyāyanaḥ kaṭhaḥ \|*  
*pāṇinirjājaliścaiva ṛṣyaśṛṃgo vibhāṇḍakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*taittiriścāpyāpiśalirmārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*sanakaśca sanandaśca voḍhuḥ pailaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sanatkumāro bhagavānnaranārāyaṇāvṛṣī \|*  
*parāśaro jaratkāruḥ saṃvarttaḥ karabhastathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bharadvājaśca vālmīkiraurvaśca cyavanastathā \|*  
*agastyo 'trirutathyaśca saṅkartā''stīka āsuriḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śilālirlāṅgaliścaiva śākalyaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ \|*  
*gargo vatsaḥ pañcaśikho jamadagniśca devalaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*jaigīṣavyo vāmadevo vālakhilyādayastathā \|*  
*śaktirdakṣaḥ kardamaśca praskannaḥ kapilastathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*viśvāmitraśca kautsaścāpyṛcīko'pyaghamarṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ete cānye ca munayaḥ pitaro'gnirharipriyā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*dikpālā devatāḥ sarvā vipraṃ paścātsamāyayuḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇaṃ bodhayāmāsurvāsayāmāsurīśvari \|\| 42 \|\|*

*samūcustaṃ krameṇaiva nītiṃ nītiviśāradāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

31-43. Overcome by fear, the king also bowed in reverence to him and started crying approaching the Brahmanas. Thereafter the Brahmana, with his mind filled with agony left the place. The Brahmana had a divine form and his face was glittering with divine glory. Thereafter all the sages were grieved in terror. They said: “O Brahmana, you stop for a moment.” Thus saying again and again all of them started following him, the sages like Pulaha, Pulastya, Praceta, Bhrigu, Angira, Marlci, Kashyapa, Vasistha, Kratu, Sukra, Brihaspati, Durvasa, Lomasa, Gautama, Kanada, Kanva, Katyayana, Katha, Panini, Jajali, Srngi, Vibhandaka, Taittiri, Apishali, Markandekya, the great sage Sanaka, Sananda, Vodhu, Paila, Sanatana, Sanatkumara, Nara-Narayana, Parasara, Jaratkaru, Samvatta, Karabha, Bharadvaja, Valmiki, Aurava, Cyavana, Agastya, Atri, Utathya, Samkarta, Astlka, Asuri, Silali, Langali, Sakalya, Sakat ayana, Garga, Vatsa, Pancas'ikha, Jamadagni, Devala, Jaiglsavya, Vamadeva, Balakhilya, sakti, Daksha, Kardam, Kapila, Vishvamitra, Kautsa, Rclka and Aghmarsana and several other sages, manes, Agni, Haripriya, Dikpalas and the gods also arrived there. О goddess, they stopped the Brahmana and tried to convince him. All of them well-versed in the science of polity and started talking to him in appropriate words.

## Chapter 51

## \|\| 51.1 \|\|

*śrīpārvatyuvāca \|*  
*kimūcurbrāhmaṇaṃ brahmanbrāhmaṇā brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*nītijñā nītivacanaṃ tanmāṃ vyākhyātumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Parvati said — О Brahman, the Brahmanas who were the sons of Brahma and were well-versed in polity what type of knowledge did they extend to the Brahmana on the polity. You kindly let me know.

## \|\| 51.2 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*santoṣya taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ca stavena vinayena ca \|*  
*krameṇa vaktumārebhe munisaṃgho varānane \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sanatkumara said — After you, Lakshmi, glory, prowess, popularity, humility, immense riches, the manes and all the gods together with the god of fire, the royal grandeur also left the king. О best of the sages, now you be pleased because the Brahmanas are considered to be those who get pleased soon. О sage, the mind of the Brahmanas is soft like the butter and gets purified with the performing of continuous tapas and become spotless.

## \|\| 51.3-5 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*tvatpaścādāgatā lakṣmīḥ kīrttiḥ sattvaṃ yaśastathā \|*  
*suśīlaṃ ca mahaiśvaryaṃ pitaro'gniḥ surāstathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*āgatā nṛpagehebhyaḥ kṛtvā bhraṣṭaśriyaṃ nṛpam \|*  
*bhava tuṣṭo dvijaśreṣṭha cāśutoṣaśca vāḍavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānāṃ tu hṛdayaṃ komalaṃ navanītavat \|*  
*śuddhaṃ sunirmalaṃ caiva mārjitaṃ tapasā mune \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Therefore, О Brahmana, you kindly forgive and come to the place of the king dropping the dust of your feet there, purifying the same. Thereafter you bless him.

## \|\| 51.6 \|\|

*kṣamasvāgaccha viprendra śuddhaṃ kuru nṛpālayam \|*  
*āśiṣaṃ kuru tasmai tvaṃ pavitrapadareṇunā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Bhrigu said — The one from whose house a mendicant returns disappointed, his manes, the gods and Agni, because of not honouring the guest, also depart in disappointment. Therefore, О Brahmana, you kindly forgive him and now reaching the abode of the king you purify it because the one in whose house the guest is not honoured, earns the sin of killing a woman, killing a cow, ungratefulness, Brahmahatya and of committing sin with the wife of the Guru.

## \|\| 51.7-9 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca \|*  
*atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhātpratinivarttate \|*  
*pitarastasya devāśca vahniścaiva tathaiva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nirāśāḥ pratigacchanti cātitherapratigrahāt \|*  
*kṣamasvāgaccha viprendra śuddhaṃ kuru nṛpālayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*strīghnairgoghnaiḥ kṛtaghnaiśca brahmaghnairgurutalpagaiḥ \|*  
*tulyadoṣo bhavatyetairyasyātithiranarcitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Pulastya said — The one who looks down upon a guest arriving at home, the same guest goes away carrying all his merits and dropping all his sins at the door of such a person.

## \|\| 51.10 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*paśyanti ye vakradṛṣṭyā cātithiṃ gṛhamāgatam \|*  
*dattvā svapāpaṃ tasmai tatpuṇyamādāya gacchati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Therefore, О son, you forgive the, sin of the king. You move pleasantly as the king could not get up to welcome you because of the move of the destiny; therefore you forgive him.

## \|\| 51.11 \|\|

*kṣamasva nṛpadoṣaṃ ca gaccha vatsa yathāsukham \|*  
*rājā svakarmadoṣeṇa nottasthau tatkṣamāṃ kuru \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Pulaha said — Such of the Kshatriya or a Brahmana, who, because of the royal riches or the knowledge misbehaves with a Brahmana and does not extend due respect to him, such a Ks atrlya is deprived of all the riches and the Brahmana is deprived of performing sandhya all the three times. He is also deprived of the vrata of Ekadashi and is not considered fit for getting the naivedya of lord Vishnu. Therefore, О Brahmana you kindly forgive him and purify the king.

## \|\| 51.12-13 \|\|

*pulaha uvāca \|*  
*rājaśriyā vidyayā vā brāhmaṇaṃ yo'vamanyate \|*  
*viprastrisandhyāhīno yaḥ śrīhīnaḥ kṣatriyo bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ekādaśīvihīnaśca viṣṇunaivedyavañcitaḥ \|*  
*kṣamasvāgaccha viprendra śuddhaṃ kuru nṛpālayam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Ritu said — О Brahmana, whosoever among Brahmanas, Ksatrlyas, Vaishyas or Siidras insults a Brahmana, is deprived of dlksa, becomes a pauper having no son, is ultimately deprived of his wife also. Therefore О lord, you forgive him and moving into the abode of the king you kindly purify it.

## \|\| 51.14-15 \|\|

*kraturuvāca \|*  
*brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vā'pi vaiśyo vā śūdra eva ca \|*  
*dīkṣāhīno bhavetso'pi brāhmaṇaṃ yo'vamanyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dhanahīnaḥ putrahīno bhāryyāhīno bhaveddhruvam \|*  
*kṣamasvāgaccha bhagavañchuddhaṃ kuru nṛpālayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Angira said — In the sacred land of Bharata, whosoever insults the Brahmanas, gods and the teacher, is always deprived of the devotion of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 51.16 \|\|

*aṅgirā uvāca \|*  
*jñānavānbrāhmaṇo bhūtvā brāhmaṇaṃ yo'vamanyate \|*  
*vṛṣavāho bhavetso'pi bhārate saptajanmasu \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Marichi said — In the sacred land of Bharata, whosoever insults the gods, the Brahmanas and the teacher, is deprived of the devotion of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 51.17 \|\|

*marīciruvāca \|*  
*puṇyakṣetre bhārate ca devaṃ ca brāhmaṇaṃ gurum \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktivihīnaśca sa bhavedyo'vamanyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Kashyapa said — The one who laughs at a Vais nava Brahmana and also insults him, is deprived of the mantra of Vishnu and his devotion.

## \|\| 51.18 \|\|

*kaśyapa uvāca \|*  
*vaiṣṇavaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā yo'satyamavamanyate \|*  
*viṣṇumantravihīnaśca tatpūjāvirato bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Pracheta said — On finding a Brahmana beggar who does not get up to welcome him, he is deprived of the devotion of his parents in the land of Bharata.

## \|\| 51.19 \|\|

*pracetā uvāca \|*  
*atithiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā nābhyutthānaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*pitṛbhaktivihīnassyātsa bhavedbhārate bhuvi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The foolish fellow is born as an elephant for seven births. Therefore, О best of the Brahmanas, you move quickly and offer your blessing to the king.

## \|\| 51.20 \|\|

*prāpnoti kauñjarīṃ yoniṃ sa mūḍhaḥ saptajanmasu \|*  
*śīghraṃ gaccha dvijaśreṣṭha rājñe dehyāśiṣaśśubhāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Durvasa said — The one who does not bow in reverence while coming across the image of the teacher, Brahmana and gods, is reborn as a pig on earth and the one who indulges himself in giving false evidence, becomes a betrayer. Therefore, you kindly forgive the sins of all of us and accept the welcome by the king.

## \|\| 51.21-22 \|\|

*durvāsā uvāca \|*  
*guruṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā'pi devatāpratimāmapi \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā śīghraṃ na praṇametsa bhavetsūkaro bhuvi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mithyāsākṣī ca bhavati tathā viśvāsaghātakaḥ \|*  
*kṣamasva sarvamasmākamātithyagrahaṇaṃ kuru \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The king said — All the sages here have followed Dharma deceitfully, therefore you enlighten me on the truth.

## \|\| 51.23 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*chalena kathito dharmo yuṣmābhirmunipuṅgavaiḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ kṛtvā ca vispaṣṭaṃ māṃ mūḍhaṃ bodhayantvaho \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О best of the yogis, those, who indulge in the killing of women and cows, are ungrateful and by enjoying the company of the wife of a Guru also indulge in the killing of the Brahmana, what a type of sin is attracted by them. You kindly tell me.

## \|\| 51.24 \|\|

*strīghnagoghnakṛtaghnānāṃ gurustrīgāmināṃ tathā \|*  
*brahmaghnānāṃ ca ko doṣo brūta māṃ yogināṃ varāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Vasistha said — О king, the one who intentionally kills the cow, such a person should go on a pilgrimage for a year and he should consume the pulp of barley and should consume water with hands only.

## \|\| 51.25 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*kāmato govadhe rājanvarṣaṃ tīrthaṃ bhramennaraḥ \|*  
*yavayāvakabhojī ca kareṇa ca jalaṃ pibet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thereafter he should offer the best of cows to the Brahmana, feed a hundred Brahmana give daksina. He is then relieved of his sin.

## \|\| 51.26 \|\|

*tadā dhenuśataṃ divyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sadakṣiṇam \|*  
*dattvā muñcati pāpācca bhojayitvā śataṃ dvijān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Even after repenting, he is not freed from the entire sin and because of this, he has to be born and a Chandala.

## \|\| 51.27 \|\|

*prāyaścitte tu vai cīrṇe sarvapāpānna mucyate \|*  
*pāpāvaśeṣādbhavati duḥkhī cāṇḍāla eva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereafter the great sinner is born as a pig for seven births and for another seven births he is born as a serpent. He is purified thereafter.

## \|\| 51.28 \|\|

*ātideśikahatyāyāṃ tadardhaṃ phalamaśnute \|*  
*prāyaścittānukalpena sarvapāpānna mucyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. lirhaspati said — One earns double the sin of killing a woman by indulging in Brahmahatya. For this he has to remain for a lakh of years in Kumbhlpaka hell.

## \|\| 51.29 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*gohatyādviguṇaṃ pāpaṃ strīhatyāyāṃ bhaveddhruvam \|*  
*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi kālasūtre vaseddhruvam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thereafter the condemned sinner is reborn as an insect of refuse for a hundred years and is further reborn as a snake for seven births, before he is purified.

## \|\| 51.30 \|\|

*tato bhavenmahāpāpī sūkaraḥ saptajanmasu \|*  
*tato bhavati sarpaśca saptajanmanyataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Gautama said — О king, an ungrateful person attracts four time more the sin than Brahmahatya and it is certain that the Vedas do not prescribe the redemption of an ungrateful person.

## \|\| 51.31 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*strīhatyādviguṇaṃ pāpaṃ brahmahatyākṛto bhavet \|*  
*lakṣavarṣaṃ mahāghore kumbhīpāke vaseddhruvam \|\| 31\|\|*

31\. If one kills a cow at the instance of another, he earns half of the sin and he also cannot be relieved of all the sins, by performing acts of repentance.

## \|\| 51.32 \|\|

*tato bhavenmahāpāpī viṣṭhākīṭaḥ śatābdakam \|*  
*tato bhavati sarpaśca saptajanmanyataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Sukra said — One earns double the sin of Gohatya by killing a woman and for that he has to fall into the kalasutra hell and remain there for sixty thousand years.

## \|\| 51.33 \|\|

*gautama uvāca \|*  
*doṣaḥ kṛtaghne rājendra brahmahatyācaturguṇaḥ \|*  
*niṣkṛtirnāsti vedoktā kṛtaghnānāṃ ca niścitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The king said — О best of those well-versed in the Vedas, you kindly enlighten me on the symptoms of the ungrateful people, its different divisions and what type of sin is attracted by each one of them.

## \|\| 51.34 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ ca kṛtaghnānāṃ vada vedavidāṃ vara \|*  
*kṛtaghnaḥ katidhā proktaḥ keṣu ko doṣa eva ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Rsyasrnga said — In the Samaveda sixteen types of ungrateful people have been listed. Each one has to suffer for the sin committed by him.

## \|\| 51.35 \|\|

*ṛṣyaśṛṅga uvāca \|*  
*kṛtaghnāḥ ṣoḍaśavidhāḥ sāmavede nirūpitāḥ \|*  
*sarvaḥ pratyekadoṣeṇa pratyekaṃ phalamaśnute \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The one who performs good to others, is truthful, performs noble deed, is devoted to his Dharma, is truthful to the vow taken by him, performs charity, keeps up his words and the one who performs the task of his teacher, the task of the gods, performs good deeds, adore the Brahmanas, adores the lord daily, is always commendable but the one who creates obstruction in the performing of these noble deeds, is considered to be an ungrateful person. The sinners get different abodes in the hell for committing different sins and have also to be born variously.

## \|\| 51.36-39 \|\|

*kṛte satye ca puṇye ca svadharme tapasi sthite \|*  
*pratijñāyāṃ ca dāne ca svagoṣṭhīparipālane \|\| 36 \|\|*

*gurukṛtye devakṛtye kāmyakṛtye dvijārcane \|*  
*nityakṛtye ca viśvāse paradharmapradānayoḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*etānyo hanti pāpiṣṭhaḥ sa kṛtaghna iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ santi lokāśca tajjanma bhinnayoniṣu \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yānyāṃśca narakāṃste ca yānti rājendra pāpinaḥ \|*  
*te te ca narakāḥ santi yamaloke suniścitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. О king, whichever hell is visited by the sinners, Yama is always found present there.

## \|\| 51.40 \|\|

*suyajña uvāca \|*  
*ke kiṃ kṛtvā kṛtaghnāśca kāṃskāngacchanti rauravān \|*  
*pratyekaṃ śrotumicchāmi vaktumarhasi me prabho \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Suyajna said — О lord, by performing which deed one is termed as ungrateful and to which of the terrific hells he has to move. You kindly tell me, because I am quite anxious to know about them.

## \|\| 51.41 \|\|

*kātyāyana uvāca \|*  
*kṛtvā śapatharūpaṃ ca satyaṃ hanti na pālayet \|*  
*sa kṛtaghnaḥ kālasūtre vasedeva caturyugam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Katayayana said — The one who is not truthful after taking an oath and desecrates the same, such an ungrateful fellow falls into kalastitra hell and remains there for four yugas.

## \|\| 51.42 \|\|

*saptajanmasu kākaśca saptajanmasu pecakaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ śūdro mahāvyādhiḥ saptajanmasvataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thereafter for seven births he is born as an owl and for seven births he is born as a Stidra suffering from some ailment. He is redeemed thereafter.

## \|\| 51.43 \|\|

*śrīsanandana uvāca \|*  
*puṇyaṃ kṛtvā vadatyeva kīrtivarddhanahetunā \|*  
*sa kṛtaghnastaptasūrmyāṃ vasatyeva yugatrayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. performing the good deeds, praises himself such an ungrateful person falls into the hell named Taptasunnl and remains there for three yugas.

## \|\| 51.44 \|\|

*pañcajanmasu maṇḍūkastriṣu janmasu karkaṭaḥ \|*  
*tadā mūko mahāvyādhirdaridraśca tataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thereafter for five births he is born as a frog, for three births he is born as a crab, then he is born as a dumb person suffering from grave ailment and a pauper. He is purified thereafter.

## \|\| 51.45-47 \|\|

*sanātana uvāca \|*  
*svadharmaṃ hanti yo vipraḥ sandhyātrayavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*atarpayaṃśca yaḥ snāti viṣṇunaivedyavarjitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*viṣṇupūjāvihīnaśca viṣṇumantravihīnakaḥ \|*  
*ekādaśīvihīnaḥ śrīkṛṣṇajanmadine tadā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śivarātrau ca yo bhuṅkte śrīrāmanavamīdine \|*  
*pitṛkṛtyādihīno yaḥ sa kṛtaghra iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Sanatana said — Such of Brahmanas who does not perform the sandhya thrice and takes a bath without performing tarpana, discarding his dharma or eats without first offering the food to Vishnu or neglects the devotion of Vishnu, the mantra of Vishnu, Ekadasi-vrata or takes food on the birthday of Krishna, Shivaratri or RamanavamI and does not perfonn the rites for the manes, is considered to be an ungrateful person.

## \|\| 51.48-53 \|\|

*kumbhīpāke vasatyeva yāvadindrāścaturdaśa \|*  
*tataścāṇḍālatāṃ yāti saptajanmasu niścitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*śatajanmani gṛdhraśca śatajanmani sūkaraḥ \|*  
*tato bhavedbrāhmaṇaśca śūdrāṇāṃ sūpakārakaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tato bhavejjanma sapta brāhmaṇo vṛṣavāhakaḥ \|*  
*śūdrāṇāṃ śavadāhī ca bhavetsaptasu janmasu \|\| 50 \|\|*

*dvijo bhūtvā saptajanau bhārate vṛṣalīpatiḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā svabhogaleśaṃ ca bhramitvā yāti rauravam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*punaḥ punaḥ pāpayoniṃ narakaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tato bhavedgardabhaśca mārjāraḥ pañcajanmasu \|\| 52 \|\|*

*pañcajanmasu maṇḍūko bhavecchuddhastataḥ kramāt \|\| 53 \|\|*

48-53. Because of these sins, he remains in Kitmbhlpaka hell up to the time equivalent to the life of fourteen Indras. Thereafter, he is born as a vulture for a hundred times, as a pig for a hundred times and becomes a store-keeper of the Shudras thereafter. After that, he is born for seven births as the one who loads weight on the bulls or yokes them to the plough. For further seven births he is reborn as a Brahmana burning the dead bodies of Shudra and for further seven births he becomes a Brahmana having a Shudra woman as his wife. Thus he remains in the terrific hell till a fraction of the sins committed by him remains. He takes birth in the sinful way and again falls into the hell. Thereafter he is born as an ass seven times and a frog five times before he is purified.

## \|\| 51.54-55 \|\|

*suyajña uvāca \|*  
*śūdrāṇāṃ sūpakaraṇe śūdrāṇāṃ śavadāhane \|*  
*śūdrānnabhojane vā'pi śūdrastrīgamane'pi ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānāṃ ca ko doṣo vṛṣāṇāṃ vāhane tathā \|*  
*etānsarvānsamālocya brūhi māṃ niścayaṃ mune \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Suyajna said — О sage, what type of sin is attracted by a person by becoming a store-keeper of the Shudras, by burning their dead bodies, by eating the food of the Shudras and by keeping company of the Shudra woman or a Brahmana becoming a weight-loader of the bulls? You kindly tell me everything in detail.

## \|\| 51.56 \|\|

*parāśara uvāca \|*  
*śūdrāṇāṃ sūpakāraśca yo vipro jñānadurbalaḥ \|*  
*asipatre vasatyeva yugānāmekasaptatiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Parasara said — Because of the lack of knowledge a Brahmana becomes a store-keeper of the Shudras. He falls in the Asipatra hell for seventy one yugas.

## \|\| 51.57 \|\|

*tato bhavedgardabhaśca mūṣikaḥ saptajanmasu \|*  
*tailakīṭassaptajanmasvataḥ śuddho bhavennaraḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thereafter he becomes an ass, a mouse, an insect of oil for seven births before he is purified.

## \|\| 51.58 \|\|

*jaratkāruruvāca \|*  
*bhṛtyadvārā svayaṃ vā'pi yo vipro vṛṣavāhakaḥ \|*  
*sa kṛtaghna iti khyātaḥ prasiddho bhārate nṛpa \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Jaratkam said — О Brahmana, the one who himself being a Brahmana engages himself in the loading of the bulls or yoking them to the plough, is known as an ungrateful person in the land of Bharata.

## \|\| 51.59 \|\|

*brahmahatyāsamaṃ pāpaṃ tannityaṃ vṛṣatāḍane \|*  
*vṛṣapṛṣṭhe bhāradānātpāpaṃ taddviguṇaṃ bhaveta \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. By maintainings the bull daily and beating it, one earns the sin of Brahmahatya and by loading the weight over the bull, one earns double the sin.

## \|\| 51.60 \|\|

*sūryyātape vāhayedyaḥ kṣudhitaṃ tṛṣṭitaṃ vṛṣam \|*  
*brahmahatyāśataṃ pāpaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Thus the one who yokes to the plough a hungry and thirsty bull in the summer, earns the sin of Brahmahatya. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 51.61-67 \|\|

*annaṃ viṣṭhā jalaṃ mūtraṃ viprāṇāṃ vṛṣavāhinām \|*  
*nādhikāro bhavetteṣāṃ pitṛdevārcane nṛpa \|\| 61 \|\|*

*devatā nahi gṛhana teṣāṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ jalam \|*  
*dadāti yadi dambhena vipātāya prakalpate \|\| 62 \|\|*

*yo g kāmato'nanaṃ ca brāhmaṇo vṛṣavāhinām \|*  
*nādhikāro bhavetteṣāṃ pitṛdevārcane nṛpa \|\| 63 \|\|*

*lālākuṇḍe vasatyeva yāvaccandradivākarau \|*  
*viṣṭhābhakṣyaṃ mūtrajalaṃ tatra tasya bhaveddhruvam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*trisandhyaṃ tāḍayettaṃ ca śūlena yamakiṅkaraḥ \|*  
*ulkāṃ dadāti mukhataḥ sūcyā kṛntati santatam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṭhāyāṃ ca kṛmirbhavet \|*  
*tataḥ kākaḥ pañcajanmasvathaivaṃ baka eva ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

*pañcajanmasu gṛdhraśca śṛgālaḥ saptajanmasu \|*  
*tato daridraḥ śūdraśca mahāvyādhistataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 67\|\|*

61-67. О Brahmana, the food of such a Brahmana who loads the bulls, is considered to be like the refuse and the water is like the urine. As such the sraddha and tarpana performed by such a Brahmana for the manes are not accepted by them. The gods also do not accept the flowers offered by him. A Branmana who willingly gives food to the driver of the bullock, is deprived of all the rites of the manes and the gods. He has to fall into the terrific hell and remains there till the moon and the sun last, consuming refuse and urine. The messengers of Yama torture him with tridents at the time of the three sandhyas. They thrust the burning wood into their mouths and prick their bodies continuously with needles. Thereafter, he is born as the insect of refuse for sixty thousand years. For five births he appears as a crow, skylark and a vulture. For seven births he has to be born as a jackal. Thereafter he is born as a pauper and a Shudra suffering from great ailment before he is purified.

## \|\| 51.68-69 \|\|

*bhāradvāja uvāca \|*  
*śūdrāṇāṃ śavadāhī yaḥ sa kṛtaghna iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*vayaḥpramāṇāṃ rājendra brahmahatyāṃ labheddhruvam \|*  
*tattulyayonibhramaṇāttattulyanarakācchuciḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*yo doṣo brāhmaṇānāṃ ca śūdrāṇāṃ śavadāhane \|*  
*tāvadeva bhaveddoṣaḥ śūdraśrāddhānnabhojane \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Bharadvaja said — О best of the kings, the one who burnt the bodies of the Siidras, is called an ungrateful person. He earns the sin of Brahmahatya according to the appropriate time. Thereafter, he wanders in similar forms and falls ultimately into the hell and is purified thereafter. The sin which a Brahmana earns by burning the dead bodies of the Siidras, the same sin is earned by him by taking food and drink with the Siidras.

## \|\| 51.70 \|\|

*vibhāṇḍaka uvāca \|*  
*pitṛśrāddhe ca śūdrāṇāṃ bhuṅkte yo brāhmaṇo'dhamaḥ \|*  
*surāpītī brahmaghātī pitṛdevārcanādbahiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Vibhandaka said — Such of the degraded Brahmana who takes food in the sraddha performed by the Shudra, is discarded for participating in noble deeds, like the drunkards sfnd the killers of the Brahmana.

## \|\| 51.71-74 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*yo doṣo brāhmaṇānāṃ ca śūdrastrīgamane nṛpa \|*  
*ahaṃ vakṣyāmi vedoktaṃ sāvadhānaṃ niśāmaya \|\| 71 \|\|*

*kṛtaghnānāṃ pradhānaśca yo vipro vṛṣalīpatiḥ \|*  
*kṛmidaṃṣṭre vasetso'pi yāvadindrāścaturdaśa \|\| 72 \|\|*

*kṛmibhakṣyo bhavedvipro vihvalo yamakiṅkaraiḥ \|*  
*pratimāṃ tāṃ taptalauhīmāśleṣayati nityaśaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tataśca puṃścalīyonau kṛmirbhavati niścitam \|*  
*evaṃ varṣasahasraṃ ca tataḥ śūdrastataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

71-74. Markandeya said — О king, the sin which a Brahmana earns by cohabiting with the wife of a Shudra, the same is going to be defined by me. You please listen to me attentively. The Brahmana who takes a Shudra woman as his wife, he is considered to be an ungrateful person and he has to remain in the Krmidamstra hell up to the period equivalent to the life of fourteen Indras. He is bitten by the insects there and the messengers of Yama torture him at the same time. He is made to embrace the daily burning image of the said woman. Thereafter he is born as an insect of the vagina of the wicked woman. He has to remain in that position for a thousand years before he is purified.

## \|\| 51.75-76 \|\|

*suyajña uvāca \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ ca kṛtaghnānāṃ vada karmaphalaṃ mune \|*  
*ślāghyo me brāhmaśāpaśca kasya sampadvinā''padam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*dhanyo'haṃ kṛtakṛtyo'haṃ saphalaṃ jīvanaṃ mama \|*  
*āgatāstu yato muktā madgehe munayaḥ surāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. Suyajna said — О sage, you kindly enlighten me on the results of the deeds of other ungrateful people. We find the curse of the Brahmana dominating us. One cannot earn riches without facing the trouble. We have been gratified; our life has been successful, because the best of the sages and the ascetics have assembled here.

## Chapter 52

## \|\| 52.1 \|\|

*śrīpārvatyuvāca \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ ca kṛtaghnānāṃ yadyatkarmaphalaṃ prabho \|*  
*teṣāṃ kimūcurmunayo vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Parvati said — О lord, what is the result of the deeds of the ungrateful people as prescribed in the Vedic and post-Vedic literature?

## \|\| 52.2 \|\|

*śrīmaheśvara uvāca \|*  
*praśnaṃ kurvati rājendre sarveṣu muniṣu priye \|*  
*tatra pravaktumārebhe ṛṣirnārāyaṇo mahān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Maheshvara said — О dear, a similar question was asked from the sages by the king Suyajna which was replied to the sage Narayana thus.

## \|\| 52.3-5 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*svadattāṃ paradattāṃ vā brahmavṛttiṃ harettu yaḥ \|*  
*sa kṛtaghna iti jñeyaḥ phalaṃ ca śṛṇu bhūmipa \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yāvanto reṇavaḥ siktā viprāṇāṃ netrabindubhiḥ \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasraṃ ca śūlapote sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 4 \|\|*

*taptāṅgāraṃ ca tadbhakṣyaṃ pānaṃ vai taptamūtrakam \|*  
*taptāṅgāre ca śayanaṃ tāḍito yamakiṅkaraiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Narayana said — О lord of the earth, the one who snatches away the livelihood given by himself as well as the one given by others to a Brahmana is considered to be an ungrateful person. You kindly listen to the result of the same. Whatever earth is soaked with the dropping of the tears of such a Brahmana on the ground, he falls into the Sitlapotd hell because of that sin and remains there up to the period equivalent to the number of the particles of dust multiplied by one thousand. He has to consume the burning flames and the boiling urine sleeping on the burning bed of flames. The messengers of Yama torture him beside that.

## \|\| 52.6 \|\|

*tadante ca mahāpāpī viṣṭhāyāṃ jāyate kṛmiḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi devamānena bhārate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thereafter, that great sinner is born on the earth as an insect of refuse for sixty thousand divine years.

## \|\| 52.7 \|\|

*tato bhavedbhūmihīnaḥ prajāhīnaśca mānavaḥ \|*  
*daridraḥ kṛpaṇo rogī śūdro nindyastataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He is then reborn as a Shudra deprived of his land, sons and becomes a pauper, miser and suffering from ailment.

## \|\| 52.8 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*hanti yaḥ parakīrtti ca svakīrttiṃ vā narādhamaḥ \|*  
*sa kṛtaghna iti khyātastatphalaṃ ca niśāmaya \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Narada said — The degraded person who shatters his own glory and also of others, is turned as an ungrateful person. I am going to tell you the result of the same, you please listen to me.

## \|\| 52.9 \|\|

*andhakūpe vasetso'pi yāvadindrāścaturdaśa \|*  
*kīṭairnakulagṛdhraiśca bhakṣitaḥ satataṃ nṛpa \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О king, such a person falls into the andhakupa hell and remains there as long as the life of fourteen Indras. His body is eaten up by insects and vultures daily.

## \|\| 52.10 \|\|

*taptakṣārodakaṃ pāpī nityaṃ pibati vai tataḥ \|*  
*saptajanmasvataḥ sarpaḥ kākaḥ pañcasvataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Such a sinner daily consumes boiling and saline water. Thereafter he is reborn as a snake seven times and a crow five times before he is purified.

## \|\| 52.11-12 \|\|

*devala uvāca \|*  
*brahmasvaṃ vā gurusvaṃ vā devasvaṃ vā'pi yo haret \|*  
*sa kṛtaghna iti jñeyo mahāpāpī ca bhārate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*avaṭode vasetso'pi yāvadindrāścaturdaśa \|*  
*tato bhavetsurāpī sa tataḥ śūdrastataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Devala said — Such of the person as misappropriates the riches of a Brahmana, a teacher and gods; such a sinner is termed as an ungrateful person in the land of Bharata. He falls into the Avatoda hell and remains there as long as the life of fourteen Indras. He is then reborn as a drunkard Stidra and is purified thereafter.

## \|\| 52.13-15 \|\|

*jaigīṣavya uvāca \|*  
*pitṛmātṛgurūṃścāpi bhaktihīno na pālayet \|*  
*vācā'pi tāḍayettāṃśca sa kṛtaghra iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*vācā ca tāḍayennityaṃ svāminaṃ kulaṭā ca yā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sā kṛtaghnīti vikhyātā bhārate pāpinī varā \|*  
*vahnikuṇḍaṃ mahāghoraṃ tau prayātassuniścitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tatra vahnau vasatyeva yāvaccandradivākarau \|*  
*tato bhavejjalaukāśca saptajanmasvataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Jaigisavya said — The one who getting deprived of the devotion does not serve well the parents and teacher and speak harsh words to them, is considered to be an ungrateful person; similarly a degraded woman who speaks harsh words to her husband and antagonises him, is also called an ungrateful woman. Both of these types fall into the hell with burning flames and have to suffer there till the sun and the moon last. Thereafter they are born as leeches seven times before they are purified.

## \|\| 52.16 \|\|

*vālmīkiruvāca \|*  
*yathā taruṣu vṛkṣatvaṃ sarvatra na jahāti ca \|*  
*tathā kṛtaghnatā rājansarvapāpeṣu varttate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Valmlki said — О king, as the element of becoming a tree is found in all the trees, so ungratefulness is also found in all the sins.

## \|\| 52.17 \|\|

*mithyāsākṣyaṃ yo dadāti kāmātkrodhāttathā bhayāt \|*  
*sabhāyāṃ pākṣikaṃ vakti sa kṛtaghna iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The one who indulges in passions, anger or gives false evidence due to some consideration, leaning towards someone, he is called an ungrateful person.

## \|\| 52.18 \|\|

*puṇyamātraṃ cāpi rājanyo hanti sa kṛtaghnakaḥ \|*  
*sarvatrāpi ca sarveṣāṃ puṇyahānau kṛtaghnatā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О king, the one who is responsible for the desecration of noble deeds, is called the ungrateful person, because when all the merits disappear, all will become ungrateful.

## \|\| 52.19 \|\|

*mithyāsākṣyaṃ pākṣikaṃ vā bhārate vakti yo nṛpa \|*  
*yāvadindrasahasraṃ ca sarpakuṇḍe vaseddhruvam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О king, in the land of Bharata whosoever gives any false evidence or supports an undesirable person, falls in the sarpa-kunda remaining there up to the age of a thousand Indras.

## \|\| 52.20 \|\|

*santataṃ veṣṭitaḥ sarpairbhīto vai bhakṣitastathā \|*  
*bhuṅkte ca sarvaviṇmūtraṃ yamadūtena tāḍitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The snakes always entangle his body and terrifying him they eat him up. Thus living among the snakes, he has to consume the refuse and the urine of the snakes, get tortured by the messengers of Yama.

## \|\| 52.21-22 \|\|

*kṛkalāso bhavettatra bhārate saptajanmasu \|*  
*saptajanmasu maṇḍūkaḥ pitṛbhiḥ saptabhiḥ saha \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tato bhavedvai vṛkṣaśca mahāraṇye tu śālmaliḥ \|*  
*tato bhavennaro mūkastataḥ śūdrastataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Thereafter he is born in the land of Bharata seven times as a chameleon and then as a frog; similarly and then is grown as a silk-cotton tree in the forest. He is then born as a dumb Shudra. Thereafter he is purified.

## \|\| 52.23 \|\|

*āstīka uvāca \|*  
*gurvaṅganānāṃ gamane mātṛgāmī bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*narāṇāṃ mātṛgamane prāyaścittaṃ na vidyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Astika said — The one who cohabits with teacher’s spouse earns the sin of cohabiting with his own mother and there is no remedy prescribed to relieve one of the sin of cohabiting with a mother.

## \|\| 52.24 \|\|

*bhārate ca nṛpaśreṣṭa yo doṣo mātṛgāminām \|*  
*brāhmaṇīgamane caiva śūdrāṇāṃ tāvadeva hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О best of the kings, the sin one earns by cohabiting with one's own mother, the same sin is earned by the Stidra cohabiting with a Brahmana woman.

## \|\| 52.25-26 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyāstāvadeva syāddoṣaḥ śūdreṇa maithune \|*  
*kanyānāṃ putrapatnīnāṃ śvaśrūṇāṃ gamane tathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sagarbhabhrātṛpatnīnā bhaginīnāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*doṣaṃ vakṣyāmi rājendra yadāha kamalodbhavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. О king, if a Brahmana woman cohabits with a Stidra, she earns the same type of sin. Now I am going to describe the sin one earns for cohabiting with one's own daughters, the daughter-in-law, brother's pregnant wives and sisters whatever has been told to me by Brahma himself.

## \|\| 52.27 \|\|

*yaḥ karoti mahāpāpī caitābhiḥ saha maithunam \|*  
*jīvanmṛto bhavetso'pi caṇḍālo'spṛśya eva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The great sinners who cohabits with such a woman is deemed to be a dead person while still alive and becomes untouchable like a Chandala.

## \|\| 52.28-29 \|\|

*nādhikāro bhavettasya sūryyamaṇḍaladarśane \|*  
*śālagrāmaṃ tajjalaṃ ca tulasyāśca dalaṃ jalam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sarvatīrthajalaṃ caiva viprapādodakaṃ tathā \|*  
*spraṣṭuṃ ca naiva śaknoti viṭtulyaḥ pātakī naraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Не forfeits the right to look at the sun besides Shalagrama and the sacred water, the leaves of Tulasi and its water of all the Tirthas. He is also deprived of the water with which the feet of the Brahmanas are washed because he always remains under the shadow of the great sin.

## \|\| 52.30-32 \|\|

*daivaṃ guruṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ca namaskartuṃ na cārhati \|*  
*viṣṭhādhikaṃ tadannaṃ ca jalaṃ mūtrādhikaṃ tathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*devatāḥ pitaro viprā naiva gṛhṇanti bhārate \|*  
*bhavettadaṅgavātena tīrthamaṅgāravāhanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*saptarātraṃ hyupavaseddaivasparśāttathā dvijaḥ \|*  
*bhārakrāntā ca pṛthivī tadbhāraṃ voḍhumakṣamā \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. He becomes incapable of bowing in reverence to the gods, teachers and the Brahmanas. Thereafter in the land of Bharata the food and water offered by such a person is considered to be like the refuse and the urine by the Brahmanas who do not accept the same; the sacred places start burning with the touch of such a person; a Brahmana, after coming in touch with such a person, should observe fast for seven nights. The earth feels disturbed by his weight and expresses her inability to carry his weight.

## \|\| 52.33-34 \|\|

*tatpāpātpatito deśaḥ kanyāvikrayiṇo yathā \|*  
*tatsparśācca tadālāpācchayanāśrayabhojanāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*nṛṇāṃ ca tatsamaṃ pāpaṃ bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kumbhīpāke vasetso'pi yāvadvai brahmaṇaḥ śatam \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Like the person who sells away his own daughter, he gets degraded and by talking to him or eating with him, the people earn sin. There is no doubt about it. Thereafter he is lodged in the Kumbhipaka hell up to the age of a hundred Brahmana.

## \|\| 52.35 \|\|

*divāniśaṃ bhramettatra cakrāvarttaṃ nirantaram \|*  
*dagdho vā'gniśikhābhiśca yamadūtaiśca tāḍitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He has to move about in the waves like the circular potter-wheel. He is burnt with the flames of fire and is tortured by the messengers of Yama.

## \|\| 52.36-37 \|\|

*evaṃ nityaṃ mahāpāpī bhuṅkte nirayayātanām \|*  
*viṣṭhāhāraśca sarvatra kumbhīpāke'tha pātitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*gate prākṛtike ghore mahati pralaye tathā \|*  
*punaḥ sṛṣṭeḥ samārambhe tadvidho vā bhavetpunaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Thus the great sinner has to suffer immensely body pains. After falling in the Kumbhipaka hell, he has only to consume the refuse. After the expire of the great dissolution and the re-creation of the universe, his position remains unchanged.

## \|\| 52.38-42 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi kṛmiśca pucalībhage \|*  
*ghaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṭhāyāṃ ca kṛmirbhavet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tato bhavati caṇḍālo bhāryāhīno napuṃsakaḥ \|*  
*sapajanmasu galatvuṣṭau cāṇḍālo' spṛśya eva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tattīrthe bhavedvṛkṣaḥ kṣudhitaḥ sapjanmasu \|*  
*sakṣajanyasu sarpaśca bhāryāhīno napuṃsakaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*saptajanmasu śuddhaśca galatkuṣṭhī napuṃsakaḥ \|*  
*tato bhavedbrāhmaṇaścāpyandhaḥ kuṣṭhī napuṃsakaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*labdhvaivaṃ sapta janmāni mahāpāpī bhavecchuciḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

38-42. For sixty thousand years he has to remain as a germ of the vagina of a wicked woman. Thereafter, he is reborn as a Chandala having no wives becoming impatient. For next seven births he is reborn as a human being suffering from leprosy in the family of Chandalas. Thereafter he reappears as a tree in a sacred place, as a hungry man for seven births, a snake for seven birth and a person deprived of manhood and wife. For seven times more he becomes a Shudra suffering from leprosy being implant, a blind and a Brahmana suffering from leprosy deprived of manhood. Thus he has to suffer variously in his next seven births before he is finely purified.

## \|\| 52.43-46 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvamasmābhirvo yathāgamam \|*  
*ebhistulyo bhaveddoṣo'pyatithīnāṃ parābhave \|\| 43 \|\|*

*praṇāmaṃ kuru viprendraṃ gṛhaṃ prāpaya niścitam \|*  
*saṃpūjya brāhmaṇaṃ yatnādgṛhītvā brāhmaṇāśiṣam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*vanaṃ gaccha mahārāja tapasyāṃ kuru satvaram \|*  
*brahmaśāpairvinirmuktaḥ punarevāgamiṣyasi \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ityuktvā munayaḥ sarve yayustūrṇaṃ svamandiram \|*  
*surāścāpi ca rājāno bandhuvargāśca pārvati \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-46. The sage said — Thus we have spoken everything according to the Shastras, the sin earned by one by disregarding a guest is similar to the same. Therefore you should bow in reverence to the Brahmana and taking him to your house adore him making great efforts, О lord, thereafter you go to the forest and perform tapas which will relieve you of the curse of the Brahmana and enable you to regain your kingdom. О Parvati, thus speaking, the sages went back to their respective abodes. Thereafter, the gods and the kings also left the place.

## Chapter 53

## \|\| 53.1-2 \|\|

*śrīpārvatyuvāca \|*  
*gateṣu munisaṃgheṣu śrutvā karmaphalaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*kiṃ cakāra nṛpaśreṣṭho brahmaśāpena vihvalaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*atithirbrāhmaṇo vā'pi kiṃ cakāra tadā prabho \|*  
*jagāma nṛpagehaṃ vā na vā tadvaktumarhasi \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Parvati said — After the departure of the sages, what did the king who was upset by the curse of the Brahmana do after hearing about the result of the deeds. О lord, thereafter what did the guest Brahmana do? Did he go to the place of the king or not? You kindly tell me.

## \|\| 53.3-4 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*gateṣu munisaṃgheṣu nindāgrasto narādhipaḥ \|*  
*preritaśca vasiṣṭhena dharmiṣṭhena purodhasā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*papāta daṇḍavadbhūmau pādayorbrāhmaṇasya ca \|*  
*tyaktvā manyuṃ dvijaśreṣṭho dadau tasmai śubhāśiṣam \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Maheshvara said — After the departure of the sages, the worried king at the instance of the royal priest Vasistha fell at the feet of the Brahmana. Thereafter the Brahmana also shedding all his anger blessed him.

## \|\| 53.5 \|\|

*sasmitaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā tyaktamanyuṃ kṛpāmayam \|*  
*uvāca nṛpatiśreṣṭhaḥ sāśrunetraḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Wearing a serene smile on his face and finding the Brahmana in a pleasant mood, the king spoke to him with folded hands with tears flowing from his eyes.

## \|\| 53.6-7 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kutra vaṃśe bhavāñjātaḥ kiṃ nāma bhavataḥ prabho \|*  
*kiṃnāmā vā'pi tadbrūhi kva vāsaḥ kathamāgataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*viprarūpī svayaṃ viṣṇurgūḍhaḥ kapaṭamānuṣaḥ \|*  
*sākṣātsa mūrtimānagniḥ prajvalanbrahmatejasā \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The king said — “O sage, in which race have you been born and what is your name? Where do you live and tell me what is your purpose of arrival here? You are indeed none else than lord Vishnu appearing in the form of a Brahmana who has deceitfully taken to the human form and whose eyes are having the lustre of a Brahmana and like the flames of fire.

## \|\| 53.8-9 \|\|

*ko vā guruste bhagavanniṣṭadevaśca bhārate \|*  
*tava veṣaḥ kathamayaṃ jñānapūrṇasya sāmpratam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gṛhāṇa rājyaṃ nikhilamaiśvaryyaṃ kośameva ca \|*  
*svabhṛtyaṃ kuru me putraṃ māṃ ca dāsīṃ striyaṃ mune \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Out of them the great knowledgeable Tvasta went to Puskara-ksetra and performed tapas there for a thousand divine years, observing great austerities. He performed great tapas for the lord for achieving Brahman. He was therefore blessed with a son.

## \|\| 53.10-11 \|\|

*saptasāgarasaṃyuktāṃ saptadvīpāṃ vasundharām \|*  
*aṣṭādaśopadvīpāḍhyāṃ saśailavanaśobhitām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*mayā bhṛtyena śādhi tvaṃ rājendro bhava bhārate \|*  
*ratnendrasārakhacite tiṣṭha siṃhāsane vare \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. О lord, who is your Guru and the supreme god of devotion in this land of Bharata. You are filled with immense knowledge but why do you appear in such a shabby form? О sage, you kindly accept this kingdom with all the treasures and let me serve you as your servant together with my wife and son.

## \|\| 53.12 \|\|

*nṛpasya vacanaṃ śrutvā jahāsa munipuṅgavaḥ \|*  
*uvāca paramaṃ tattvamajñātaṃ sarvadurlabham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You rule over the seven oceans, seven continents, eighteen islands filled with mountains and forests. You rule over the country. Becoming a great king on earth, you become the proud owner of the invaluable gems and occupy the well established lion-throne.

## \|\| 53.13 \|\|

*atithiruvāca \|*  
*marīcirbrahmaṇaḥ putrastatputraḥ kaśyapaḥ svayam \|*  
*kaśyapasya sutāḥ sarve prāptā devatvamīpsitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On hearing the words of the king, the sage smiled. Thereafter he started speaking on a spiritual theme which was unknown to anyone.

## \|\| 53.14-15 \|\|

*teṣu tvaṣṭā mahājñānī cakāra paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ ca puṣkare duṣkaraṃ tapaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*siṣeve brāhmaṇārthaṃ ca devadevaṃ hariṃ param \|*  
*nārāyaṇādvaraṃ prāpa vipraṃ tejasvinaṃ sutam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The guest said — Marlci was the son the Brahma and Kashyapa was the son of Marlci all the sons of Kashyapa achieved the desired god-hood.

## \|\| 53.16 \|\|

*tato babhūva tejasvī viśvarūpastapodhanaḥ \|*  
*purodhasaṃ cakārendro vākpatau taṃ krudhā gate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thereafter he got a glorious son of universal form who was appointed by Indra as his priest after Brihaspati left him in anger.

## \|\| 53.17 \|\|

*mātāmahebhyo daityebhyo dattavantaṃ ghṛtāhutim \|*  
*ciccheda taṃ śunāsīro brāhmaṇaṃ māturājñayā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. As soon as in the yajna of grand mother performed by Daityas, the offering of ghee was made by the Brahmana, Indra at the command of his mother killed that Brahmana.

## \|\| 53.18-24 \|\|

*viśvarūpasya tanayo virūpo matpitā nṛpa \|*  
*ahaṃ ca sutapā nāma virāgī kaśyapo dvijaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mahādevo mama gururvidyājñānamanupradaḥ \|*  
*abhīṣṭadevaḥ sarvātmā śrīkṛṣṇaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*taccintayāmi pādābjaṃ na me vāñchā 'sti sampadi \|*  
*sālokyasārṣṭisārūpyasāmīpyaṃ rādhikāpateḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tena dattaṃ na gṛhṇāmi vinā tatsevanaṃ śubham \|*  
*brahmatvamamaratvaṃ vā manye'haṃ jalabimbavat \|\| 21 \|\|*

*bhaktivyavahitaṃ mithyābhramameva tu naśvaram \|*  
*indratvaṃ vā manutvaṃ vā sauratvaṃ vā narādhipa \|\| 22 \|\|*

*na manye jalarekheti nṛpatvaṃ kena gaṇyate \|*  
*śrutvā suyajñayajñe te munīnāṃ gamanaṃ nṛpa \|\| 23 \|\|*

*lālasāṃ viṣṇubhaktiṃ te saṃprāpayitumāgataḥ \|*  
*kevalānugṛhītastvaṃ nahi śapto mayā'dhunā \|\| 24 \|\|*

18-24. О king the same son of Vishvarupa happened to be my father. My name is Sutapa. I am a recluse and belong to the race of Kashyapa, lord Shiva who is the embodiment of knowledge and learning and happens to be my teacher. Lord Krishna who happens to be the soul of everyone and beyond Prakriti happens to be my chief god whom I adore always with devotion at the lotus-like feet of the lord. Therefore I have no desire for riches and learnings. I am also not desirous of the salvation of Salokya, Sayujya, SarUpya and Samlpya which might deprive me of the adoration of lord Krishna, the husband of Radhika. I also consider the Brahmanhood, etemalship to be like the bubble of the water. All these things, О king, are of no consequence and are considered by me as an obstruction in the devotion. I am not desirous of the place of Indra, Manu, Surya which are all perishable like a line drawn over the water. Therefore, this kingship is of no consequence for me. О king Suyajna, learning about the arrival of the sages in your yajha I have arrived here to bestow the devotion of Krishna on you. In reality, I have not pronounced a curse on you, but on the other hand, you have been gratified with the same. The universe drags one to degradation. You had fallen and actually I have redeemed you.

## \|\| 53.25 \|\|

*samuddhṛtaśca patito ghore nimne bhavārṇave \|*  
*nahyammayāni tīrthāni na devā mṛcchilāmayāḥ \|\| 25\|\|*

25\. Because neither the sacred places are filled with water nor the gods reside in images made of earth or stone. But they get purified with a simple look. The devotees of lord Krishna purify everyone with a glance.

## \|\| 53.26-28 \|\|

*te punantyurukālena kṛṣṇabhaktāśca darśanāt \|*  
*rājannirgamyatāṃ gehāddehi rājyaṃ sutāya ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

*putre nyasya priyāṃ sādhvīṃ gaccha vatsa vanaṃ drutam \|*  
*brahmādistambaparyantaṃ sarvaṃ mithyaiva bhūmipa \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śrīkṛṣṇaṃ bhaja rādheśaṃ paramātmā namīśvaram \|*  
*dhyānasādhyaṃ durārādhyaṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivādibhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Therefore, О king, entrust the kingship to your son and proceed on to the forest for performing tapas. О son, О king, you entrust the care of your chaste wife and the kingdom to your son and proceed at once to the forest for tapas because everything right from a straw to Brahma is false. Therefore you recite the name of lord Krishna who happens to be the beloved of Radha who could be won over by immense devotion. He is beyond Prakriti and also beyond the reach of Brahma, Vis nua and Shiva.

## \|\| 53.29 \|\|

*āvirbhūtaistirobhūtaiḥ prākṛtaiḥ prakṛteḥ param \|*  
*brahmā sraṣṭā hariḥ pātā haraḥ saṃhārakārakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By his grace, Brahma creates the universe, Vishnu maintains it and Shiva destroys it and by his grace the Dikpalas got all the quarters and roam about in all the directions for safety.

## \|\| 53.30-32 \|\|

*dikpālāśca digīśāśca bhramantyevāsya māyayā \|*  
*yadājñayā vāti vāyuḥ sūryyo dinapatiḥ sadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*niśāpatiḥ śaśī śaśvatsasyasusnigdhatākaraḥ \|*  
*kālena mṛtyuḥ sarveṣāṃ sarvaviśveṣu vai bhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kāle varṣati śakraśca dahatyagniśca kālataḥ \|*  
*bhītavadviśvaśāstā ca prajāsaṃyamano yamaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. At his command the wind-blow, the sun remains the lord of the day, the moon becomes the lord of the night, he grows all the crops on earth with abundance and by his command the death reigns in the entire universe in all the times. By his command Indra drops the rain, the fire burns, the rulers controlling the people also get terrified with the god of death and rule the country faithfully. In time the universe comes to an end, in time the universe is created.

## \|\| 53.33-36 \|\|

*kālaḥ saṃharate kāle kāle sṛjati pāti ca \|*  
*svadeśe vai samudraśca svadeśe vai vasundharā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*svadeśe parvatāścaiva svāḥ pātālāḥ svadeśataḥ \|*  
*svarlokāḥ sapta rājendra saptadvīpā vasundharā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śailasāgarasaṃyuktāḥ pātālāḥ sapta caiva hi \|*  
*brahmāṇḍamebhirlokaiśca ḍimbākāraṃ jalaplutam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*santyeva pratividhyaṇḍe brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|*  
*surā narāśca nāgāśca gandharvā rākṣasādayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. In the entire country the seven oceans appear. In the same country the land is filled with mountains and also surrounded by the nether world. О king, the seven heavens, the land with seven continents filled with mountains, the seven Patala the nether-world, together with the seven oceans, stir the globe. Thus in every globe Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and other gods reside. The gods, humans, Narayana, Gandharvas, demons and others are all false.

## \|\| 53.37-39 \|\|

*āpātālādbrahmalokaparyyantaṃ ḍimbarūpakam \|*  
*idameva tu vidhyaṇḍamuttamaṃ kṛtrimaṃ nṛpa \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nābhipadme virāḍviṣṇoḥ kṣudrasya jalaśāyinaḥ \|*  
*sthitaṃ yathā padmabījaṃ karṇikāyāṃ ca paṅkaje \|\| 38 \|\|*

*evaṃ so'pi śayānassyājjalatalpe suviplute \|*  
*dhyāyatyeva mahāyogī prākṛtaḥ prakṛteḥ param \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. О king, the entire Prakriti and the globe are false creations, Brahma dwells on the lotus emerging from the navel of lord Vishnu residing in the ocean, on the lotus flower as the seed remains on the lotus. The vast bed on which Vishnu resides as a Mahayogi is filled with Prakriti and is also beyond Prakriti; people adore such a lord always.

## \|\| 53.40 \|\|

*kālabhītaśca kāleśaṃ kṛṣṇamātmānamīśvaram \|*  
*mahāviṣṇorlomakūpasādhāraḥ so'sti vistṛte \|*  
*kūpeṣu lomnāṃ pratyekamevaṃ viśvāni santi vai \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Lord Krishna who happens to be a great lord, the soul of all and the lord of the death gets terrified from him like the god of death. He remains in the hair pit of Maha-Vishnu in whose every hair-pit a globe is enshrined.

## \|\| 53.41 \|\|

*mahāviṣṇorgātralomnāṃ brahmāṇḍānāṃ ca bhūmipa \|*  
*saṃkhyāṃ karttuṃ na śaknoti kṛṣṇo'pyanyasya kā kathā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O king, even lord Krishna is unable to count the hair on the body of lord Vishnu and the number of globes enshrined therein what to speak of others?

## \|\| 53.42 \|\|

*mahāviṣṇuḥ prākṛtikaḥ so'pi ḍimbodbhavaḥ sadā \|*  
*bhavetkṛṣṇecchayā ḍimbaḥ prakṛtergarbhasambhavaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Lord Maha-Vishnu also is born of the same source by Prakriti. At the will of lord Krishna, a globe is born out of the womb of Prakriti.

## \|\| 53.43 \|\|

*sarvādhāro mahānviṣṇuḥ kālabhītaḥ sa śaṅkitaḥ \|*  
*kāleśaṃ dhyāyati svairaṃ kṛṣṇamātmānamīśvaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thus lord Maha-Vishnu who happens to be the base of all, feeling panicky from Kala becomes apprehensive and always adores at the feet of lord Vishnu regularly.

## \|\| 53.44-45 \|\|

*evaṃ ca sarvaviśvasthā brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|*  
*mahānvirāṭ kṣudravirāṭ sarve prākṛtikāḥ sadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sā sarvabījarūpā ca mūlaprakṛtirīścarī \|*  
*kāle līnā ca kāleśe kṛṣṇe taṃ dhyāyati sma sā \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Therefore Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva residing in all the globes together with Mahavirat and the small Virat emerge from the nature, the same Mula-Prakriti is free of the seed of everyone, which in due course of time merges into lord Krishna and always adores him.

## \|\| 53.46 \|\|

*evaṃ sarve kālabhītāḥ prakṛtiḥ prākṛtāstathā \|*  
*āvirbhūtāstirobhūtāḥ kālena paramātmani \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Therefore all the people are terrified by the death and because of their birth from Prakriti they at the same time appear from it and merge into the same.

## \|\| 53.47 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ mahājñānaṃ sudurlabham \|*  
*śivena guruṇā dattaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus I have imparted to you the great knowledge which I have received from lord Shiva; what more do you want to listen to from me?

## Chapter 54

## \|\| 54.1 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*kutrādhāro mahāviṣṇoḥ sarvādhārasya tasya ca \|*  
*kālabhītasya kati ca kālamāyā munīśvara \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The king said — О great sage, what is the base of lord Maha-Vishnu, who happens to be the base of all and what is the span of its age of Kalabhltal

## \|\| 54.2 \|\|

*kṣudrasya katicitkālaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prakṛtestathā \|*  
*manorindrasya candrasya sūryyasyāyustathaiva ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. What is the duration of the age of small Virat, Brahma, Prakriti, Manu, Indra, the sun and the moon?

## \|\| 54.3-4 \|\|

*anyeṣāṃ vai janānāṃ ca prākṛtānāṃ paraṃ vayaḥ \|*  
*vedoktaṃ suvicāryyaṃ ca vada vedavidāṃ vara \|\| 3 \|\|*

*viśvānāmūrdhvabhāge ca kassyādvā loka eva saḥ \|*  
*kathayasva mahābhāga sandehacchedanaṃ kuru \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. О king, possessed of his Prakriti, this is believed to be the base of Maha-Vishnu who happens to be the base of the universe.

## \|\| 54.5 \|\|

*muniruvāca \|*  
*goloko nṛpa viśvānāṃ vistṛtaśca nabhassamaḥ \|*  
*tathā nityaṃ ḍimbarūpaśśrīkṛṣṇecchāsamudbhavaḥ \|\| 5\|\|*

5\. О king, the same Maha-Vishnu appeared from the golden egg of the Prakriti. Mahavirat, who happens to be his base resides in the vast expanse of the ocean.

## \|\| 54.6 \|\|

*jalena paripūrṇaśca kṛṣṇasya mukhabindunā \|*  
*sṛṣṭyunmukhasyādisarge pariśrāntasya khelataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He is described as the sixteenth part of lord Krishna, the beloved of Radha; he has the dark complexion of Ditrva-gmss and has four arms and wears a serene smile on his face.

## \|\| 54.7 \|\|

*prakṛtyā saha yuktasya kalayā nijayā nṛpa \|*  
*tatrādhāro mahāviṣṇorviśvādhārasya vistṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О best of those well-versed in the Vedas, you kindly enlighten me about the duration of the age of others as well as what is prescribed in the Vedas. How many are the lokas, about the universe? or is it the same everywhere? О gracious one, you kindly remove my doubt.

## \|\| 54.8 \|\|

*prakṛtirgarbhasaṃryuktaḍimbodbhūtasya bhūmipa \|*  
*suvistṛte jalādhāre śayānaśca mahāvirāṭ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The sage said — О king of all the globes, it is Goloka only which is quite vast in area like the sky which was created with the desire of lord Krishna and always remains in the form of an egg.

## \|\| 54.9 \|\|

*rādheśvarasya kṛṣṇasya ṣoḍaśāṃśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*dūrvādalaśyāmarūpaḥ sasmitaśca caturbhujaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. At the time of creation of the universe, while turning his face a drop fell from the face of lord Krishna which was filled with water.

## \|\| 54.10 \|\|

*vanamālādharaḥ śrīmāñchobhitaḥ pītavāsasā \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ nabhasi tadviṣṇornityavaikuṇṭha eva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He wears a long garland of forest flowers, is graceful and is clad in yellow lower garment. The eternal Vaikuntha of Vishnu is lodged in the space.

## \|\| 54.11 \|\|

*ātmā''kāśasamo nityo vistṛtaścandrabimbavat \|*  
*īśvarecchāsamudbhūto nirlakṣyaśca nirāśrayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The one who is eternal like the soul and the sky; it is as vast as the reflection of the moon, has been created by the desire of the lord, has no base and is without a goal.

## \|\| 54.12 \|\|

*ākāśavatsuvistāro ratnaughaiśca vinirmitaḥ \|*  
*tatra nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmānvanamālī caturbhujaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Like the sky it is spread over a vast area and has been created by the use of gems. There lord Narayana wearing the long garland of forest flowers, having four heads resides there.

## \|\| 54.13 \|\|

*lakṣmīsarasvatīgaṅgātulasīpatirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sunandanandakumudapārṣadādibhirāvṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The lord has four spouses named Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Gatiga and Tulasi. He is surrounded by his attendants named Sunanda, Nanda and Kumuda.

## \|\| 54.15-16 \|\|

*caturbhujaśca vaikuṇṭhe goloke dvibhujaḥ svayam \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ vaikuṇṭhalokācca pañcāśatkoṭiyojanāta \|\| 15 \|\|*

*goloko varttulākāro variṣṭhassarvalokataḥ \|*  
*amūlyaratnakhacitairmandiraiśca vibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. О great lord, he is the lord of all the siddhas. He incarnates on earth for the benefit of his devotees. Lord Krishna has two arms and with his four anus he stays in Vaikuntha, but with his two arms he dwells in Goloka, which is lodged fifty crores yojanas beyond Vaikuntha. In the circular Goloka there are several buildings studded with gems.

## \|\| 54.17-18 \|\|

*ratnendrasārakhacitaiḥ stambhasopānacitritaiḥ \|*  
*maṇīndradarpaṇāsaktaiḥ kapāṭaiḥ kalaśojjvalaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*nānācitravicitraiśca śibiraiśca virājitaḥ \|*  
*koṭiyojanavistīrṇo dairghye śataguṇastathā \|*  
*virajāsaridākīrṇaiśśataśṛṃgaissuveṣṭitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The pillars and the steps of those buildings are studded with gems; their doors are decorated with mirrors of gems and beautiful vases. There are many camps of astonishing manner in Goloka. It is crores of yojanas in width and its length is a hundred times more than this.

## \|\| 54.19-26 \|\|

*saridardhapramāṇena dairghyeṇa ca tatena ca \|*  
*śailārddhaparimāṇena yukto vṛndāvanena ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tadarddhamānavilasadrāsamaṇḍalamaṇḍitaḥ \|*  
*saricchailavanādīnāṃ madhye goloka eva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yathā paṃkajamadhye ca karṇikā sumanoharā \|*  
*tatra gogopagopībhirgopīśo rāsamaṇḍale \|\| 21 \|\|*

*rāseśvaryyā rādhikayā saṃyuktaḥ santataṃ nṛpa \|*  
*dvibhujo muralīhastaḥ śiśurgopālarūpadhṛk \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vahniśuddhāṃśukādhāno ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*candanokṣitasarvāṃgo ratnamālāvirājitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsanasthaśca ratnacchatreṇa śobhitaḥ \|*  
*tathā sa priyagopālaiḥ sevitaḥ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bhūṣitābhiśca gopībhirmālācandanacarcitaḥ \|*  
*sasmitaḥ sakaṭākṣābhiḥ suveṣābhiśca vīkṣitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kathito lokavistāro yathāśakti yathāgamam \|*  
*yathāśrutaṃ śambhuvaktrātkālamānaṃ niśāmaya \|\| 26 \|\|*

19-26. The place is surrounded by a stream named Viraja, the mountains are half the size of the stream while Vrindavana is also half size of the same. The Rasamandala is located half the size of the same, in the Goloka. There are many rivers, mountains, forests in Goloka and it looks like the pericarp of a lotus. О king, in the Rasamandala, dwells Krishna the lord of gopis, Radha the goddess of the divine dance, together with the cows, cowherds and cowherdesses. He is always found with two arms holding a flute in his hand in the form of the cowherd. He is always clad in the garments purified by fire. He is adorned with gems studded ornaments and all his limbs are plastered with sandal-paste. He wears the garland of gems and is seated on the lion throne studded with gems. He has an umbrella over his head studded with gems and the dear cowherds swing the white fly whisks. The beautifully clad lady applies sandal-paste on his body and looks at him with side glances always, which makes the lord smile with pleasure. Thus I have narrated to you according to my own ability the details about Goloka as prescribed in the Vedas.

## \|\| 54.27-28 \|\|

*pātraṃ ṣaṭpalasaṃbhūtaṃ gabhīraṃ caturaṅgulam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*svarṇamāṣakṛtacchidraṃ daṇḍaiśca caturaṃgulaiḥ \|*  
*yāvajjalaplutaṃ pātraṃ tatkālaṃ daṇḍameva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Now I tell you something about the measure of time which I had heard about from lord Shiva. You please listen to it. Let there be a vase made of six palas of gold which should be four fingers deep. It should be pierced with four holes with the nails made of one Masa (gold-smith's weight). Then the vase should be kept on the water. When the water fills the vase emerging out of those holes, it is called a dandas.

## \|\| 54.29-30 \|\|

*daṇḍadvayaṃ muhūrtaṃ ca yāmastasya catuṣṭayam \|*  
*vāsaraścāṣṭabhiryāmaiḥ pakṣastairdaśapañcabhiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*māso dvābhyāṃ ca pakṣābhyāṃ varṣaṃ dvādaśamāsakaiḥ \|*  
*māsena vai narāṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ tadaharniśam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Even otherwise two dandas make a muhiirta and four muhUrtas make a Yama (Prahara), eight yamas make a day and night. Fifteen days make a fortnight and two fort-nights make a month. Twelve months make a year. A year of the humans equates with an Ahoratra of the manes.

## \|\| 54.31 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣe dinaṃ proktaṃ śukle rātriḥ prakīrttitā \|*  
*vatsareṇa narāṇāṃ ca devānāṃ ca divāniśam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Their day is known in the black fortnight and the night in the bright fortnight. One year of the human being is equal to the day and night of the gods.

## \|\| 54.32 \|\|

*ayanaṃ hyuttaramaho rātrirvai dakṣiṇāyanam \|*  
*yugakarmānurūpaṃ ca narādīnāṃ vayo nṛpa \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Uttarayana is the day for them and Daks inayana is the night for them. О king, the age of the human beings is reckoned with the yuga-kanna.

## \|\| 54.33 \|\|

*prakṛteḥ prākṛtānāṃ ca brahmādīnāṃ niśāmaya \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliśceti caturyugam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Now I explain to you the age of Prakriti and Brahma which you please listen to from me. Satyayuga, Treta, Dvapara and Kali are the four

## \|\| 54.34-35 \|\|

*divyairdvādaśasāhasraiḥ sāvadhānaṃ niśāmaya \|*  
*catvāri trīṇi ca dvayekaṃ sahasrāṇi kṛtādikam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ ca sandhyāsandhyāṃśau dve sahasre prakīrtite \|*  
*tricatvāriṃśakairlakṣaissaviṃśatisahasrakaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. The length of these extends to twelve thousand divine years. You listen to the same carefully; Satyayuga lasts for four thousand years. Treta lasts for three thousand years. Dvapara lasts for two thousand years and Kali for a thousand years. The sandhya of these and parts of sandhya also extend for two thousand years each. With the measure of the years for a human, the yugas equates with forty three lakhs and twenty thousand years.

## \|\| 54.36-40 \|\|

*caturyugaṃ parimitaṃ naramānakrameṇa ca \|*  
*lakṣaiśca saptadaśabhissāṣṭaviṃśasahasrakaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ yugaṃ nṛmānena saṃkhyāvidbhiḥ prakīrttitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*sahasraiṣṣaṇṇavatibhirlakṣairdvādaśabhissaha \|*  
*tretāyugaṃ parimitaṃ kālavidbhiḥ prakīrttitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*aṣṭalakṣaissaha mitaṃ catuṣṣaṣṭisahasrakam \|*  
*parimāṇaṃ dvāparasya saṃkhyāvidbhiritīritam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sadvātriṃśatsahasraiśca caturlakṣaiśca vatsaraiḥ \|*  
*nṛmānādvai kaliyugaṃ viduḥ kālavido bughāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

36-40. Now I am going to tell you separately about the measure of years for all the four yugas. the Krtayuga is of seventeen lakhs and twenty eight thousand years; this figure has been told by the mathematicians. Similarly Tretayuga has the duration of twelve lakhs and ninety six thousand years. The Dvapara has the duration of eight lakhs and sixty four thousand years and the Kaliyuga continues for four lakhs and thirty two thousand years. These figures have been given by those well-versed in the relevant field.

## \|\| 54.41-42 \|\|

*tatra sapta ca vārā vai tithayaḥ ṣoḍaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*divārātryaśca pakṣau dvau māso varṣaṃ ca nirmitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tathā bhramati taccakramevamevaṃ caturyugam \|*  
*tathā yugāni rājendra tathā manvantarāṇi ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. There are seven days, sixteen Tithis, day and night, two fortnights, a month and a year have been prescribed, О king in each one of the yugas the time moves on like the potter's wheels in the yugas and manvantaras.

## \|\| 54.43 \|\|

*manvantaraṃ tu divyānāṃ yuganamekasaptahih \|*  
*evaṃ kramādabhramantyeva manavaśca caṃturdaśa \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Seventy-one divine yugas make a manvantara; Similarly fourteen manvantaras go on rotating.

## \|\| 54.44 \|\|

*pañcaviṃśatisāhasraṃ ṣaṣṭyantaśatapañcakam \|*  
*naramānayugaṃ caiva paraṃ manvantaraṃ smṛtam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. From the measure of the human time a manvantara consists of twenty five thousand, five hundred and sixty yugas.

## \|\| 54.45 \|\|

*ākhyānaṃ ca manūnāṃ ca dharmiṣṭhānāṃ narādhipa \|*  
*yacchrutaṃ śivavaktreṇa tattvaṃ matto niśāmaya \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О king, I have heard the account from religious people as well as from the mouth of Shiva and the same has been narrated by me to you.

## \|\| 54.46 \|\|

*ādyo manurbrahmaputraḥ śatarūpā pativratā \|*  
*dharmiṣṭhānāṃ variṣṭhaśca gariṣṭho manuṣu prabhuḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The primeval Manu, the son of Brahma and the husband of SatarOpa, is the best among the religious people. He is quite glorious and quite competent among the Manus.

## \|\| 54.47 \|\|

*svāyambhuvaḥ śambhuśiṣyo viṣṇuvrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*jīvanmukto mahājñānī bhavataḥ prapitāmahaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Svayambhuva Manu happened to be the disciple of lord Shiva and had been perfonning vratas for Vishnu. He is free from birth, is a great intellectual and happens to be your grandfather.

## \|\| 54.48-50 \|\|

*rājasūyasahasraṃ ca cakre vai narmadātaṭe \|*  
*trilakṣamaśvamedhaṃ ca trilakṣaṃ naramedhakam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*gomedhaṃ ca caturlakṣaṃ vidhivanmahadadbhutam \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ trikoṭīśca bhojayāmāsa nityaśaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*pañcalakṣagavāṃ māṃsaiḥ supakvairghṛtasaṃskṛtaiḥ \|*  
*carvyaiṃścoṣyairlehyapeyairmiṣṭadravyaiḥ sudurlabhaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. He perfomied a thousand Rajashuya-yajnas, three lakhs of Asvamedha-yajnas, three lakhs of Narmedha-yajnas, four lakhs of Gomedha-yajhas at the bank of the rive Narmada in a proper manner. He managed them all quite astonishingly. Three crores of Brahmanas daily took their food there. The ghee derived from five lakhs of cows was used for the cooking of the meat besides cooking of other eatables, such as those required for chewing, sucking, pasting, drinking and besides various other sweet preparation.

## \|\| 54.51-56 \|\|

*amūlyaratnalakṣaṃ ca daśakoṭisuvarṇakam \|*  
*svarṇaśṛṅgayutaṃ divyaṃ gavāṃ lakṣaṃ supūjitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vahniśuddhāni vastrāṇi munīndrāṇāṃ ca lakṣakam \|*  
*bhūmiṃ ca sarvasasyāḍhyāṃ gajendrāṇāṃ ca lakṣakam \|\| 52\|\|*

*trilakṣamaśvaratnaṃ ca śātakuṃbhavibhūṣitam \|*  
*sahasraṃ ratharatnaṃ ca śibikālakṣameva ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

*trikoṭisvarṇapātrāṇi sānnaṃ sajalamīpsitam \|*  
*trikoṭisvarṇabhūṣāśca karpūrādisuvāsitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tāmbūlaṃ suvicitraṃ ca trikoṭisvarṇatalpakam \|*  
*ratnendrakhacitairmañcaiḥ racitairviśvakarmaṇā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vahniśuddhāṃśukaiścitrai rājitaṃ mālyajālakaiḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ dadau brāhmaṇebhyo viṣṇuprītyā śivājñayā \|\| 56 \|\|*

51-56. He distributed daily a lakh of invaluable gems, ten crores of gold coins, cows the horns of which were decorated with gold leaves, ten lakhs of horses decorated with gold, a thousand beautiful chariots, a lakh of palanquins, three crores of gold vases filled with cereals and water, three crores of gold ornaments, the betels with camphor and three crores of beds made of gold studded with gems Vishvakarma, the garment sanctified by fire and various astonishing types of garlands of gems to the Brahmanas at the advice of Shiva for the pleasure of lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 54.57 \|\|

*saṃprāpya śaṃkarājjñānaṃ kṛṣṇamaṃtraṃ sudurlabham \|*  
*saṃprāpya kṛṣṇadāsyaṃ ca golokaṃ vai jagāma saḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He then received divine knowledge from Shiva which is difficult to get besides the mantra of lord Vishnu. He then became the courtier of lord Krishna and went to Goloka.

## \|\| 54.58 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā muktaṃ svaputraṃ ca prahaṣṭo'bhūtprajāpatiḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva śaṃkaraṃ tuṣṭaḥ sasṛje'nyaṃ manuṃ vidhiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. At that point of time Brahma felt delighted on finding his son getting free and prayed to Shiva. Thereafter Brahma again created Manu.

## \|\| 54.59-60 \|\|

*yataḥ svayambhuputro'yamataḥ svāyambhuvo manuḥ \|*  
*svārociṣo manuścaiva dvitīyo vahninandanaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*rājā vadānyo dharmiṣṭhaḥ svāyambhuvasamo mahān \|*  
*priyavratasutāvanyau dvau manū dharmiṇāṃ varau \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. He was the son of Svayambhuva Manu. He was given the name of Svayambhuva Manu. Another Manu who was the son of Agni was known as Svarocisa-manu who was quite a charitable and religious king. He was as great as the Svayambhuva. Priyavrata who was quite noble had two sons who also became Manus.

## \|\| 54.61 \|\|

*tau tṛtīyau caturthau ca vaiṣṇavau tāpasottamau \|*  
*tau ca śaṅkaraśiṣyau ca kṛṣṇabhaktiparāyaṇau \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Both of them were Vaishnavas, great ascetics, disciples of Shiva and were also immensely devotee of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 54.62 \|\|

*dharmiṣṭhānāṃ variṣṭhaśca raivataḥ pañcamo manuḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhaśca cākṣuṣo jñeyo viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The fifth Manu was known as Raivata who was the best of the noble people, the sixth Manu was known as Caksusa Manu, who was always engrossed in the devotion of Vishnu.

## \|\| 54.63 \|\|

*śrāddhadevaḥ sūryasuto vaiṣṇavaḥ saptamo manuḥ \|*  
*sāvarṇiḥ sūryatanayo vaiṣṇavo manuraṣṭamaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Vaishnava Sraddhadeva who happened to be the son of Stirya was the seventh Manu. The eighth Manu was also a Vaishnava and the son of Stirya and known as Savarni.

## \|\| 54.64-65 \|\|

*navamo dakṣasāvarṇirviṣṇuvrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*daśamo brahmasāvarṇirbrahmajñānaviśāradaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tataśca dharmasāvarṇirmanurekādaśaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*dharmiṣṭhaśca variṣṭhaśca vaiṣṇavavratatatparaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. The ninth Manu was Dakshasavarni who was quite devoted to lord Vishnu; the tenth Manu was Brahmasavarni who was possessed of divine knowledge; the eleventh Manu was devoted to Dharma, was the best of the people and was always devoted to lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 54.66-69 \|\|

*jñānī ca rudrasāvarṇirmanuśca dvādaśaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*dharmātmā devasāvarṇirmanurevaṃ trayodaśaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*caturdaśo mahājñānī candrasāvarṇireva ca \|*  
*yāvadāyurmanūnāṃ syādindrāṇāṃ tāvadeva hi \|\| 67 \|\|*

*caturdaśendrāvacchinnaṃ brahmaṇo dinamucyate \|*  
*tāvatī brahmaṇo rātriḥ sā ca brāhmī niśā nṛpa \|\| 68 \|\|*

*kālarātriśca sā jñeyā vedeṣu parikīrttitā \|*  
*brahmaṇo vāsare rājankṣudrakalpaḥ prakīrttitaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

66-69. Rudrasavarni happened to be the twelfth Manu while Dharmasavarni was the thirteenth Manu. The great intellect Chandrasavarni was the fourteenth Manu. The age of Manu compares fully with that of the age of Indra. О king, a day of Brahma is equal to the life of fourteen Indras collectively and the night is of the same duration. It is called Kalaratri in the Vedas. О king, a day of Brahma is called the semi-kalpas.

## \|\| 54.70-72 \|\|

*saptakalpe ciraṃjīvī mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*brahmalokādadhaḥ sarve lokā dagdhāśca tatra vai \|\| 70 \|\|*

*utthitenaiva sahasā saṅkarṣaṇamukhāgninā \|*  
*candrārkabrahmaputrāśca brahmalokaṃ gatā dhruvam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*brahmarātrivyatīte tu punaśca sasṛje vidhiḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ brahmaniśāyāṃ ca kṣudraḥ pralaya ucyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-72. The great sage Markandeya had the life span of seven such kalpas; at the rising of serpent Ses a, he emits fire from his mouth which destroys all the lokas except the Brahmaloka. Thereafter the moon, the sun and the sons of Brahma proceed to Brahmaloka. Thus after the expiry of the night, Brahma again engages himself in creation, his Brahmaratri is called semi-dissolution.

## \|\| 54.73-75 \|\|

*devāśca manavaścaiva tatra dagdhā narādayaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ triṃśaddivārātrairbrahmaṇo māsa eva ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

*varṣaṃ dvādaśamāsaiśca brahmasambandhi caiva hi \|*  
*evaṃ pañcadaśābde tu gate ca brahmaṇo nṛpa \|\| 74 \|\|*

*dainaṃdinastu pralayo vedeṣu parikīrttitaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. All the sages, the gods and the humans are consumed by the fire; thus Brahma's thirty days and nights make a month and his twelve months makes a year. О king, thus after the expiry of fifteen years of Brahma, there comes the dissolution which is called Dainandina in the Vedas.

## \|\| 54.76-80 \|\|

*moharātriśca sā proktā vedavidbhiḥ purātanaiḥ \|*  
*tatra sarve praṇaṣṭāssyuścandrārkādidigīśvarāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*ādityā vasavo rudrā manavo mānavādayaḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo munayaścaiva gandharvā rākṣasādayaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*mārkaṇḍeyo lomaśaśca pecakaścirajīvinaḥ \|*  
*indradyumnaśca nṛpatiścākūpāraśca kacchapaḥ \|\| 78\|\|*

*nāḍījaṃgho bakaścaiva sarve naṣṭāśca tatra vai \|*  
*brahmalokādadhaḥ sarve lokā nāgālayāstathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*brahmalokaṃ yayuḥ sarve brahmaputrādayastathā \|*  
*gate dainaṃdine brahmā lokāṃśca sasṛje punaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

76-80. All the Vaishnavas merge into Narayana and all the Rudras who spread destruction, merge into Mahadeva who has over-powered the death because he happens to be the form of tamoguna. Thus with the fall of Brahma it becomes a second for Prakriti. О king, after the end of second Narayana, Vishnu, Shiva, Maha-Vishnu and other creations start with the desire of lord Krsna.

## \|\| 54.81-83 \|\|

*evaṃ śatābdaparyyantaṃ paramāyuḥ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇaśca nipāte syānmahākalpo bhavennṛpa \|\| 81 \|\|*

*prakīrtitā mahārātriḥ saiva ceha purātanaiḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇaśca nipāte ca brahmāṇḍaugho jalaplutaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*devamātā ca sāvitrī vedā dharmmādayastathā \|*  
*sarve praṇaṣṭā mṛtyuśca prakṛtiṃ ca śivaṃ vinā \|\| 83 \|\|*

81-83. The ancient seers of the Vedas call it as Moharatri in which the moon, the sun, Dikpalas, Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, the sages, humans, mendicants, ascetics, Gandharvas, Raksasas, those having long life, Markandeya, Lomasa, Pecaka, the king Indradyumna, Акйрйга, tortoise, Nadijangha and Baka are all destroyed. All the lokas below the Brahmaloka also are burnt out. The sons of Brahma revert to Brahmaloka. Thus after the expire of Dainandina, Brahma again creates the universe.

## \|\| 54.84-86 \|\|

*nārāyaṇe pralīnāśca viśvasthā vaiṣṇavāstathā \|*  
*kālāgnirudraḥ saṃharttā sarvarudragaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 84 \|\|*

*mṛtyuñjaye mahādeve pralīnaḥ sa tamo guṇaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇaśca nipātena nimeṣaḥ prakṛterbhavet \|\| 85 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇasya śambhośca mahāviṣṇośca niścitam \|*  
*nimeṣānte punaḥ sṛṣṭirbhavetkṛṣṇecchayā nṛpa \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-86. О king, thus Brahma enjoys the life of a hundred years and after the end of Brahma, there is dissolution everywhere. The ancients called it Maharatri. With the end of Brahma, the entire globe is submerged into water. At that point of time Aditi and mother of gods, Savitri, Vedas, Dhanna and death are also destroyed leaving Shiva and Prakriti behind.

## \|\| 54.87-89 \|\|

*kṛṣṇo nimeṣarahito nirguṇaḥ prakṛte paraḥ \|*  
*saguṇānāṃ nimeṣaśca kālasaṃkhyāvayomitaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*nirguṇasya ca nityasya cādyantarahitasya ca \|*  
*nimeṣāṇāṃ sahasreṇa prakṛterdaṇḍa ucyate \|\| 88\|\|*

*ṣaṣṭidaṇḍātmikāstasyā vāsaraśca prakīrttitaḥ \|*  
*triṃśadrātriṃ dinairmāso varṣaṃ dvādaśamāsakaiḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

87-89. Lord Krishna is beyond Prakriti. His incarnated form has a specified life but his eternal form is devoid of gunas, the beginning or end and is always ultimated. A thousand seconds of Prakriti make a dandas for him. Sixty dandas form a day; thirty days form a month and twelve months form a year.

## \|\| 54.90 \|\|

*evaṃ gate śatābde ca śrīkṛṣṇe prakṛterlayaḥ \|*  
*prakṛtyāṃ ca pralīnāyāṃ śrīkṛṣṇe prākṛto layaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Thus with the expiry of a hundred years of Prakriti, lord Krishna merges and after the merging of Prakriti into Krishna, he is known as Prakrtalaya.

## \|\| 54.91 \|\|

*sarvānsaṃhṛtya sā caikā mahāviṣṇoḥ prasūśca yā \|*  
*kṛṣṇavakṣasi līnā ca mūlaprakṛtirīśvarī \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Thus the mother of Maha-Vishnu who is the great goddess, is known as Mula-Prakriti. After absorbing everything into her body, she merges into the chest of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 54.92 \|\|

*santo vadanti tāṃ durgāṃ viṣṇumāyāṃ sanātanīm \|*  
*sarvaśaktisvarūpāṃ ca parāṃ nārāyaṇīṃ satīm \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The one who is called by the sages and the great ascetics as Durga, Vishnumaya, Sanatani, the form of all the strength and the best of all, is called the chaste Narayani.

## \|\| 54.93 \|\|

*buddhyadhiṣṭhātṛdevī ca śrīkṛṣṇasyaiva nirguṇām \|*  
*yanmāyāmohitāścaiva brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. She is the great goddess of intelligence of lord Krishna whose illusion influences Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva.

## \|\| 54.94 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavāstāṃ mahālakṣmīṃ parāṃ rādhāṃ vadanti te \|*  
*arddhāṅgāṃ ca mahālakṣmīḥ priyā nārāyaṇasya ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The gods call her as Maha-Lakshmi and best of Radha who happens to be the spouse of lord Narayana and is also known as Maha-Lakshmi.

## \|\| 54.95-96 \|\|

*prāṇādhiṣṭhātṛdevīṃ ca premṇā prāṇādhikāṃ varām \|*  
*sthirapremamayīṃ śaktīṃ nirguṇāṃ nirguṇasya ca \|\| 95 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇaśca śambhuśca saṃhṛtya svagaṇānbahūn \|*  
*śuddhasattvasvarūpī śrīkṛṣṇe līnaśca nirguṇe \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. She happens to be the life of the god who is dearer to him than his life even and in her invisible form she is the eternal energy. Narayana (Vishnu) and Shiva collecting all their virtues merge into the formless form of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 54.97 \|\|

*gopā gopyaśca gāvaśca savatsāśca narādhipa \|*  
*sarve līnāḥ prakṛtyāṃ ca prakṛtiḥ parameśvare \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. О king, the cowherds, cowherdesses, the cow with calves, merge into the nature known as Prakriti and Prakriti in turn merges into lord.

## \|\| 54.98 \|\|

*mahāviṣṇau vilīnāśca te sarve kṣudraviṣṇavaḥ \|*  
*mahāviṣṇuḥ prakṛtyāṃ ca sā caivaṃ paramātmani \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. All the small Vishnus merge into Maha-Vishnu and Maha-Vishnu in turn into Prakriti, whereas Prakriti merges into the great soul.

## \|\| 54.99-100 \|\|

*prakṛtiryoganidrā ca śrīkṛṣṇanayanadvaye \|*  
*adhiṣṭhānaṃ cakāraivaṃ māyayā ceśvarecchayā \|\| 99 \|\|*

*prakṛtervāsaro yāvanmitaḥ kālaḥ prakīrttitaḥ \|*  
*tāvadvṛndāvane nidrā kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. The will of the lord also known as Prakriti turns herself into yoganidra, overpowers lord Krishna's eyes, dwelling there. As long as the day of Prakriti lasts, lord Krishna sleeps in Vrindavana.

## \|\| 54.101-104 \|\|

*amūlya ratnatalpe ca vahniśuddhāṃśukārcite \|*  
*gandhacandanamālyaughavāyvādisurabhīkṛte \|\| 101 \|\|*

*punaḥ prajāgare tasya sarvasṛṣṭirbhavetpunaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sarve prākṛtāśca śrīkṛṣṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ vinā \|\| 102 \|\|*

*tadvandanaṃ tatsmaraṇaṃ tasya dhyānaṃ tadarcanam \|*  
*kīrttanaṃ tadguṇānāṃ ca mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yadyanmṛtyuñjayācchrutam \|*  
*yathāgamaṃ mahārāja kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi \|\| 104 \|\|*

101-104. He sleeps on the bed studded with invaluable, gems, who wears the garment purified by fire, is clad in beautiful garments. His body is adorned with the sandal-paste and fragrance together with the garland of flowers. When he wakes up the creation starts. Thus except lord Krishna, who is deprived of all the gunas, all are said to have been born out of Prakriti. Therefore he should be adored by reciting his name, dhyanam adoration and reciting of his virtues which relieves one of all the great sins.
